title: internal/ui refused tall fonts: layout, column stack and rail all closed panels
description:
Root cause found while bringing CI to green on the ci/github-actions branch (PR #107).

internal/ui/layout.go refused a child whose measured height exceeded the box (default branch), and layoutButtonContent clipped only on width. Any font with taller line metrics than the one the panels were tuned against closed the whole surface: launcher rows lost their foot padding, the info card's label overran its card, the settings rail pushed its last tab past the pane.

Fixed in PR #107: LayoutColumn clips text-shaped children to the room left in the box (only when the child starts inside it, so the launcher's floating chrome still overflows deliberately); a launcher label column takes the icon slot height; the settings rail became a bounded scroll, so its list scrolls instead of growing past the pane.

Two related items remain:
- settings scroll lookup by walk order (findScroll) is now key-based (settingsBodyKey) because the rail's new scroll shadowed the content scroll. Other panels may have the same latent assumption.
- internal/ui/column.go columnChildHeight honours an explicit column Height, which the launcher fix now relies on.

title: TestLockPreviewLoopAnimatesUnlessReducedMotion flaked once in CI
notes: Root cause found 2026-10-07 while merging the lock-lane PRs (this flaked again on PR #134 run 37619644179). Not timer/load nondeterminism: lockPreviewLoop calls renderer.New, one Step() (renderer wants a step before it draws), then Step+publish per frame. Step -> effect.Tick -> fx.Update(); fx.Render(). RainEffect.init seeds width/3 drops at Y = -rand.Intn(height), i.e. ALL above the screen; Update moves each down by Speed and only reseeds at the bottom; Render draws only drops with 0 <= Y < height. So a drop is invisible until several Updates accumulate, and with frames=3, every=time.Millisecond the first two published frames can both be blank. clearBuffers then yields an identical grid, so got[0] == got[1] even though the loop advanced correctly. Effect.Tick does bump gen unconditionally, but the test compares pixels, not gen. Fix direction: compare a frame the effect can actually draw (let it run until non-empty, or use an effect that is visible on frame one), or compare gen instead of pixels. PR #136 fixed an unrelated race; this is untouched.

title: sysc-lock: effect_policy treats Charging as on-battery, contradicting README ('while discharging') — auto never picks GPU on AC until battery Full
description:
Found during the 2026-10-07 sysc-1010 live-window audit.

Repro on archThink laptop (2026-10-07): BAT0 type=Battery status=Charging, AC online=1, capacity 53%, charge_control_end_threshold=100. resolveEffectPolicy(auto, powerSave=true, ..., systemBattery) -> onBatt=true -> GPU=false. So with shipping defaults on a plugged-in-but-charging laptop, effect_backend=auto runs the CPU path; GPU engages only when status becomes 'Full' (or on machines with no battery). README (sysc-lock) says: 'effect_gpu_power_save (default true) chooses the CPU outright while discharging' - the code at internal/lockd/effect_policy.go only skips status == 'Full', so Charging also counts as battery. The plan text (2026-10-06-gpu-effects.md Task 7) actually specified 'status != Full -> true', so code matches the plan and the README is the outlier - but the owner intent (2026-10-07) is 'GPU on AC', so the charging case should not demote. Laptops with a sub-100 charge threshold could stay on CPU indefinitely on AC.

Candidate a874c66 (staged, sha 40e7a564...) contains this behavior; any fix invalidates that candidate's evidence set and needs its own PR + fresh tests (no live window touched by this issue). Suggested fix: treat only 'Discharging'/'Not charging' as battery, or consult AC online; add a table test for Full/Charging/Discharging/absent.

title: sysc-lock GPU backend uses Mesa surfaceless platform -> llvmpipe software rendering (no hardware acceleration)
description: Live window 2026-10-07 (candidate a874c66, laptop archThink): with effect_backend=gpu the locker process maps libLLVM x5 and never opens /dev/dri (no renderD fd during or after lock cycles) => EGL context is Mesa llvmpipe (software rasterizer), not the Intel GPU. Hardware works: Intel UHD 620 (WhisperLake-U GT2) renders via iris under GBM (es2_info via Xwayland: Mesa Intel(R) UHD Graphics 620 (WHL GT2); eglinfo GBM platform same). Root cause: internal/lockd/effect_gpu.go prefers EGL_PLATFORM_SURFACELESS_MESA via eglGetPlatformDisplay(NULL) - Mesa surfaceless is a software platform. Fix direction: EGL_PLATFORM_GBM_KHR + gbm_create_device(/dev/dri/renderD128) or EGL_EXT_platform_device (eglQueryDevicesEXT); log GL_RENDERER/GL_VENDOR at init. Evidence: ~/lock-evidence/a874c66-live/renderer-probe.txt (+ maps). Gpu unit tests pass on llvmpipe - they cover the API path, not hardware.

notes: Found 2026-10-07 gating PR #132. Proof: with GOTMPDIR=/home/nomadx/.gotmp the single test fails in 0.003s with 'listen unix /home/nomadx/.gotmp/TestApplyEffectLeavesPriorWallpaperWhenTerminalSocketIsLiveForei1199394004/001/terminal-DP-1.sock: bind: invalid argument'; with the default /tmp it passes. title: Decide how the shell learns sysc-lock's clock style names: a public ClockStyles() from the locker, or the mirrored list with a drift test
description:
A decision, not work. The shell cannot import sysc-lock internal/art, so internal/lockconfig mirrors the names. Two options:

A) sysc-lock exports a plain ClockStyles() []string from its own module. The shell imports it, so a new style can never drift. Cost: a new exported surface in the locker, and a module dependency between the two repos.

B) The shell keeps the mirrored list plus a test that fails when the locker adds a style. Cost: the test has to know the locker, so it needs the locker source or a generated manifest on disk; still a one-line fix when the locker does add a style.

Today's mirror is verified correct: art.Names() = [kompaktblk phm_blocky_reverse phmvga phm_slanted plain], matching internal/lockconfig name for name and in order, and art.Lookup falls back to DefaultStyle (kompaktblk) the same way the shell does. So this is only about drift, not correctness.

Owner 2026-10-07: sysc-lock is being left alone for now. This decision is parked until then and blocks only the new-composition preview half of sysc-1013; the clock-style half already shipped in merged PR #130.

title: archPC session start: niri spawn-at-startup races sysc-shell.service; unit can hit start-limit-hit
description: Observed 2026-10-09 while executing the Home B1 handover (sysc-1052). niri config.kdl (~/.config/niri/config.kdl line 390) has spawn-at-startup "/home/nomadx/.local/bin/sysc-shell" AND the user unit sysc-shell.service runs the same binary. The single-instance lock (ipc ErrSingleInstance) means whichever starts second exits; on session start at 01:05 the niri-spawned shell won and the unit failed 5x in 30s -> failed (start-limit-hit), leaving the session on an unsupervised, deploy-invisible process. scripts/deploy then restarts the unit and requires is-active, so the stray had to be killed by hand before deploying 0fc6fc87. Fix options: drop spawn-at-startup on machines with the unit installed, or make the second instance exit 0 when the winner is the unit and let systemd own it. Owner decision on niri config.

description: Audit sysc-1110 at main 9bb8d528 reproduces a closed feedback loop: Registry.applyNotify always calls toastHost.recompute, which always sends presentation.renew; daemon answers every command, notifyclient publishes the reply, and ApplyNotify repeats. Ten synthetic lifetime replies generated ten new renewal commands and surface updates without content changes. Historical 08:07 profile: ApplyNotify 7.52 CPU s/10s, recompute 5.20, rebuild 3.90. Fix at notifications.go:180 and toasthost.go:900: refresh authoritative lifetimes without renewing/rebuilding unchanged content; preserve countdown redraw, timed lease renewal, hover/queue holds, DND and producer replies. Prove finite command count and idle invalidations, then comparable live quiet/burst CPU and responsiveness.

title: Keep brightness hardware reads outside the cache lock
description: Audit sysc-1110 confirmed a live ~390ms stall every 2.5s. diagnostics-20261011T083457 stacks show Brightness.poll reading DDC at brightness.go:326 while holding b.mu; Registry.Status holds Registry.mu while blocked in Brightness.Available. Control Centre home calls CachedState/CachedDisplays under Registry.mu and reaches the same lock. Offline probe confirms CachedState blocks behind a device read. Snapshot devices under lock, perform I/O off lock, then publish completed cache with device-generation and concurrent-write guards. Preserve 50ms DDC settle, read cache, debounce, hotplug and cooldown; use existing Audio.poll ownership pattern. One blocked-read check must show cached reads and UI work return promptly; repeat live latency and CPU.

title: Reduce full-display toast buffer retention and clearing
description: Audit sysc-1110 measured two fullscreen toast memfd generations: DP-1 3440x1440 and DP-3 2560x1440 at scale1, two ARGB buffers each, totaling 65.92MiB RSS even with no panel open. toastHost.spec anchors all four edges; render clears every pixel; shm.go retains two slots. A card-width strip of 380x1440 on both outputs would use 8.35MiB before margins/shadow, an estimated ~57MiB reduction. Design within toast owner: tight stack/strip surfaces or empty-state unmap, preserving output geometry, slide, pointer/swipe/reply coordinates, compositor blur, scale and queue presentation. Never reduce release-safe double buffering. Measure idle/visible RSS and pixel clearing with no input-region regression.

title: Bound renderer geometry caches by retained bytes
description: Audit sysc-1110: render/mask.go globals masks, rings and shadows retain every radius/size indefinitely. A synthetic 64-width sweep (3001..3064 x80) retains 14.81MiB in rounded masks alone after callers drop references. Tooltip resizing, output scales, changing labels and dynamic cards create new keys. Add simple bounded eviction at the owning cache, matching icons.Worker/weather sprite conventions; preserve immutable masks, concurrency, shape/ring/shadow correctness, and useful cache hits. Avoid constant-size-independent entry caps alone. Byte budget and repeated-size plateau check, plus paint comparison. Live 255MiB anonymous RSS is not yet attributable to this cache without heap profiling.

title: Decode notification images once per retained revision
description: Audit sysc-1110: toast recompute builds a card for height, again in cardRects, again for its retained tree, on each output. notificationCard calls protocolImage, so each pass repeats PNG decode and source.At per-pixel BGRA conversion under Registry.mu. A synthetic 256x256 PNG costs 1.66ms,834181B,65553 allocations per decode. Cache a validated immutable raster per notification/history revision and reuse layout measurements; bound lifetime/bytes and prune on replace/remove/reconnect. Use png.DecodeConfig to reject dimensions before allocation; retain bounds and alpha validation. Preserve images, reply fields, text layout, fallback icons, and scale. Measure burst CPU/allocations and input lock time.

title: Reduce duplicate font-map retention across shell surfaces
description: Audit sysc-1110: NewSystemFontMap warm creation costs6.93ms,10.39MB allocated,53076 allocations; retaining eight private maps adds36.70MiB heap after GC. Bars and auxiliary/panel hosts each create maps; many first-use paths run under Registry.mu. Investigate measured live retained font ownership before choosing bounded renderer reuse or shared immutable font data/catalog. font.Font is shareable; font.Face/fontscan.FontMap/shapers remain mutable and must keep ownership/synchronization. Preserve CJK, fallback, variable fonts, hot font changes, per-output fonts, and panel close cleanup. No shared mutable face shortcut. Compare first/repeat opens and live post-close heap/RSS.

title: Avoid copying clipboard history into every bar update
description: Audit sysc-1110: Registry.viewLocked clones the complete clipboard snapshot and all MIME slices, and metrics.Histories copies all leased rings, for each output on clock/media/notify/plugin updates. Bar clipboard widget reads availability, entry count and persistence only. Synthetic1000-entry clone costs58.5us,179456B,1001 allocations per call; earlier burst profile attributes0.84CPU s/10s to cloneClipboardSnapshot. Build the minimal bar projection or safely reuse immutable published snapshots; keep full metadata for clipboard panel, preserve caller ownership and the existing mutation-isolation checks. Histories need equivalent ownership proof before sharing. Verify unrelated update allocations no longer scale with clipboard length.

Avoid production per-frame logging or a metrics service. Preserve 0600 files, credentials/privacy and bounded diagnostic request handling; no forced GC on the live owner by default. title: Keep AI Usage refreshes off the plugin input loop
description: The live AI Usage executable is d04ef299+dirty from aiusage-provider-audit. Round at loop.go:219 holds Loop.mu while calling each collector serially; Snapshot uses the same mutex. A synthetic collector held Snapshot for 100ms in cf7cc799 and the inspected current worktree snapshot. HTTP collectors allow 20s each, so stalls can add across providers. Extend the existing plugin loop with one bounded serial refresh worker and completion channel, retain last-good report and publish busy before return. Snapshot/Reconfigure must avoid fetch and disk I/O under cache mutex; use generations to discard old-config completions. Preserve provider floors, backoff, credentials and notification deduplication. This is separate from provider correctness sysc-1107 and the resolved shell text-input issue sysc-1104. Prove ViewOpen, close, input and shutdown proceed while a collector is held; no overlapping fetch rounds.

title: Move ProtonVPN polling off the plugin input loop

Reuse existing async completion channel with one coalesced polling worker; publish immutable status on owner, guard generations against stale status overwriting connect/disconnect. Apply same ownership to info/config/settings/signout calls. Keep click feedback, close and shutdown responsive with CLI held; bound cancellation and do not retry effectful commands.

title: Bound tray D-Bus calls so one item cannot stall later commands
description: Audited sysc-tray v0.1.1 source; live binary has no VCS stamp, so exact source identity remains unknown. presenter/connection.go:182 reads and dispatches serially. menu/proxy.go:211 GetLayout, :247 Event and :258 AboutToShow and item/proxy.go:189 GetAll/:232 Activate use godbus Call with background context. Synthetic private-bus peer held AboutToShow for 250ms until released. A hung item blocks subsequent command dispatch from the sole presenter, including unrelated items, and proxy refresh cancellation cannot interrupt the call. Use installed godbus CallWithContext, owner-scoped cancellation and a short menu-refresh budget. Preserve generation/revision checks and never retry activation. Prove stalled peer cancellation and a following independent command; coordinate native menu qualification sysc-959/sysc-1120.

title: Avoid copying all clipboard payloads on every durable save
description: Deployed clipboard 8e1f2c72: daemon/service.go:389 commit calls store.Save(history.Items()) on reducer. History.Items clones all payloads; Store.Save :83 calls item.Payload and NewItem (which hashes then clones payload again) before skipping already-present encrypted payload files. Synthetic unchanged 16MiB history warm save: 13.72ms, 50,378,792 B/op and 357 allocations. This creates about three full-history copies per metadata change and rehashes old data. Current live encrypted payloads total only 168,366 bytes across 100 entries; idle RSS is 9.62MiB, so this is a burst/large-image risk. Extend immutable item ownership and changed-entry persistence at the responsible history/store boundary, then move durable work to one ordered bounded worker. Preserve encrypted files, symlink validation, atomic manifest, fsync ordering, removals and accurate durable/volatile ACK semantics; do not weaken trust-boundary validation or drop data. Benchmark warm pin/move saves vs history bytes; reuse sysc-699 for owner-selected caps.

title: Keep clipboard thumbnails and restore waits outside metadata reducer
description: Deployed clipboard 8e1f2c72: daemon/service.go:337 execute handles restore synchronously and :370 thumbnail decode/resize/PNG encode synchronously on the same reducer used by snapshot, capture and pin/delete. 4096x2048 synthetic PNG thumbnail: 41.90ms, 35,238,813 B/op, 36,919 allocations. Blocking restore hook made CurrentSnapshot miss a 100ms deadline; Wayland Restore waits without a caller context. Run image work in bounded workers with item identity/revision validation, small byte-bounded thumbnail cache keyed by ID+size, and context-bounded restore completion outside reducer. Retain Wayland proxy ownership, ordering, privacy and stale-offer guards. Prove metadata/capture remains responsive under held image/restore work, cancellation and cache eviction.

title: Keep plugin host-call replies flowing during input bursts
description: Active calendar, notes, timer, KDE Connect, mini-docker, GitHub Notifications and Games call host synchronously from their event/completion loops. internal/hostcall correctly describes the existing hazard: sole c.Recv goroutine cannot decode HostReply when its bounded incoming queue is full; loop waits for Call and cannot drain that queue. Current 5s deadlines limit the wait but leave multi-second input latency; GitHub saveCache and notify also call for 5s on completion. Reuse existing Faith/Herdr/Cat worker/completion patterns at affected call sites; keep receive progressing and serialize protocol writes. Keep queued work bounded and coalesce state writes without losing the latest value. A smallest fixture must fill incoming while a host reply arrives and show input/close and reply complete promptly. No general new plugin framework needed.

title: Measure existing static wallpaper backends against gSlapper memory
description: Live two static-image gSlapper children together use 295.91MiB summed RSS but only 125.34MiB PSS, 54.36MiB anonymous and 0.233% of one core. Inputs have the same digest and size; shared driver/library mappings dominate RSS. Existing wallpaper code owns awww/swaybg static fallback, but selects gSlapper first. Compare equivalent image/per-output updates using those installed backends in an authorized live window, including transition and independent output lifecycles. Prefer existing backend routing if behavior and measured memory/latency justify it. Do not collapse gSlapper into one all-output worker: gslapper.go:66 documents that a later per-output assignment blanks other outputs. No new renderer/dependency or predicted saving claimed.

title: Bound decorative backdrop capture before lock acquisition
description: Audited deployed sysc-lock 408570ac: cmd/sysc-lock/main.go:298 CaptureBlur precedes :300 Client.Lock. capture.go:120 pumpUntil bounds Roundtrip count to32 but has no elapsed-time budget. Connect resets read deadline before capture; pinned sysc-wayland Roundtrip dispatches until sync callback. Run acquisition deadline begins after this capture phase. A nonreplying compositor can hold the decorative phase before sealing; source evidence only, no live lock attempted. Put decorative capture within a bounded acquisition budget using existing owner/poll/deadline capabilities, fall back to opaque promptly and preserve protocol stream validity and security ordering. Prove withheld sync/capture response does not hold the seal request indefinitely in an isolated mocked/nested compositor. Coordinate sysc-974; do not weaken PAM, capture-before-seal privacy, fail-closed behavior or the sleep inhibitor.

title: Group the sysmon widgets in one holder pill
description:
Live review 2026-08-31: cpu and memory each getting their own capsule reads as loose numbers. Owner wants them grouped; battery stays separate in its own pill.

The references disagree, so this is an owner decision, not a correction. DMS gives every status widget its own capsule. Noctalia runs the sysmon cluster as one continuous group with no inner pills.

Decision: one holder pill containing flat icon and value runs. Do not nest pills inside pills. The workspace row is already a pill row inside a capsule and reads as one indistinct blob in the live capture, our capsule contrast is 1.08 to 1 so two nested surfaces cannot be told apart, and Noctalia, the grouped reference, is flat inside.

Blocker: grouping is not expressible. Bar.Left, Center and Right are flat Item slices. Add an explicit group item carrying nested items, built as one capsule wrapping a KindRow. The layout machinery already exists from the parity tranche: capsuled wraps anything, measureNode sizes a row inside a capsule, and placeSection arranges capsule contents.

Sequence after sysc-53: a group of bare numbers is barely better than two pills of bare numbers, so the icons are what make a grouped cluster legible.

title: setSessionProfile runs a command under Registry.mu
description:
internal/shell/popout_session.go:243 calls r.runArgv(powerProfileSetArgv(name)) straight from an action handler, which holds Registry.mu. That is command I/O under the lock, which the project constraint forbids: no command or filesystem work may run while Registry.mu or the Wayland owner is blocked.

The same file already has the correct shape two functions up: scheduleLoadProfiles copies the exec hooks, runs off the owner without the lock, re-takes it, checks the panel host is still current, then applies. The set path should schedule the same way.

Found while designing the control centre (sysc-158). The control centre routes every command through its own scheduleControl seam rather than copying this, so it is not blocked on the fix.

The same file already has the correct shape two functions up: scheduleLoadProfiles copies the exec hooks, runs off the owner without the lock, re-takes it, checks the panel host is still current, then applies. The set path should schedule the same way.

Found while designing the control centre (sysc-158). The control centre routes every command through its own scheduleControl seam rather than copying this, so it is not blocked on the fix.

title: [pleamar] Springs: a velocity-preserving integrator inside the existing per-surface animator
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-core-rt-01).

Recommendation: Add spring physics as a second motion shape inside the animator every surface already owns, instead of the fixed duration table: a value in flight keeps position and velocity, a retarget writes only the new target and leaves the velocity alone, and the integrator advances in fixed sub-steps so a late or skipped tick does not change the motion. The reopening argument is sysc's own: sysc-590's owner-approved design deferred springs "with a named trigger (notification stack reflow)" (docs/plans/README.md:584) and the sysc-592 notification work then built the toast collapse slide that is that trigger point (docs/plans/README.md:587) - this rec is the engine the trigger was waiting for, and it is the only direct-in-go item in this cluster. No new UI primitive: the first consumers are channels that already exist (hover, selection, panel enter/exit, meter glide) plus the notification stack's collapse; plugin-facing stiffness stays out of the protocol until a second real consumer needs it.

Approach: internal/ui/transition.go is where pure motion math already lives (EaseOutCubic/EaseOutQuart/LerpRect, with clocks deliberately kept in the shell: transition.go:5-8), so add a clock-free Spring{stiffness,damping} beside it whose At(dt) steps semi-implicit Euler in sub-steps of at most 2 ms with an at-rest early-out, mirroring pleamar scene.rs:2073-2099/2523-2549. internal/shell/animation.go then gains a spring variant of animValue (animation.go:92-130) storing x, v, target, spring and last-advance, integrated forward on at()/Value() (:520-526); Target() (:368-382) stops rebasing `from` and restarting the envelope - it writes target and spring and leaves x and v, which is the whole pleamar trick (render.rs:2957-2963). Everything else stays: the channel catalogue (:56-82), the 8 ms tick and frame cap (:41, :612-617), animateSurface/animateSurfaceResting (:631-695), nudge/wake (:190-195), Settled/SettledExceptEffects (:531-554) which must treat a resting spring as settled so an idle shell still schedules nothing. duration()/easeFor() (:199-253) stay for linear channels (ripple, sprite, sweep, gradient, effect) and for reduced motion, where springs snap exactly like hover does today. Route only animHover/animSelect/animVisible/animProgress through springs first; every surface already constructs its own animator (bar.go:155, panelhost.go:1307, osd.go:112, toasthost.go:147), so this lands per surface without a cross-cutting refactor. Stiffness presets ride theme MotionSet (render/style.go:235-240, assembled at shell/theme.go:201) so theme speed and reduced motion keep working, and no config vocabulary is added yet.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: Feel is subjective and overshoot can escape tight clip rects (hover scale, panel slide): the six house presets are starting points tuned in review, and ripple/sprite/sweep must stay on their linear path. Reduced motion has to resolve springs to the existing snap or accessibility parity breaks. The deferral's trigger is a register note, not a bd item (no bd row mentions springs), so confirm the notification-stack work is actually scheduled before spending scope beyond the four existing channels.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-core-01)
Audit: pass — Stack/Niri/CGO clean; rung existing matches the shipped animator + transition machinery (transition.go:24-46, animation.go:368/520/570 verified in sysc-main); no new primitive - consumers are existing channels; register :584/:587 verified as the deferral trigger; no pins; no estimates. | Springs unowned: sysc-590 defers them with a named trigger and sysc-592 built that trigger (register :584/:587); no bd row. O2 boundary: keep both with REC-uint-01 - that rec ships on the existing eased channel and must not require this spring engine.

title: [pleamar] Reload-on-save: an inotify watcher feeding the existing reload channel
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-core-lang-06).

Recommendation: Make a saved config.json take effect without a signal or a restart: watch the config path and feed the same reload channel SIGHUP and the settings writer already use, so validation, keep-last-good and apply stay the one code path that exists. The watcher stays deliberately dumb - a debounced directory event, no parsing, no polling - because the owner still re-reads and validates the file itself. This turns the documented hand-edit workflow (docs/metrics-widgets.md:21) into save-and-see and removes the manual reload step for agent edits of the bd sysc-676 class.

Approach: Add internal/config/watch.go with an inotify loop modelled on the existing one in internal/services/brightness.go:788-817 (unix.InotifyInit1 + InotifyAddWatch over golang.org/x/sys/unix, already a pinned module at go.mod:11): watch the config directory for IN_CLOSE_WRITE|IN_MOVED_TO so config.Write's temp+rename swap (write.go:8-23) is caught, debounce a burst, and invoke a supplied notify func. Wire it in cmd/sysc-shell/main.go next to the SIGHUP funnel (main.go:369-383) into the same size-1 reloads channel passed as Callbacks.Reloads/ConfigPath (main.go:431-432), so owner.reloadConfig (internal/platform/wayland/client.go:1129-1148) re-reads, validates and applies the candidate exactly as it does today. Non-blocking sends already guard that channel (popout_settings.go:1798-1803); a duplicate reload caused by the settings UI's own write is coalesced by the debounce rather than special-cased. Share one debounced inotify helper with REC-int-07: its host-side watcher registry is that helper's natural home (this config watcher and the component-facing service are its consumers; sysc-754's plugin-directory watcher joins them). Until that lands, this rec keeps a small local loop.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: Editors save in different shapes (rename-over, truncate-write, symlinked path - write.go already replaces a symlink at the path), so watch the directory and debounce rather than the file alone; a network-mounted config dir may deliver no inotify events, so the watcher must fail silent and leave SIGHUP/restart as the fallback. Keep the debounce long enough to cover a save burst and short enough that the settings UI still feels immediate, and never let the watcher parse or validate on its own goroutine.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-core-02)
Audit: pass — rung existing: inotify loop precedent verified (brightness.go:788-817) and x/sys already pinned at go.mod:11; no new dependency or pin; no estimates. | Config-file save-reload unowned; adjacent sysc-754 (plugin dirs only), sysc-735 (reload change-sets), sysc-739/778 (watched state/theme files) cover other files/mechanisms. O5 boundary: share one debounced inotify helper with REC-int-07 instead of two.

title: [pleamar] Positional config diagnostics: path:line:col with excerpt and caret
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-core-lang-02).

Recommendation: Give config errors a position, not only a dotted path: render `config: <path>:<line>:<col>: <message>`, then the offending source line and a caret under the column, and fall back to today's path-only text whenever no position is known. The position data is what sysc-1410 (open) is already adding - file and position per dotted path, for the settings writer - so this rec consumes that index instead of building a second one; syntax-level failures can use encoding/json's SyntaxError.Offset, which Parse discards today (load.go:318-330). The gain lands on the hand-edit workflow (docs/metrics-widgets.md:21) and on agent edits of the bd sysc-676 class, where hunting a dotted path in a sparse one-line document is the whole cost.

Approach: internal/config/config.go: make pathErr (:800-802) return a small typed error carrying path and message (`pathError`), so all ~114 call sites keep compiling unchanged, and add one formatter that renders either the positional or the path-only form. internal/config/load.go: Parse (:314-330) keeps the bytes it decoded and wraps decoder failures with SyntaxError.Offset mapped to line:col; validation errors resolve their dotted path to a position through sysc-1410's origin index and render the excerpt shape the gap records from pleamar (4-wide margin, source line, caret under the column - src/language/mod.rs:40-49). Every consumer of the error string - reloadConfig's stderr line (internal/platform/wayland/client.go:1137), the settings label (popout_settings.go:1775-1781) and the status field from REC-core-04 - gets positions for free from that one formatter.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: sysc-1410 (origin index for validation positions; the SyntaxError.Offset half is independent).
Risk: sysc-1410 also carries per-output layer semantics, so it may land late or partially: the formatter must degrade to the current text, never to a guessed line. Byte offsets describe the file as read, so keep the bytes with the error rather than re-reading (a file rewritten in between would render a wrong caret, which is worse than none). Pin the format with tests over multi-line, CRLF and multi-value documents.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-core-03)
Audit: pass — rung existing; pathErr config.go:800 and Parse load.go:318-330 verified; owner-gated upstream sysc-1410 carried as prerequisite; no deps; no estimates. | sysc-1410 (partial) supplies the origin index only; error formatting/excerpt/caret unowned. Prereq sysc-1410 resolves (bd open).

title: [pleamar] A refused reload becomes visible: registry state, message OSD, status field
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-core-lang-07).

Recommendation: Make a rejected reload visible where the user is, without inventing a surface type: carry the rejection out of the owner loop through a new optional callback, keep the message on the registry until a good apply clears it, raise a short message OSD when it happens, and expose the full text through the existing IPC status payload so the settings panel, agents and `sysc-shell ipc status` read the reason without the journal. The OSD is the shell's existing always-available channel (the same path the audio, brightness and DND kinds use) and the settings panel already has an error label, so the only addition is one OSD kind and one stored string.

Approach: internal/platform/wayland/client.go: add ReloadRejected func(error) to Callbacks (:117-162) and call it from owner.reloadConfig on both reject paths (:1129-1143), keeping the existing stderr line; cmd/sysc-shell/main.go:418-432 wires it to a registry method that stores lastConfigError/configErrorAt beside r.cfg under r.mu (registry.go:1127) and adds both to Status() (:1139-1148), which the existing ipc subcommand path already exposes (main.go:443-455). In-band, raise it the way registry.go:516/:1194 raise OSDs (r.OSD().Show(OSDView{...})) with one new Kind in osdview.go:10-17 and its icon/label cases (:46-108); the OSD body is 220x64 (osd.go:13-18, tree and layout at :214-230), so the view carries a short summary while the complete message stays in the stored error. When a settings panel is open the same string can flow into its existing errLabel (popout_settings.go:1775-1781); a successful reload clears the stored error. The callback does no work on the owner beyond handing over the error.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: Length versus OSD geometry: a full config error would clip, so keep the on-screen line short and the detail in the status field - do not grow the OSD into a log viewer. With REC-core-02 in place the signal repeats on every save until the config is fixed (intended, but it must not fire when the file did not change). Clearing must be tied to a successful apply, not to the OSD hiding, or a transient hide reads as 'fixed'.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-core-04)
Audit: pass — rung existing (Callbacks client.go:117-162, reloadConfig :1131, Status registry.go:1116/1140 verified); one OSD kind with the reload-rejection event as the named consumer; no deps; no estimates. | Adjacent sysc-765 broadens OSD kinds through the same OSDView.Kind vocabulary, but no kind or issue covers a refused-reload message; the registry/status/OSD wiring is new.

title: [pleamar] Nearest-match suggestions for unknown keys and item ids
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-core-lang-03).

Recommendation: Add 'did you mean' suggestions to the two hand-edit failures the loader currently states without candidates: an unknown config key (the strict decoder names it, load.go:318-330, but nothing else) and an unknown bar item id (resolveItem writes `%q is not a known item`, load.go:1143-1145). Enum-valued options already print their valid lists (load.go:961/989/995), so they need nothing. The suggestion only changes the message; it never changes which error is raised or how validation proceeds.

Approach: internal/config: one unexported closest-match helper (edit distance over short ASCII keys, accept within a bounded threshold - the shape pleamar uses is 1+len/4, src/language/mod.rs:396-413), called from two places. For keys, build the candidate table from the wire struct graph's JSON tags (wireConfig and its section structs, load.go:217-273) and keep it honest with a test; for the path too, a generic walk of the decoded document (map[string]json.RawMessage) resolves the nested key to its dotted path before the strict typed decode stays the source of truth. For item ids, resolveItem already has the vocabulary in hand via knownItems/KnownItemIDs (config.go:804-815). Stdlib only, no new dependency, no new UI.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: S · impact: L.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: A suggestion can mislead: only offer it when a single candidate is inside the threshold, and never downgrade or replace the error. The key table is derived from struct tags, so a hand-kept duplicate list would rot - generate it from the structs in one place and fail a test when a tag is added without coverage.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-core-05)
Audit: pass — message-only change inside internal/config; stdlib only; no primitive, no pin, no estimates. | No issue or register row for suggestions; did-you-mean/levenshtein absent from bd and the register. Message-only change, sysc-740 unaffected.

title: [pleamar] Declare the config format: optional version marker with a named mismatch
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-core-lang-05).

Recommendation: Decide the marker deliberately - this is the cluster's lowest-confidence row (0.55) and the reconciliation asks for a Wave-4 decision rather than inferred ownership - and recommend the small version: record the current format in what config.Write already emits, so a document states what wrote it, and when Parse meets a declared format it does not understand, refuse it with a message naming both numbers instead of a bare `unknown field`. An absent key means a legacy document and keeps loading exactly as today; this stops at detect-and-name, it does not promise migration (pleamar ships none either - docs/08-limitations.md:63, G26).

Approach: internal/config: one optional top-level key beside the existing 18 in wireConfig (load.go:217-236), emitted by Write's sparse writer (write.go:18-23, which already records the selected preset and so is the natural place for provenance), and checked in Parse before validation (load.go:314-330). If sysc-740 (schema single-sourcing) lands first, the marker belongs in that schema rather than as a hand-added field; until then it is one constant and one comparison. No dependency, no UI.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: S · impact: L.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: The marker must not be sold as compatibility: an older shell still refuses a newer file through DisallowUnknownFields, so the gain is a clear message and a future migration anchor. If the owner prefers no marker, the honest alternative is to keep the current refusal as the contract and record that decision; either way the choice should be explicit rather than implied by the loader.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-core-06)
Audit: pass — internal/config only; the deliberate Wave-4/owner decision is recorded (0.55 row); no dependency, no UI; no estimates. | sysc-740 does not add a version marker; reconciliation leaves this to a Wave-4/owner decision and the rec makes it explicitly (detect-and-name only).

title: [pleamar] Collect multiple config problems per pass, bounded and deduplicated
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-core-lang-04).

Recommendation: Let one reload report several problems instead of one per attempt, bounded and deduplicated, while keeping whole-candidate atomicity. Parse already applies independent sections one after another and returns on the first failure (load.go:330-430), so a collector can keep each section's error and continue, and items() can accumulate per-item errors inside one bar (load.go:1077-1089). The candidate is still refused entire - Resolve (reload.go:11-20) and the owner's keep-last-good (client.go:1129-1148) do not change - so nothing partial is applied. The joined list appears wherever today's single error appears, capped and deduplicated by path+message, reusing the aggregation the shell already trusts (errors.Join in the settings rollback, popout_settings.go:1722) and pleamar's cap of eight errors (compiler.rs:998-1011).

Approach: internal/config: a small collector threaded through Parse's section dispatch (load.go:330-430) and items() (load.go:1077-1089); individual apply* helpers keep returning their own first error, so the change is local to the two accumulation points plus the formatter. Stop accumulating at structural decode errors (load.go:318-330): after a malformed JSON document nothing further is trustworthy. The cap and dedupe live in one place and apply to whichever renderer formats the error - with REC-core-03 the entries already carry positions, so the list reads as N located problems rather than N paths.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: L.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: Aggregation must never become partial application: Resolve and keep-last-good stay whole-candidate. Some failures are causal (a bad value in one section can make later sections' errors meaningless), so cap the list and do not chase completeness; and a badly edited file must not produce hundreds of lines - the cap is part of the deliverable, not a nicety.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-core-07)
Audit: pass — extends Parse/items accumulation with the atomic-reject and keep-last-good contract untouched; no dependency; no estimates. | Multi-error collection unowned: sysc-740 single-sources schema validation but does not aggregate; fail-fast is the loader's current intent.

title: [pleamar] Keep the single dispatch loop; shrink, measure and cap its first-party frame work
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-core-rt-02).

Recommendation: Keep the single dispatch/owner rule - AGENTS.md:18 and client.go:186-188 put Wayland dispatch on one goroutine, and this rec moves no dispatch, so REC-perf-04's bounded raster-only paint worker stays compatible (it splits raster, not dispatch). Finish the owned work that moves unbounded first-party effort off the loop (sysc-1152, sysc-1148) and enforce the discipline the plugin path already proves: work whose cost depends on data (directory reads, process scans, shaping a cold string) runs on a worker, never in the owner's renderJob. Add the piece the reconciliation calls unowned, with this rec as its single owner (distinct from REC-perf-05/06's recorder and census): bounded frame-work measurement on the render path, because stallwatch's 3-second threshold (stallwatch.go:14-30) cannot see a 30 ms layout+paint stall, plus a degradation lever that already exists - the animator's frame cap - for a surface class that repeatedly exceeds its budget.

Approach: internal/platform/wayland: stamp the render path (client.go:1040-1055, u.app.Render at :1047) with the existing trace region (startTraceRegion, client.go:1042) and keep a bounded per-surface-class histogram exported through the existing diagnostics route (cmd/sysc-shell/diagnostics.go:19-42) or sysc-metrics. Model any automatic degradation on the plugin preparer's overrun window/limit (internal/plugin/prepare.go:66-75, :111-128) and pull the lever that exists: animateSurface's minInterval callback and animator.frameCap (internal/shell/animation.go:612-617, :631-695). sysc-454 (frame-callback-driven sampling) is the owned clock work and should land first; sysc-317's design rule (no work under the dispatch loop) is the policy this enforces. Dispatch does not move and REC-perf-04's bounded raster-only paint worker remains compatible; the render-path histogram is owned here (REC-perf-05/06 own their recorder and census, not it).

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: L.
Prerequisites: sysc-1152, sysc-1148, sysc-454.
Risk: Telemetry without a consumer is dead weight: the histogram must feed a named gate (deploy/completion evidence via sysc-metrics) or the degradation lever, else drop it. Silently capping a first-party surface hides bugs, so any automatic pacing must be reported once in the stall-dump/report style. The architectural alternative - a separate renderer/clock that keeps painting - is an owner decision against AGENTS.md:18, not a Wave-4 rec; if the owner wants it, it needs its own design.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-core-08)
Audit: revise — single-dispatch rule kept per AGENTS.md:18; rung existing (stallwatch.go, diagnostics.go, prepare.go:66-128 verified); histogram explicitly gated on a named consumer; no new renderer goroutine; no estimates. | O4: drop the absolute 'one goroutine, no architecture change' framing so it cannot be read as foreclosing REC-perf-04's raster-only paint worker, and name one owner for render-path frame-work measurement (this rec) vs REC-perf-05/06's recorder/census so the diagnostics are not built twice. Partial ownership (sysc-1152/1148/454) is stated correctly.

title: [pleamar] Report-only build takeover and no-op deploys that skip the restart
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-core-lang-08).

Recommendation: Keep the deploy guard's integrity trade and treat takeover as reporting, not self-reexec. sysc-744 (open) already owns the fitting shape - a check that only reports plus the existing unit restart - so this rec adds the two unowned pieces around it: the check names the running build's provenance as well as the newer stamped build it found, and scripts/deploy stops paying a full unit restart, and the panel-state loss that costs, when the build it just made is byte-identical to what is already installed. Automatic self-takeover stays excluded; if the owner ever wants it, it belongs in the unit/path-watch layer as a separate approved design, not in the shell process.

Approach: scripts/deploy-install.sh already installs, hashes and stamps the binary (:29-39) and restarts the unit at :41-49; compute the freshly built binary's sha256 before install and skip install+restart when it matches the installed one - the same comparison the guard makes at startup (scripts/sysc-shell-guard:26-27, stamp path :14). For the report, extend sysc-744's check to compare the running binary against the stamp and print the running and deployed revisions; the running side comes from the stamp's revision field, so the shell never re-implements the guard's hashing and the guard stays the single owner of the stamp format.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: S · impact: L.
Prerequisites: sysc-744 (owns the report-only check; this rec extends its content and the deploy path).
Risk: The stamp is XDG state written by a shell script, not a stable API: read it in one place and tolerate a missing or partial stamp (report unknown, never fail startup, matching the guard's never-block contract). Skipping the restart is safe only when the comparison is the installed binary's hash; a rebuild that differs at all still restarts, which is the safe direction. Do not let the report grow an automatic restart action without the owner's decision - that is the boundary the guard exists to hold.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-core-09)
Audit: pass — scripts verified (deploy-install.sh:29-39, sysc-shell-guard:14/26-27); self-takeover excluded per the owner-decision gap; rung existing; no deps; no estimates. | sysc-744 (partial) owns the report-only check; running-build provenance in the report and the byte-identical no-op deploy skip are unowned.

title: [pleamar] User-settable repaint cap for animating surfaces
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-perf-02).

Recommendation: Expose the already theme-resolved pacing cap as a user setting, so an always-animating surface on a 120/165 Hz output can be capped without a rebuild: add an appearance.frame-cap entry (closed vocabulary, default = display rate, otherwise 60/90/120) beside appearance.motion-speed, and plumb it config -> theme -> render.MotionSet.Durations so animator.frameCap (internal/shell/animation.go:612) and every minInterval closure (bar.go:767, panelhost.go:4453, toasthost.go:870, osd.go:270) pick it up unchanged. The cap only ever lowers the publish rate: effect-only surfaces keep their 66 ms floor (animation.go:53), the settling frame keeps publishing inside the cap window (animation.go:675), and reduced motion is unaffected because it settles immediately. This is the user-facing half of GAP-perf-02; the mechanism itself shipped fixed at 4 ms by the rendering-smoothness plan.

Approach: internal/theme/profile.go: carry the cap beside MotionTokens.FrameCap (profile.go:381-412) and keep it out of AtSpeed, which deliberately does not scale FrameCap (profile.go:419-442); resolve it where durations are already resolved (Composition.Durations, profile.go:666-668) or in a sibling resolver. internal/shell/theme.go:201 (Motion: render.MotionSet{Durations: comp.Durations(), ...}) is the one place the resolved table reaches every surface, so no animator call site changes. internal/config: a new appearance/theme field with a closed vocabulary validated exactly like Wallpaper.FPS (config.go:411, load.go:1681 and the wallpaperFPS map with pathErr at load.go:1709) so an unknown value is a load error rather than a silent default. internal/settings/registry.go: one KindEnum entry modelled on appearance.motion (registry.go:255-262) with Get/Set writing the config field, placed in the Appearance/Animation group beside appearance.motion-speed (registry.go:264-270) so settings search and the theme IPC path carry it for free. Rung existing: config validation, the settings registry, theme resolution and the publish gate all ship in-tree; no new dependency and no new UI primitive (the settings row reuses KindEnum).

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: A cap that is too slow makes short transitions steppy: the value must stay below the shortest motion token (75 ms Short, profile.go:399) while a surface is interacting, and lowering the cap mid-animation must never leave a settled value unpainted (the settling publish at animation.go:675). Effect-only surfaces must keep the 66 ms floor so a weather panel does not return to interaction-rate painting, which is the baseline sysc-413 measures against. The display-rate default keeps today's behaviour, so the change is opt-in and reversible from settings.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-perf-01)
Audit: pass — FrameCap is fixed today (profile.go:412) and the four frameCap call sites check out (bar.go:767, panelhost.go:4453, toasthost.go:870, osd.go:270); one KindEnum reuse so no new primitive; no dependency; no estimates. | FrameCap never reaches config/settings and no issue exposes it; bd's only effect-rate control (sysc-1013, in_progress) is the locker's effect_fps, a different binary.

title: [pleamar] Adopt the built damage path: bar first, then panels, toasts and the OSD
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-perf-07).

Recommendation: Turn the smoothness plan's built-but-unadopted damage path into a production win. Publish the bar's existing node-diff regions through HostCallbacks.Damaged (host.go:53-57) so renderJob submits per-rectangle DamageBuffer calls instead of the whole buffer (client.go:1056, with the full-buffer fallback in damageRects at client.go:1004), then generalise the bar's region cache into a shared per-surface paint cache that panels, toasts and the OSD use, reusing render.PaintRegion (paint.go:173) and following the selector, which is the only production opt-in today (screenshot_selector.go:168). Context and prerequisite: sysc-413 (open) owns the weather-effect region and the register already records the path as built, not adopted (sysc-shell/docs/plans/README.md:302); this rec is the adoption half, not new machinery.

Approach: internal/shell/bar_render_cache.go: barDamageRegions and mergeBarDamage (:71, :208) already compute the regions and render.PaintRegion already repaints them (bar.go:646); keep the last painted frame's regions on the bar host and return them from Damaged, remembering two contracts: a callback that reports nothing means the whole buffer (damageRects, client.go:1006-1011) and each callback must copy the last complete frame into the slot before partial paint (the reasoning is documented at bar_render_cache.go:10-23). internal/shell: lift barPaintCache (bar_render_cache.go:14-53) into a surface-agnostic cache and give PanelHost.render (panelhost.go:2278) and toastHost.paintCard (toasthost.go:487) the same previous-tree diff, then set Damaged on their AuxSpec callbacks; panels already paint a copied tree (panelhost.go:2290 copyNode), so the comparator is samePaintNode/barTreeCacheable (bar_render_cache.go:58, :119) with a kind allow-list rather than the bar-only blacklist. Keep render.DamageSet as the accumulator and MarkFull as the escape hatch (damage.go:34, :42) and do not move damage into the Scheduler - design D1 rejected that (sysc-worktree/docs/plans/2026-09-11-rendering-smoothness-design.md). For the weather panel the container's dirty rect is the effect node's physical box, which is the region sysc-413 asks for. Rung existing: DamageSet, damageRects, PaintRegion, the node comparator and the bar's region logic all ship in-tree.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: sysc-413.
Risk: Damage is an optimisation and never a correctness boundary (damage.go:5-10; design D5): a region that is too small leaves stale pixels rather than crashing, so each surface's region set needs a pixel-diff test against full paint, and any tree that cannot be diffed (dynamic lists, Item/Schedule nodes - barTreeCacheable, bar_render_cache.go:58) must fall back to full buffer. Panels hold a backdrop captured once, so partial painting must not assume the backdrop is repainted; and the bar already paints partially on the CPU, so the user-visible win is compositor traffic and power, not the bar's own paint cost.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-perf-02)
Audit: pass — rung existing (bar_render_cache.go, damage.go:34/42, screenshot_selector.go:168 opt-in verified); nothing new is drawn; prerequisite sysc-413; no estimates. | sysc-413 (partial) covers the weather-effect region only; adoption for bar/panels/toasts/OSD is unowned (register :302: built, not adopted). O6 boundary with REC-perf-04, sequence damage adoption first.

title: M7 live Niri gate: launcher on a real compositor
description:
Live Niri gate for the launcher. sysc-90 is closed; panels paint (sysc-41 closed). No extra sysc-launch daemon: that module is an in-process library plus a one-shot CLI (query/launch). The shell already constructs launcher.NewService and relays results.

Desktop icons: v1 does not render them. Entry.IconName is populated from the desktop file. launcherRow paints KindButton/KindText only; launcherIconSlot (40) is reserved and unused. The Icon seam from the pre-extraction plan was dropped. Real icons are sysc-117 (shell-side KindImage + internal/icons), not a new service.

Remaining live checks: Super+Space opens on the focused output; typing filters; arrows move; Enter spawns via niri; right-click actions; reopen after >60s rescans. One output is enough for this gate.

title: [pleamar] Reuse a bounded offscreen scratch for translucent groups and batch disjoint siblings
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-perf-05).

Recommendation: Stop allocating a fresh full-surface canvas for every translucent group. Paint opacity groups through a bounded, size-keyed scratch buffer that internal/render owns and reuses across groups and frames, and where two or more sibling groups cannot see each other (their physical bounds are disjoint) paint them in one scratch pass and composite each group's own box once. The bar's blur regions already batch rows this way (ui.BlurStrips and mergeRows, internal/ui/blurshape.go:33, :124-129) and the toast host already keeps a per-surface scratch for exactly this reason (toasthost.go:56, :496-499); this rec generalises both into the renderer. The effect path is already on this discipline - RoundedMask is served from the bounded geometry cache (mask.go:125-132) and weather sprites are baked once and shared process-wide (weather_sprite.go:112) - so it is left alone and the translucent-group canvas is the remaining per-paint allocation.

Approach: internal/render/paint.go: paintNodeOpacity (paint.go:316-357) is the allocation to fix - replace NewCanvas(make([]byte, len(c.Pix)), ...) with a scratch taken from a pool, paint the group under the existing clip (offscreen.restrict = c.restrict, paint.go:330), then clear only the group's box before returning it to the pool (the toast copy loop at toasthost.go:519-528 is the in-tree precedent for a reused scratch plus a box copy). internal/render/canvas.go: hold the pool beside NewCanvas (canvas.go:118) as a small size-keyed freelist with a retained-bytes budget and eviction, matching the conventions already in the tree - geometryCacheBudget and its eviction loop (mask.go:52-57, :77-89), the text shape/raster budgets (text.go:120, :252-253) and icons.Worker.store (icons/worker.go:445-463) - and release it on resize the way pleamar releases idle offscreen layers (pleamar/src/gpu.rs:2320-2336). Batch only provably disjoint siblings into one scratch pass; overlapping groups composite sequentially and each is cleared inside its own box. The effect path needs no change: paintEffect (effect.go:20-49) already takes its RoundedMask from the bounded geometry cache (mask.go:125-132) and its weather raster from the process-wide baked sprite cache (weather_sprite.go:112). Rung existing: the offscreen mechanism, the clip discipline, the budget/eviction conventions and a per-surface scratch precedent all ship.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: A pooled scratch must never outlive the paint that owns it (a surface retaining the canvas is how a stale frame appears) and must be cleared only inside the group's own box, or overlapping siblings composite wrongly. Batch eligibility needs disjointness in physical pixels (scale x logical bounds), not logical bounds, and any doubt falls back to per-group painting. The pool must be bounded: the gap's cost driver is bytes, so an unbounded pool trades an allocation for RSS. Pixel output must stay byte-identical - the composition tests (internal/render/composition_test.go) and the paint goldens are the gate.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-perf-03)
Audit: pass — rung existing (paintNodeOpacity, toast scratch, geometry/text/icon budgets verified); bounded pool only, no dependency; no estimates. | O3 canonical: the pooled offscreen scratch belongs here; REC-vis-05 is revised to stop re-specifying the same allocation/bounding change. sysc-1114 (partial, cache bytes) is a different mechanism.

title: [pleamar] Snapshot under the registry lock, raster off the owner loop
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-perf-01).

Recommendation: Keep the one dispatch goroutine - the owner stays the only thing that talks to Wayland, handles input and commits buffers - but stop paint from being the work that can block it. Split each surface's render callback into a locked snapshot step (copy the retained tree, resolve style/theme) and an unlocked raster step, and hand the raster to a bounded paint worker that fills a spare buffer generation and gives it back to the owner to attach. The owner then returns to its poll immediately after queueing paint (client.go:1393-1404), so a long Registry.mu holder on a service path delays a frame instead of freezing every surface at once. This is the residual class of GAP-perf-01 after the named paths sysc-1152 and sysc-1148 fix, and it is a raster-only split: dispatch does not move.

Approach: internal/platform/wayland/client.go: renderJob (:1038-1058) is the split point - today the owner asks u.app.Render for pixels and submits on the same turn; add a paint queue in front of it so nextJob (:1393) can hand off the raster while the loop keeps polling, with the completed generation attached and damaged on the next turn (the buffer lifecycle already keeps alternating generations plus the Damaged callback, host.go:53-57, client.go:1056). internal/shell: the render callbacks are where the lock is taken today - PanelHost.render (panelhost.go:2278) already copies its tree (copyNode, :2290) and hosting calls it under Registry.mu (panelhost.go:2102); move the copy/resolve under the lock and the render.Paint call outside it. Bar.render (bar.go:631) already retains its last complete frame in barPaintCache (bar_render_cache.go:10-23), so it snapshots the same way; toasts already paint from a per-card scratch (toasthost.go:487). Service state should keep reaching paint through the existing lease/pushed-snapshot pattern (internal/services/leases.go; network.go:197 Acquire) instead of being read synchronously from a paint path, which is what makes the snapshot lock-short. Extend stallwatch.go (:38-56) to distinguish owner-blocked from raster-worker-slow so a regression stays attributable, and keep the startTraceRegion stages (trace.go:11-16) on both halves. Sequence: land REC-perf-02's damage adoption (the repaint path) first - both rewrite renderJob and the buffer generations (client.go:1038-1058) - and split raster after it, so the repaint path changes once. Rung existing: the owner loop, the generation/buffer lifecycle, the per-surface caches and the stall watchdog all ship; only the handoff is new.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: L · impact: M.
Prerequisites: sysc-1152, sysc-1148.
Risk: The snapshot must be immutable while it is painted (the panel's copyNode exists for this reason; the bar's tree is rebuilt by the registry under r.mu), so the worker must never hold Registry.mu. Queued paint adds up to one buffered frame of latency unless the spare generation is painted and the last complete frame stays attached. A raster-only split does not make the Wayland side async: a surface that cannot produce a snapshot at all still has to fall back to painting on the owner, so the path must degrade rather than stall.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-perf-04)
Audit: pass — rung existing with a bounded, demand-driven raster worker; one dispatch goroutine and no free-running renderer kept per AGENTS.md:18, so compliant as written (closest architecture call in the set); prerequisites sysc-1152/1148; no estimates. | sysc-1152/sysc-1148 (partial) cover the named owner-loop paths; the raster split is unowned. O4/O6 boundaries: compatible with REC-core-08 (dispatch stays) and shares renderJob with REC-perf-02.

title: [pleamar] Per-frame named-value recording: one recorder, an opt-in CLI capture plus an in-repo harness
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-perf-03).

Recommendation: Add a per-frame named-value recorder to the shell's animation path, tapped where frames are actually published, and give it two front ends. First, an opt-in user-runnable capture - sysc-shell record --names surface:key:channel,... [--seconds N] [--out FILE], a sibling of the existing sysc-shell ipc subcommand - writing ms<TAB>value... rows the way pleamar's --record does, so a user or developer can check an animation against its contract without Go tooling. Second, an in-repo harness that drives fixture trees through the same recorder with the animator's injectable clock, so the recorder's contract test runs in CI. The key design choice is that the harness is the second consumer of the same recorder rather than a separate instrument: nothing is logged unless asked for, so the P2 handover's rule against per-frame production logging on the live owner (sysc-worktree/docs/plans/2026-10-12-p2-performance-fix-handover.md:37) is respected, and the runnable capture is the capability GAP-perf-03 measured as absent.

Approach: internal/shell/animation.go: samples come from the loop that already publishes (:642-695) - emit inside the publish branch (:675) so the log contains exactly the frames that were blitted, reading the keyed value table (animKey, :86-89; ui.Node.Key is the stable identity, internal/ui/tree.go:235-239) and the surface id; the copy must be taken outside Registry.mu, or the recorder perturbs the path it measures. The animator's clock is already injectable (newAnimator(now func() time.Time, ...), :170-177; r.animClock at panelhost.go:1307), which is what lets the harness step frames deterministically instead of sleeping. Writer: a bounded TSV writer following the diagnostics file policy (0600 files under $XDG_STATE_HOME/sysc-shell, cmd/sysc-shell/diagnostics.go:44-122), flushed by whoever owns the file. Plumbing: a new ipc.Handlers field (internal/ipc/server.go:58-77) and a registry method shaped like Status (registry.go:1116-1140), wired beside the existing handlers in cmd/sysc-shell/main.go:398-408, plus the CLI subcommand next to the ipc arm (main.go:445-466); the SIGUSR2 capture can close the log with the other artefacts (diagnostics.go:70-75). Harness: tests/integration, gated like the other live gates (the hand-run ancestor is tests/integration/README.md:44, and the package already re-execs fake backends, harness_test.go:17-66), painting fixture trees through render.NewCanvas the way cmd/sysc-panel-preview/render.go:34 already does, then diffing the TSV against a contract file. Rung existing: the value table, the publish loop, the injectable clock, the diagnostics file policy and the IPC plumbing all ship.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: L.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: Recording must not change what is painted or hold Registry.mu on the publish path, so samples are emitted after the lock is released into a preallocated writer with a bounded ring. Node keys are per-surface, so recorded names must be namespaced by surface id or a plugin key can collide. A channel no surface animates should report 'nothing recorded' rather than writing an empty file, and the flag needs the naming contract documented with it or the log is unreadable. The harness must keep the same recorder in both paths, or the CI contract and the user-runnable capture drift.

title: [pleamar] Per-part growth census and an automated soak gate
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-perf-06).

Recommendation: Give long sessions a growth floor. First, a per-part 'kept' census - goroutines, open FDs, surface units and retained bytes per budgeted cache - reported by the existing IPC status method and written with the SIGUSR2 diagnostic capture, sourced from each cache owner's own accounting so it needs no Go tooling. Second, a soak gate in tests/integration that drives open/close cycles and samples RSS, threads, FDs and the census, failing on monotone growth after warm-up. This replaces the hand-run '60-minute idle run' line (tests/integration/README.md:44) with a repeatable gate, gives the memory claims per-part attribution, and leaves sysc-1119's heap profile as the deep tool and sysc-1114 as the cache-bound half.

Approach: cmd/sysc-shell/diagnostics.go: writeMemorySummary (:128-144) already writes a .mem line set from runtime.ReadMemStats - extend it with the census and log the path as the capture already does (:103, :120), keeping SIGUSR2 as the trigger (watchDiagnostics, :19-42). internal/render, internal/icons, internal/shell: expose existing accounting rather than re-measuring - geometryCacheBudget with the cache's bytes and entries (mask.go:52-57, :77-89), the text shape/raster budgets (text.go:120, :252-253), icons.Worker.store's bytes (worker.go:445-463), the baked weather sprite cache (weather_sprite.go:112), and the registry's own counts (Registry.Status is where a census key fits without a new IPC method, registry.go:1116-1140, which already enumerates panelHosts). Sample off the owner using the stallwatch ticker pattern (stallwatch.go:20-57: one goroutine, a one-second poll, no lock on the observed vector), so the sampler never touches the paint path. Harness: a Go soak test in tests/integration gated by an environment variable (the package already re-execs fake backends, harness_test.go:17-66) that opens and closes panels and toasts in a Niri session, samples every N seconds and applies pleamar-wm-style tolerances (bounded growth per part after warm-up; fail on monotone growth, not on absolute RSS). Rung existing: every count is already kept by its owner, the reader is the shell's own CLI and the gate reuses tests/integration.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: L.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: A growth gate is only useful if it is not flaky: bounded caches are supposed to grow to their budget and stop, so the gate must warm up, compare after warm-up and fail on monotone growth per part rather than on absolute RSS - otherwise eviction behaviour or a larger wallpaper is reported as a leak. A live Niri session is required, so the soak stays out of the default test path; the census must be O(caches) and lock-light or it perturbs what it measures; and samples taken around service snapshot points add noise, so the report should carry the parts, not a verdict alone.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-perf-06)
Audit: pass — rung existing; census reuses existing accounting and IPC Status; the 60-minute idle-run quote is the README line being replaced (README:44), not a work estimate; no dependency; no estimates. | No shell soak/growth gate exists (sysc-912/974 are wallpaper/lock qualification); rec correctly defers to sysc-1119 and sysc-1114 as the deep tools.

title: [pleamar] Desktop-widget host generalised from the depth-clock Bottom-layer surface
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-uiux-surf-06).

Recommendation: After the sysc-206 design lands (that issue is design-only by its own text), implement desktop widgets by generalising the wallpaper depth-clock surface into a per-output desktop-surface host in sysc-shell, then expose it on the plugin wire as the desktop view kind sysc-704 describes. Plugin path (sysc-704): add ViewDesktop to plugin/v1 knownViews (node.go:392) and route it through pluginhost.go, reusing the per-view kind validation at node.go:433.
