title: [pleamar] Pre-roll recorder countdown and capture-aware status placement
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-uiux-surf-08).

Recommendation: Cover the two parts sysc-138 leaves unowned: the recorder plugin runs a pre-roll countdown on a floating surface and starts gpu-screen-recorder only after that surface closes, so the count is never inside the video; and the shell places the recording status surface using a capture exclusion rectangle supplied by the recorder, preferring a corner or output outside the captured area. sysc-138 keeps owning the attached panel itself; this rec is the countdown plus capture-aware placement around it.

Approach: sysc-plugins/plugins/screen-recorder: add a Countdown state to the mode machine (recorder.go:16-25) and render it through the existing view layer (view.go) on the plugin floating surface; order launch so the countdown surface closes before process.go starts the recorder. sysc-shell: floating surfaces already exist (SurfaceOpenParams, plugin/v1/message.go:352; openFloatingSurface with its Placement, pluginsurface.go:126) - extend the surface-open parameters and the placement helper so the recorder can pass its capture rect and the shell picks a position outside it (panelplace.go:11 panelPlacement, using output rectangles the registry already tracks), pinning via the existing SurfacePinParams path. Rung existing: the plugin mode machine, the floating-surface host and the placement code all ship; only the Countdown state and the exclusion input are new. No new dependencies.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: sysc-138.
Risk: The plugin owns recording state, so the shell cannot count down on its own, and the portal video_source may expose no capture rect - then only the countdown half applies; the close-before-start ordering is the contract that keeps the countdown out of the file, and gpu-screen-recorder start behaviour must be observed once implemented.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-usurf-02)
Audit: pass — rung existing (recorder mode machine verified in sysc-plugins; floating-surface and placement anchors verified in sysc-main); companion work stays in an existing repo; no deps; no estimates. | sysc-138 (partial) owns the attached panel; pre-roll countdown and capture-aware placement are unowned. Adjacent sysc-766 (anchor tokens), sysc-1362/130 (recorder process items).

title: [pleamar] Shell-composed ScreenCast chooser (owner decision)
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-uiux-surf-03).

Recommendation: If the owner reverses the sysc-compositor stance that screen sharing rides the external xdg-desktop-portal-gnome pair, add an in-family pick surface: an org.freedesktop.impl.portal.ScreenCast SelectSources request opens the shell's own window/monitor chooser instead of the external dialog, and Escape answers cancel. Scope this rec to the chooser plus the Go ScreenCast backend skeleton in sysc-shell; the PipeWire stream transport is part of the same owner decision and is not assumed here.

Approach: New Go backend inside sysc-shell (one repository) exporting org.freedesktop.impl.portal.ScreenCast on the session bus with the already-pinned github.com/godbus/dbus/v5 v5.2.2 (go.mod:20; connect/export pattern as in internal/services/media_bus.go:62 and internal/services/polkit/agent.go:246). The pick surface composes the existing window switcher card and rows (window_switcher_host.go:185-233) for windows and the Monitor panel facts (monitorframe.go) for outputs; a future stream producer would sit behind an interface over the shell's existing wlr-screencopy capture (internal/platform/wayland/capture.go:188), with the PipeWire transport left to the owner decision (sysc-compositor design lines 327/337 keep the external pair and make screencast a PipeWire/compositor concern). Rung new-code: no in-family portal or ScreenCast code exists (gap-row counter-greps), while the pick UI reuses existing hosts; the rec cannot start without the owner decision.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: new-code · scope: L · impact: L.
Prerequisites: owner decision on an in-family ScreenCast backend.
Risk: The owner may keep the external chooser (the design doc's current direction); without a stream producer the pick surface has no consumer; implementing a portal backend risks scope creep toward a full portal suite and raises the second-consumer/stable-API question for a new sysc-shell service.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-usurf-03)
Audit: pass — new-code justified (no in-family portal/ScreenCast code); pin godbus v5.2.2 matches go.mod:20; OWNER-DECISION reversal of design :337 recorded; PipeWire transport and CGO explicitly out of scope; lock_or_compositor 'no' is truthful (shell overlay + session service, no compositor code); no estimates. | Owner decision: the sysc-compositor design deliberately keeps sharing on the external portal pair and no issue plans an in-family chooser; scope stays shell-side with PipeWire transport owner-gated.

title: [pleamar] Spring-carried scroll offset and drag-from-any-row in shell panels
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-uiux-int-06).

Recommendation: Give the existing scroll model travel and a pointer drag on the content itself. A wheel step or scrollbar jump currently sets ui.Node.ScrollOffset immediately (panelhost.go:2927 scrollByOn -> ui/scroll.go:3); route it through the surface's existing animator as a scroll channel so the offset travels with the shell's curve and retargets mid-flight when a second step arrives, the way pleamar's view rule moves the offset with the layout spring (pleamar/src/language/compiler.rs:6161). For drag-to-scroll, extend the panel press path that today drags only the scrollbar thumb (panelhost.go:2462-2469) to begin a content drag from any row of a KindScroll/KindVirtualList body, reusing ui.Drag (internal/ui/drag.go:22-46) and ui.ScrollBy/clampScroll; release lets the animated channel settle. Keep no inertia on release - pleamar has none either (pleamar/docs/08-limitations.md:103) - so parity is the bar, not momentum.

Approach: internal/ui/scroll.go keeps the clamp/value model (ScrollBy:3, ScrollSetFromY:66, VisibleRange:95). internal/shell/panelhost.go: add an animScroll channel to the per-surface animator (internal/shell/animation.go:60-70 channel set; Target:368 and Retarget:570 already animate and retarget mid-flight), call it from scrollAxis (:2853-2883) and scrollByOn (:2927) instead of setting the offset directly; add a content-drag branch beside scrollTrackAt (:3019) reusing ui.Drag with the hovered scroll body as source. Consumers already in-tree: plugin store list, settings, clipboard, launcher rows. Offset read-back for plugins stays on the existing view snapshot path (plugin/v1/message.go:195). Rung existing: animator, clamp and drag struct all ship; the channel plus the drag branch are the only new code. No new dependencies.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: Overscroll after clamp must not fight the animator (pin the channel to the clamp each tick); drag-to-scroll must start only after the 8 px ui.Drag threshold (drag.go:34) so row clicks survive, and must not force virtual-list row instantiation while dragging.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-uint-01)
Audit: pass — rung existing (panelhost.go:2853/2927, ui/scroll.go verified); channel reuses the existing ScrollOffset + animator, no new primitive; no dependency; no estimates. | O2 boundary with REC-core-01: scroll travel uses the shipped animator channels (Target/Retarget); a spring channel is optional later and must never be a prerequisite. No fold.

title: [pleamar] Propose/approve card for assistant-originated actions (conditional on an assistant surface)
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-uiux-int-10).

Recommendation: Prepare the approval card as a card pattern, not a toolkit: a proposal renders as a pending card with detail text, a body and 'Not this'/'Allow' actions, a free-hands tri-state chooses 'asks before each step' vs 'uses the computer', and an unapproved proposal simply waits (marea-plm/logic/chat.luau:733-773, chat_allow/deny at :1121-1130; marea-plm/scene/draw/chat.plm:54-84; settings.plm:90). Sysc has the ingredients - destructive-action confirm cards (popout_clipboard.go:298-317, bluetoothbody.go:270-277) and a keyboard-grabbing auth dialog (services/polkit/agent.go:104) - but no agent-originated actions, so this rec is conditional on the assistant integration (twin GAP-dx-plug-11) and the agent-seat decision (GAP-integ-ses-05). Keep it needs-design: the card UX can be specified now, the action pipeline cannot.

Approach: When the assistant surface exists, compose the card from existing host parts: a card subtree in the assistant panel/host tree, actions routed through the host action handler pattern (registry.go:1863-1954), keyboard loan while the card is pending via the surface keyboard modes (panelhost.go:1885) with parked focus following the toast-reply precedent (toasthost.go:610-644). The card state machine (proposed/awaiting/allowed/denied plus the free-hands tri-state) belongs to the assistant pipeline (GAP-dx-plug-11); the shell side is the card, its two actions and the settings tri-state. Rung existing: card and dialog patterns ship; the only new primitive-shaped thing is a card variant with two named actions, with the assistant as the named consumer. No new dependencies.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: S · impact: M.
Prerequisites: GAP-dx-plug-11 (assistant propose/approve pipeline), GAP-integ-ses-05 (agent-seat owner decision).
Risk: No consumer exists today, so building the card ahead of the assistant surface would be dead UI; if the owner picks a seat-driven agent instead of an assistant chat, the card's state machine moves with that choice. Attach it to the assistant scope to avoid a standalone toolkit.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-uint-02)
Audit: pass — conditional rec that writes nothing until the assistant pipeline lands; rung existing; card pattern with a named consumer, not a toolkit; no dependency; no estimates. | O7 canonical for the approval card (GAP-uiux-int-10); REC-dplug-03 revised to hand the card here. Conditional on the assistant pipeline and seat decision as declared.
notes: STAYS IN sysc-shell. Design: agent-experience-design.md D2-D2.10. Gated on a producer, NOT on the compositor: approval needs a decider and a moment, not a wl_seat, so the shell can gate in-process against HostCall/HostReply once sysc-1217 produces proposals. Blocked until sysc-1217 has an answer AND Tier 1 has shipped (Tier 1 is being implemented separately). Specified as a card pattern with a named consumer, not a toolkit. Adds no code to Tier 1's closed 13-code vocabulary; 'Not this' is a decision recorded in a separate durable decision log, not an error. Not closing.

title: [pleamar] Declarative zone vocabulary resolved over existing ui trees and plugin views
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-uiux-int-01).

Recommendation: Introduce zones as resolved metadata over the trees sysc already builds, not as a new widget layer. A zone is a named node region with an active condition, a z-rank for hit order, a cursor, a carried payload type, a scroll target and a reach (person vs agent). Hit order already works by reverse child walk with menu popups first (internal/ui/layout.go:795-836); the zone pass layers explicit z over that same walk and returns a zone identity beside the action, so bar sections, panel bodies and plugin views share one hit vocabulary. Config can then name a zone - a bar region, a panel hot area, a whole-region wheel target - instead of requiring new Go, and plugins declare the same fields on their wire nodes: the wire already carries drag_type/accept/payload (plugin/v1/node.go:328-332), so the zone extension follows a shipped precedent.

Approach: internal/ui: optional zone fields on ui.Node (cursor name, z, scrolls/within, reach, active guard) and a Zones(root) resolver built on the existing layout pass; extend Hit (layout.go:795) to consult z while keeping the reverse-walk fallback. internal/shell: bar and tray routing already dispatch per action and button (registry.go:1863-1954, tray.go:527-554) - feed it zone IDs; wheel routing (panelhost.go:2853-2881) resolves the zone's scroll target. Plugin wire: extend v1.Node with the zone fields beside DragType/Accept (node.go:328-332) and validate them like other kinds (node.go:377-388 event tables). Consumers: bar sections, plugin panels, launcher rows; aux surfaces (depth clock, selector) are not zones. Rung existing: the tree, hit walk and routing ship; the zone pass and metadata are additive. No dependencies.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: Zone metadata must not become a second layout engine: only nodes that declare a zone are affected, and non-declaring trees must keep today's behavior unchanged; explicit z must agree with paint order or menus regress.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-uint-03)
Audit: pass — zones are metadata over existing trees with named consumer classes (bar/panels/launcher); hit walk layout.go:795-836 and wire precedent node.go:328-332 verified; plugin wire fields ride a shipped precedent (not a new primitive); no dependency; no estimates. | Zone vocabulary unowned; sysc-1412 is bar-scoped scroll/dead-zone bindings, not a config-declarable zone/z/hit pass. REC-uint-04 consumes its trigger table (declared).

title: Execute the Milestone 5 live matrix once the services exist
description: Every notification and tray live check is unrun: sysc-notifyd and the sysc-tray daemon do not exist at v0.1.0-rc.2 and v0.1.0-rc.1, and only one output is connected. The matrix is written in tests/integration/README.md under 'Milestone 5'. Blocks any stable service tag.

title: [pleamar] Pointer vocabulary: press-and-hold, drag-out/in with data, per-zone cursors
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-uiux-int-04).

Recommendation: Complete the pointer vocabulary in three additive pieces. Press-and-hold: the press path starts a click or drag today (panelhost.go:2471-2488) - add a hold timer on the pressed node that fires only if motion stays under the 8 px drag threshold (internal/ui/drag.go:34), so hold and drag cannot both win. Drag-out with data: when a KindDragSource drag leaves the surface, hand the pointer to the compositor with wl_data_device.start_drag offering text/uri-list built from the held payload, reusing the data-device plumbing that already binds the seat device and manages sources/offers (internal/platform/wayland/selection.go:120-153); drag-in is the mirror - accept an incoming offer whose MIME a shell drop zone accepts and deliver it through the existing drop-zone walk (ui/drag.go:85-105). Per-zone cursors: extend the cursor-shape path (client.go:657 syncCursor; textinput.go:22 cursorShapeFor) from the two baked shapes to a zone-declared name from the pinned cursorshape set. Right/middle are already per-item on the bar (registry.go:1875-1948) and tray (tray.go:546-554); the zone trigger table of REC-uint-03 generalises them.

Approach: internal/shell/panelhost.go press/release handlers (:2471-2520) for hold and drag-out initiation; internal/ui/drag.go for hold/threshold state; internal/platform/wayland/selection.go to emit start_drag and read incoming offers (SetDataOfferHandler/SetSelectionHandler :137-151); internal/platform/wayland/client.go cursor wiring. If the pinned sysc-wayland client does not expose DataDevice.start_drag, the pin bump is the enabling dependency step and the shell wiring above is unchanged. Rung existing with that single dependency caveat: MIME/serial plumbing, drop zones and cursor shapes all ship.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: Drag-out must claim the pointer serial at the press and cancel cleanly when the compositor refuses focus; hold must not fire during scrollbar/content drags; MIME negotiation is the security boundary - offer only text/uri-list built from shell-held payloads, never arbitrary file reads.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-uint-04)
Audit: pass — rung existing; sysc-wayland pin matches go.mod:7 and the pinned module already exposes DataDevice.StartDrag (client.go:2584), so the 'bump only if missing' caveat is already satisfied; core wl_data_device, Niri-first; no estimates. | Hold, compositor drag-out/in and per-zone cursors unowned; adjacent sysc-445 (plugin-scope drag-out need), sysc-1412 (bar bindings), sysc-839 (shortcut inhibit) - none covers it.

title: [pleamar] Declarative conditional keyboard loans and guarded key rules
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-uiux-int-05).

Recommendation: Make the keyboard loan a property of the surface rather than a constant in the host. Today every host picks a fixed mode at spec time (panelhost.go:1885 exclusive, shield :1716 none, traymenuhost.go:21 on-demand, plugin floating surface pluginsurface.go:430) and one host already runs the conditional pattern by hand: the toast reply takes Exclusive while edited, returns None when parked and resumes the parked text (toasthost.go:610-644; toastreply_test.go). Generalise that shape: surface-open params gain a keyboard request with an optional while-condition re-evaluated on the host's event and rebuild path, so a surface can hold the keyboard only while its condition holds and hand it back when it stops. Guarded key rules: after the drawn field keeps a typed key (field-first rule at panelhost.go:2695-2725), check a per-surface table of combo+guard rules before the default key handling; plugin rules declare through the manifest capability vocabulary (internal/plugin/manifest.go:64-98) beside the existing shortcut keys delivered at panelhost.go:2721. Focus parks and restores by StableKey (internal/ui/tree.go:486-494), following the entry-ID restore precedent (traymenuhost.go:792-809).

Approach: internal/shell: a KeyboardRequest struct on panel/aux/plugin surface params, evaluated where the mode is applied today (panelhost.go:1885 is the single application point) with the toast host refactored onto it; a guarded-rule table in the panel key handler beside panelShortcutKey (:2842) and the plugin shortcut delivery (:2721). internal/ui/keys.go KeyInput/Mods already model combos; text editing stays ui.KindTextField's. Rung existing: every ingredient ships, the loan condition and rule table are the additions. No new dependencies.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: A loan that fails to hand back strands the keyboard: the while-condition must be re-evaluated on every event and on focus loss, with None as the fail-safe. Guarded rules must stay below the drawn field or typing breaks (see the focus-eaten-as-shortcut note at panelhost.go:3822-3825).

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-uint-05)
Audit: pass — rung existing; panelhost.go:1885 verified as the single application point; a surface parameter plus data, not a primitive; no dependency; no estimates. | sysc-823 (text input parity) and sysc-591 (key repeat) harden the existing hard-coded host modes; nothing plans declarative conditional loans or guarded key rules.

title: [pleamar] Layer claim slots with spring presence and hot-reload travel
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-uiux-int-08).

Recommendation: Give surface visibility a declarative winner rule. Define, per surface group, an ordered claim list - Always, While(cond), After(signals), FromUntil(from,until) - where the first claim whose condition holds wins and the next shows when it stops; nobody has to turn anything off (pleamar/src/scene.rs:1487-1490). Each claim owns a presence value eased 0..1 by the surface's existing animator channels (animVisible/animTheme, internal/shell/animation.go:60-70; Target :368), so swaps crossfade instead of snapping, and a hot reload retargets the in-flight presence rather than resetting it (animator.Retarget :570 is exactly that operation; first load may settle, as pleamar does, render.rs:2990). First consumers: panel-group visibility (settings rail), the media strip pin and the toast stack - all imperative open/close today. Reduced motion keeps its existing absolute cap (reducedPanelCap, animation.go:21). Claims are computed in the registry rebuild pass and keyed by StableKey so reorders keep the user's place.

Approach: internal/shell: a claim-slot registry beside the panel/aux hosts, evaluated in the same rebuild pass that opens and closes panels (registry.go panel toggles; panelhost configure); presence animated through the per-surface animator and drawn like PanelOpacity (animation.go:604). Hosts adopt by asking the slot for visibility instead of calling open/close directly; start with the panel group and the media strip, then toasts (toasthost.go). Rung existing: animator, hosts and the fade/slide catalogue (internal/ui/transition.go) all ship; the claim arbitration is the new part. No dependencies.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: The winner rule must stay a pure function of state to be hot-reload safe; equal-rank claims need a deterministic tiebreak, and a claim opening a keyboard-holding surface must respect the keyboard rules of REC-uint-05.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-uint-06)
Audit: pass — rung existing; visibility data over existing hosts (animator, hosts, transition catalogue verified); consumers named (panel group, media strip, toasts); no dependency; no estimates. | Claim slots unowned; panel visibility stays imperative host open/close, no bd/register row for claims or presence crossfade.

title: [pleamar] Agent-seat presence UX: monitor glow, self-drawn cursors and a Stop that refuses (conditional)
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-uiux-int-09).

Recommendation: If the owner approves an agent seat (owner decision: the seat and its refusal are compositor-owned, sysc-compositor is docs-only and the plugin capability vocabulary has no seat/input grant - twin GAP-integ-ses-05), build the shell-side presence layer pleamar-wm demos: per-cursor sprites with click rings and names drawn on their own overlay surface, a breathing edge glow with a travelling highlight on the output the agent works on, a breathing outline on the window it targets, and a pill ('An agent is using this monitor') whose Stop is an explicit destructive action (pleamar-wm/examples/session.plm:8400-8465). Stop is compositor-enforced - afterwards mutating verbs answer 'stopped-by-user' (pleamar-wm/src/agent.rs:409-415) - so the shell renders state and must never be the enforcement point. Keep needs-design: the seat, the facts contract and the refusal live outside sysc-shell.

Approach: Shell-side only, once a seat exists: per-output overlay surfaces reuse the aux-surface pattern (selectorSpec screenshot_selector.go:138-150; depthclock.go:277-300 as the per-output pinned-layer precedent); cursor sprites and glow are ordinary ui.Node draws on that overlay; the pill reuses the toast/floating host (toasthost.go:246 spec; pluginsurface.go:426-432 on-demand keyboard pattern); Stop routes like an existing destructive confirm (popout_clipboard.go:298-317). Facts (agent active, name, per-cursor position, target window) arrive as a compositor-published state contract; until that contract exists, implement nothing. title: [pleamar] Gesture player: keyframed gestures with interruption classes and postures
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-uiux-int-03).

Recommendation: Add a gesture player over the existing animator: a named gesture is a keyframe sequence with an interruption class (ambient/posture/reflex/asked/state), a gesture may only cut off one of its class or lower, and an interrupted play hears a rejection instead of being silently dropped (pleamar/src/render.rs:2940-2944). A posture is a gesture re-fired while its condition holds and nothing else runs (:3155). The player leads the target channels during the gesture and, at the end, sets each to the gesture's final value so the base channel takes it home (:3168-3199); the next keyframe starts from where the last ended (:3183); keyframe values are fixed when the gesture starts; reduced motion holds the keyframe furthest from base, still (:4828). First consumers: panel drag-to-move (the onboarding move is the in-tree precedent, panelhost.go:2440-2450) and a drag-to-dismiss for panels; the switcher card swipe follows. Touch is not in the event vocabulary (client.go:34-46 has pointer/key/axis only) and touchpad gestures stay with Niri, so this scopes to pointer-driven shell surfaces.

Approach: New internal/shell/gesture.go: a player with class arbitration and per-node instance state driving animator channels (animation.go:60-70; Target:368, TargetLoop:387, Value:520, Retarget:570) through the per-surface animator; the input path in panelhost.go (:2390-2530 press/release, :2516-2530 drag cancel) feeds it, and the existing interaction struct (animation.go:711-788) carries per-key state. Gestures are declared in first-party config; plugins keep plain pointer events, so no wire change is required in this rec. Rung new-code: the gap-row counter-greps found no gesture engine, and the arbitration rules cannot be had from the animator alone - though all animation machinery is reused. No dependencies.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: new-code · scope: L · impact: M.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: Class arbitration must never strand a gesture in flight - a rejected cut-off must be observable, not silent; a posture that re-fires can starve regular input if its while-condition is not tight. Keep the player first-party until semantics settle rather than exposing it to plugins.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-uint-08)
Audit: pass — new-code justified (no gesture engine in tree; class arbitration not derivable from the animator); consumers named (panel drag-to-move, drag-to-dismiss); pointer-only, touchpad gestures stay Niri's; no estimates. | Gesture player unowned: sysc-1412 covers bar bindings only, no keyframe/interruption-class engine exists; scope correctly excludes touch/touchpad (Niri).

title: [pleamar] Game-controller input read directly from /dev/input/js* (first consumer must be named)
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-uiux-int-07, GAP-integ-svc-05).

Recommendation: Read pads the way pleamar does: open /dev/input/js0..js7 as files, fixed 8-byte kernel events, no library and no helper process (pleamar/src/platform/gamepad.rs:2-20); normalise buttons/axes to one shared name set and fold d-pad-as-axis into buttons (:63-77); one poll loop for arrivals plus one goroutine per pad, publishing state on connect and on every button edge (:86-119). In sysc terms this is stdlib file I/O behind a small input source the shell and plugins can consume. The honest blocker is the consumer: sysc has no scripting layer and no gamepad capability, so the rec is explicitly needs-design and includes a manifest capability plus a named first-party consumer (shell navigation) before the input sink is built. GAP-integ-svc-05 folded into this row; nothing in bd plans it.

Approach: New internal/input/gamepad.go: os.Open plus encoding/binary fixed-size reads in per-pad goroutines, an arrival scan on a ticker, results published as a shell input source beside the Wayland pointer/key stream (client.go:34-46 Event kinds are the shape precedent, but pads are an independent kernel source, not a Wayland seat); expose to plugins as new InputEvent kinds (plugin/v1/message.go:212-224) behind a capability added to the manifest vocabulary (internal/plugin/manifest.go:75 precedent). Device access via /dev/input group membership; no daemon, no dependency. Rung stdlib: the mechanism is os/binary/time only, with no lower rung available and nothing worth pinning. Pins: none.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: stdlib · scope: M · impact: L.
Prerequisites: named first-party consumer (shell navigation) — none exists today.
Risk: Needs-design: without a declared consumer the capability is dead wire. Device permissions and hot-plug races are the second hazard - a pad opened during an arrival scan must not double-register; the owner should name the consumer before implementation.

title: [pleamar] Glass refraction family: card-sized CPU bevel/bend over the sysc-797 backdrop, GPU/EGL only on an owner decision
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-visual-fx-01).

Recommendation: Add a glass material in two explicit stages so the trade-off is on the record. Stage 1 (CPU, wl_shm): sample the captured backdrop through a bevel profile derived from the rounded-rect distance the mask code already computes, bend the sample coordinates by the bevel slope, take three channel samples for a dispersion fringe, draw a fresnel rim that widens toward the light, and displace samples along the existing animator ripple phase for a press ring; a dome magnification scales sample coordinates toward the centre. This is bounded by the surface rectangle and reuses the capture sysc-1417 builds, so it needs no GPU and no CGO. Stage 2 (full-surface and WM-scene glass, crease-free thickness walks, per-sample Cauchy dispersion): only affordable on a GPU path, and sysc's recorded position is that EGL/OpenGL ES is added only for a named failing case - the 2026-09-11 backdrop-blur evidence explicitly keeps wl_shm as the direction because a blurred panel backdrop was found affordable. Stage 2 is therefore an owner decision and this rec must not start it. Compositor-side refraction is not a route either: Niri's blur protocol carries no radius, let alone refraction (docs/niri-blur.md:55), so it would need a separate approved design. Honesty clause: if per-pixel bending cannot be held inside the frame budget at the readback gate, land the rim, the tone and the press motion only and leave bending to the owner decision.

Approach: internal/render: a new glass material applied where the backdrop is composited today (paint.go:218-227, style.Backdrop at style.go:116-119), reusing the rounded-rect distance in roundedCoverage (mask.go:239-249) for the bevel profile, render.Blur (blur.go:17) for the frosted base, and the press ripple already modelled by the animator (internal/shell/animation.go:490-513, ui.RipplePaint tree.go:156, painted at paint.go:1533-1541). Surface knobs travel with the resolved Style like BlurBehind/BlurRadius in theme.Composition (profile.go:483-488). Source pixels come from the sysc-1417 capture path. Rung new-code: no optical code exists in tree (the gap row's greps found no refract/dispersion/bevel/fresnel and no WGSL/GLSL), while the substrate (capture, blur, masks, animator ripple) is reused; the new code is confined to internal/render plus one Style/theme field.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: new-code · scope: L · impact: H.
Prerequisites: sysc-1417.
Risk: The readback cadence is unmeasured (register stop-and-review) and may make live sampling unaffordable; per-pixel bending at panel size may not beat the existing 4.94 ms blur; dispersion at quarter resolution may be invisible; the owner may decline the EGL path, leaving a bounded approximation.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-vis-01)
Audit: pass — cgo:required carries the owner-approval note (EGL stage 2 only; stage 1 wl_shm, nothing lands without the decision); compositor-side refraction rejected rather than assumed; new-code justified; no pins; no estimates. | Glass/refraction unowned; sysc-1417 (capture) is a declared prerequisite. Adjacent: sysc-202 owns the EGL/OpenGL-ES named-failing-case decision that stage 2 requires - route stage 2 through it.

title: [pleamar] Live glass lens: recapture while visible and unmix the shell's own pixels (static half stays sysc-797)
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-visual-fx-02).

Recommendation: Take only the unowned half: sysc-1417 owns the per-open capture and blur kernel, so this rec does not re-specify them. Add (a) a recapture cadence that runs only while a glass surface is visible, captures only the glass boxes plus a frost margin rounded to the render scale, skips a capture whose bytes match the previous one, and recaptures back-to-back while the surface fades in; and (b) the unmix that makes the capture usable as a background - the capture contains the shell's own pixels, so recover the clean background from the captured composite minus the shell's own presented canvas weighted by its alpha (the relationship pleamar states as ours + (1 - our alpha) * background, lens.rs:6). Without unmix, per-pixel refraction has nothing clean to sample. Everything is gated on sysc-1417's unmeasured screencopy readback: if a bounded cadence cannot fit the wl_shm frame (4.94 ms blur / 5.67 ms readback / ~11 ms per open are the recorded numbers), the cadence drops to capture-on-open only and the unmix still applies to that single frame.

Approach: internal/platform/wayland: extend the capture taken at openAux (aux_surface.go:191-200) with a visible-lifetime recapture loop, reusing the capture API at capture.go:21; unmix against the shell's own canvas pixels, which the renderer already owns as ui.Image buffers (canvas.go). Compose with render.Blur (blur.go:17) for the frost margin. Cadence and still-frame detection mirror pleamar's contract (lens.rs:368 CAPTURE_INTERVAL, lens.rs:176-196 byte-sample skip) but must be re-derived against sysc's measured costs. Rung new-code: the capture exists only as a one-shot taken before the surface exists, and the gap row's greps found no recapture path and no unmix anywhere in tree.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: new-code · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: sysc-1417.
Risk: The readback is the tranche's largest unmeasured unknown and a live cadence may exceed the frame budget; the shell keeping an extra full-frame buffer for the unmix has memory cost; without unmix the whole refraction family loses its source.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-vis-02)
Audit: pass — new-code justified (capture is one-shot today; no recapture path or unmix in tree); wl_shm plus the existing wlr-screencopy binding only; no dependency; no estimates. | sysc-1417 (partial) is the static per-open capture only; visible-lifetime recapture and the unmix are unowned, correctly gated on the unmeasured readback.
notes: Fallback, corrected 2026-10-15 (supersedes candidate path (2) in the comments below): if the lens fails, it stays at the static rung. sysc-1212 is WM-as-scene and recorded as excluded; glass D13 is the GPU/EGL gate (sysc-202). No issue owns compositor-side glass or capture exclusion, and it would never help Niri. The corrected lens scope is on sysc-1244.

title: [pleamar] Glass tone materials: smoke/milk transfer and busy-area auto-frost over the sysc-797 capture
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-visual-fx-03).

Recommendation: Add the tone step to the backdrop composite, the cheapest part of the glass family: smoke lowers what is seen through in proportion to its luma (capped), milk lifts it toward white, and frost auto frosts only where the content behind is busy, decided by comparing the sharp capture with the frosted one at a few sample points, so a word behind the glass never fights the word on it while a plain wallpaper stays clear. This is pure per-pixel math over a buffer sysc already takes; the only structural change is that auto-frost needs the pre-blur capture kept beside the blurred one, because render.Blur returns just the reduced image today (blur.go:17). The transfer is selected as a material mode on the surface Style next to Backdrop (style.go:116-119) and exposed through the frosted-path settings that already exist.

Approach: internal/render paint.go:218-227 (the backdrop composited through the body mask) gains the tone transfer before rootFill; blur.go:17/:56 returns or exposes the downsampled sharp copy for the busy check; the existing bar frost-opacity settings are the config seam for the material mode. Rung existing: the capture, the blur, the mask and the style plumbing all ship (dependent on sysc-1417 for the capture itself); only a small per-pixel transfer and one retained buffer are new; no dependency, no CGO.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: S · impact: M.
Prerequisites: sysc-1417.
Risk: Auto-frost needs one extra retained buffer and a small change to the blur API, so it must be coordinated with the sysc-1417 kernel work; a wrongly tuned smoke cap hurts legibility more than no tone at all, so the cap needs a visual gate.

title: [pleamar] Bounded emitters inside the host-owned effect layer, weather as the named first consumer
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-visual-fx-05).

Recommendation: Do not add a general particle toolkit. Extend the approved host-owned effect layer (2026-09-16 effect-rendering design: a procedural programme, no shader code, no independent render loops) with a bounded emitter descriptor and a deterministic per-particle raster: each particle is a function of index and phase with no stored state, budgets fixed like the existing precipitation counts (weather_precip.go:10-16), with colours, gravity, speed, spread and direction as descriptor fields. The weather programme is the named first consumer: re-express its precipitation as an emitter so the primitive ships with a real user; no second consumer exists today, so no plugin-facing vocabulary is added - the negotiated declarative capability the effect-rendering design reserves stays closed until the owner opens it.

Approach: internal/render/effect.go:20-48 (the closed host catalogue dispatch) plus a new emitter raster beside weather_precip.go; internal/ui/effect.go:11-14 keeps the programme catalogue and its validation (:49-55) rejecting anything that is not a host programme; frame liveness through the existing animator (internal/shell/animation.go:631 animateSurface, :543 SettledExceptEffects) so an idle emitter does not request frames. Rung existing: the effect layer, its clipping to card shapes and its frame scheduling ship (the weather programme is the proof); the emitter descriptor and raster are new code inside that layer, and no dependency is added.

title: [pleamar] Group compositing effects on the offscreen subtree pass sysc already pays for
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-visual-fx-06).

Recommendation: Extend the one subtree-offscreen pass sysc already runs for a node's opacity (paintNodeOpacity, paint.go:322-355) into a small post-effect chain evaluated on the offscreen buffer before it is composited: group blur (render.Blur), glow (blurred alpha drawn under the content), tone (saturation/brightness/contrast/hue on straight colour), coverage masks (RoundedMask/RingMask plus the radial form of REC-vis-11), and add/screen/multiply modes (extend the blend helpers). Expose them as optional fields on the group kinds that already exist (KindStack/KindColumn) with roles resolved through the theme; do not add a toolkit kind. First consumers: floating cards and popouts, and the attach junction. Bound the cost: render only card-sized subtrees in the damaged region, on the bounded, size-keyed scratch REC-perf-03 owns - the chain runs on that existing offscreen pass (paintNodeOpacity) rather than re-specifying the allocation, so the two recs change one buffer, not two. Prerequisite: REC-perf-03 (its pool replaces today's canvas-sized allocation).

Approach: paint.go:322-355 is the seam; blur.go:17, mask.go:119/158, canvas.go:489/494 and gradient.go:102 are the existing effects to chain; ui/tree.go:58-64 gives the group kinds; theme files resolve the effect roles. Rung existing: the offscreen pass, the blur, the masks and the blend helpers all ship; only the chain and its fields are new; no dependency.

title: [pleamar] Smooth-min melding at the attach junction, reusing the existing rounded-rect distance
description:

Recommendation: Do not build a distance-field scene pipeline. sysc already maps a rounded-rect distance to alpha coverage (roundedCoverage, mask.go:239-249); add a meld coverage that combines two rectangles' distances with a polynomial smooth-min (radius k as the blend amount, as pleamar's blend: does) and reuse the existing coverage-to-mask path. title: [pleamar] SVG as geometry: per-layer contours into the existing mask pipeline, on the already-pinned pure-Go stack
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-visual-sys-01).

Recommendation: Read SVG paths as geometry instead of stamping the document: parse into per-layer contour sets with the pure-Go stack already pinned in go.mod (github.com/srwiley/oksvg for path data and github.com/srwiley/rasterx for fill/stroke geometry, both used by the icon resolver at worker.go:19-20), rasterise coverage with the renderer's existing contour rasteriser (sparkline.go:175 rasterize, backed by golang.org/x/image/vector, also used at text.go:315) and paint through blendMask so paths take the same fills, gradients and masks as everything else. title: [pleamar] Text gradient, outline and shadow painted through the existing run mask
description:

title: [pleamar] Per-letter reveals from the retained shaped run, not a per-glyph raster cache
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-visual-sys-03).

Recommendation: Build per-letter motion on what the text renderer already retains: shaped runs are cached immutably (text.go:99-103) and a run rasterises to one Mask (text.go:57-69 and :289). title: [pleamar] Per-element rim, light direction and shadow numbers, with the cut-shadow diagnosis
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-visual-sys-04).

Recommendation: Promote the surface-level finish to element level. Today Rim is one token stroked on floating panels (style.go:87-90, paint.go:225-227) and shadow is one of three elevation alphas from a cached pre-blurred texture (ShadowTexture, mask.go:251-280; DrawShadow, canvas.go:493-497). Add optional per-element rim width/alpha and a light direction, plus shadow dx/dy/blur/alpha numbers rendered through the existing cached shadow path or a per-node blurred-alpha shadow; when a shadow's spread is clipped by the surface edge, report it naming the sides and the missing pixels, the diagnosis pleamar's renderer performs. The named consumers are already filed: sysc-587 (bar rim/shadow parity) and sysc-192 (launcher shadow instead of a drawn rim).

Approach: internal/ui node fields (ui.Node carries no Rim/Shadow/Light/Glass today), internal/render style.go:87-123 and paint.go:213-229 for the rim, mask.go:251-280 and canvas.go:493-497 for shadows, plus a diagnostic when the shadow box exceeds the surface bounds. Rung existing: the rim stroke, the cached shadow texture and the mask pipeline ship; only the per-element numbers, the light plumb and the diagnosis are new; no dependency.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: Per-element shadows can multiply composite work (keep the texture cache keyed by spread and strength); a light direction that disagrees with the compositor's backdrop looks wrong, so start pointer-relative; the diagnosis needs a non-spamming report channel.

title: [pleamar] Radial gradient: one more axis in the existing gradient sampler
description:

title: [pleamar] A material axis as a live, animatable theme value
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-visual-sys-06).

Recommendation: Thread one material scalar (glassiness, 0..1) through the composition that already carries BlurBehind/BlurRadius (profile.go:464-489) into the resolved surface Style, so every surface reads the same live value, and render it through the material function of REC-vis-03 (and later REC-vis-01) so a skin switch changes the material, not just opacity. title: [pleamar] Agent seat with compositor-enforced Stop (cua-inject model, Go-native) — owner decision for sysc-compositor
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-integ-ses-05).

Recommendation: Conditional on the owner pursuing computer-use agents: put the agent seat in sysc-compositor, not the shell — compositor-created seats for injected input, a 0600 same-user runtime socket verified by peer credentials, per-window targets, a compositor-enforced Stop that makes every mutating verb answer stopped-by-user, and agent presence facts on the IPC stream so the shell can draw an indicator. sysc-shell binds one wl_seat as a client and sysc-main AGENTS.md:9 keeps a lock screen and compositor out of the shell; sysc-lock (peer-verified same-user registration, sysc-lock README:105-108) is the family precedent for the privileged socket. If the owner declines, record a deliberate parity exclusion; shell-side approval/presence UX (GAP-uiux-int-09, D5a) is not assumed here.

Approach: sysc-compositor (docs-only today, sysc-compositor README:5) folds this into its design and milestones: extend the M0 seat work (sysc-compositor m0 spec:147,177 creates one seat plus cursor) into a seat table in internal/server with per-seat input routing, attach the planned virtual-keyboard/virtual-pointer globals (sysc-compositor design:307) per seat, and add a session-local control socket (0600 under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, SO_PEERCRED real-UID check — model on sysc-lock internal/lockd/client.go patterns) speaking a cua-inject-v1-style verb set; track windows the agent opened in internal/wm for pid:N / root:N / app-id targets; publish agent.active and agent.N.* facts on the niri-ipc event stream (internal/ipc; niri-ipc 26.4.0 pin) and enforce Stop in the compositor. The shell consumes published facts only.

Target repo: sysc-compositor · rung: new-code · scope: L · impact: H.
Prerequisites: REC-int-04.
Risk: Design commitment, not code: the repo has no code yet, so this lands as design-doc text plus milestones. A second non-user seat and an injection socket touch niri's security model (sysc-compositor design:316); the socket must never become an unlock path, and Stop semantics must be enforced where input is routed, not in the shell. The shell-side presence piece stays blocked until facts exist and D5a defines the UX.

title: [pleamar] Network fallback tier: iwd backend plus a stdlib kernel read-only tier behind the existing backend seam
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-integ-svc-01).

Recommendation: On iwd-only or wpa_supplicant-only machines the network glyph and panel are dead: NewSystemNetwork installs an inert unavailableBackend when NetworkManager is unreachable (sysc-shell/internal/services/network.go:288-319). Populate the backend seam (network.go:72-90) with two tiers, mirroring pleamar's NM then iwd then kernel order (pleamar/src/platform/mod.rs:123-125): an iwd backend on the system bus, and a kernel read-only tier that reports at least interface/kind/connected. Revise the 'we are building neither' note (network.go:75-78) instead of leaving it contradicting the code; the kernel tier contradicts nothing — it is a read-only fallback, not a swappable writable backend — while the iwd half needs the owner to accept a second writable backend.

Approach: sysc-shell/internal/services: a new iwd backend implementing the existing backend interface (networkbackend.go:9-26 is the model; State/AccessPoints/Scan/SetWirelessEnabled/Activate/Forget/Watch) against iwd's D-Bus service (net.connman.iwd) over the already-pinned github.com/godbus/dbus/v5 v5.2.2 (go.mod:20), reporting the same NetworkState/AccessPoint shapes so sysc-shell/internal/shell/panelhost.go:1481 and sysc-shell/internal/shell/registry.go:877 need no change; select it in NewSystemNetwork (network.go:288-302) when NM is unreachable; passphrases stay behind the existing secret slot (network.go:110-118), answered via iwd's agent. Kernel tier: a read-only backend reading /proc/net/wireless and /sys/class/net/*/{operstate,wireless,address} with the stdlib only (no netlink, no iw exec), replacing unavailableBackend's ConnUnknown (network.go:304-319) for state display while scan/connect keep refusing. Available() (network.go:137-141) turns true when any tier is live.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: system-service · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: iwd and NM differ in scan/connect semantics; keep one decode path (the service re-reads on Watch wakes as today, networkbackend.go:209-231). A second writable backend is a real maintenance line the note warns about, so land the read-only tier first as the zero-policy floor and the iwd backend only on owner acceptance.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-int-02)
Audit: pass — system-service rung matches the iwd native service with a stdlib kernel tier; godbus v5.2.2 (go.mod:20) and Wifx/gonetworkmanager v2.2.0 (go.mod:51) are existing pins; the iwd half is owner-gated in notes; no estimates. | bd network items (sysc-254/268/503/769, sysc-1390) are NetworkManager-panel fixes; no alternate backend or kernel read-only tier is planned or registered.

title: [pleamar] Sound-output subsystem (mixer + lazy stream + decoders) so earcons and component playback can be revisited
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-integ-svc-03).

Recommendation: Re-open the deliberate earcon rejection with its own reason answered. The register recorded 'Rejected: earcons (no audio subsystem)' (sysc-shell/docs/plans/README.md:587), so the blocker was the missing subsystem, not the cue; this recommendation builds the subsystem first and keeps earcons as its first consumer. What is new: pleamar/src/platform/sound.rs shows the whole playback path is bounded — one mixer thread, one stream opened lazily and closed after ~4 s of silence, WAV/Vorbis decoders, tone synthesis, 48 voices at ~40 ms; and a pure-Go PulseAudio-protocol client now exists (jfreymuth/pulse, no CGO), so the Go-only rule holds. If the owner still declines, the register entry stands and nothing proceeds.

Approach: sysc-shell/internal/services: add the output side beside the existing control plane (audio.go:49 wpctl default sink; audioenum.go:25,82 pw-dump node parsing), leaving control-plane code untouched. One mixer goroutine owns a lazily-opened stream to the PulseAudio-protocol endpoint pipewire-pulse provides (pleamar/src/platform/sound.rs:105-113, :288-300, :25 is the model); decode WAV 8/16/24/32-bit PCM with stdlib encoding/binary, Vorbis via pinned github.com/jfreymuth/oggvorbis v1.0.5, synthesise tones in Go; playback through pinned github.com/jfreymuth/pulse v0.1.3. Expose a small Go API (play/stop/volume, bounded voices) and wire the first consumer — OSD/notification earcons — through the existing UI event paths; the plugin wire call/capability is a later step so the one-repository rule holds until a second real consumer (sysc-notify, which cannot ring today) is actually served.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: dependency · scope: L · impact: M.
Prerequisites: owner re-decision of the docs/plans/README.md:587 rejection.
Risk: Assumes a PulseAudio-protocol endpoint (pipewire-pulse) as pleamar does; if absent, stay silent rather than fail the shell. Playback must run off the owner goroutine and stay bounded (voices, latency); volume should reflect the sink state the control plane already reads rather than inventing a second mixer authority.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-int-03)
Audit: pass — dependency rung with both new pins versioned and reasoned; jfreymuth/pulse v0.1.3 and jfreymuth/oggvorbis v1.0.5 resolve on the Go module proxy and pulse is documented pure Go/no CGO (README verified); reopens the register :587 owner decision explicitly; no estimates. | The register rejection ('no audio subsystem', :587) stands; rec correctly re-opens it as an owner decision with a pure-Go client, no CGO.

title: [pleamar] Multi-seat input model with injected seats isolated from clipboard focus and cursor
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-integ-ses-03).

Recommendation: Conditional on remote or agent input being pursued (REC-int-06, REC-int-01): sysc-compositor should grow its seat model beyond M0's single seat plus cursor, with pleamar-wm's isolation rules — a keyboard on an injected seat must never move the user's data-device/primary-selection focus, and an injected seat must never set the drawn cursor. sysc-shell cannot act here: it binds exactly one wl_seat as a client (sysc-shell/internal/platform/wayland/client.go:423, registry.go:52) and seats are compositor-owned today (Niri) and in the plan; if the answer is no, the isolation question disappears with it, so the seat model is only worth designing together with a consumer.

Approach: sysc-compositor: extend the M0 seat/cursor work (sysc-compositor m0 spec:147,177; design:87 requires wl_seat) into a seat table in internal/server with input devices assigned per seat, and attach the planned virtual-keyboard/virtual-pointer globals (sysc-compositor design:307) to a chosen seat rather than implicitly to the user seat; in internal/wm implement the focus asymmetry pleamar-wm uses (pleamar-wm/src/nest.rs:3354-3363 focus_changed early-return, :3367-3371 cursor_image ignored; agent.rs:1711-1714 is_agent_seat gates), and have the compositor publish per-seat presence on the niri-ipc event stream. sysc-lock's one-graphical-session-per-UID verification (sysc-lock README:105-108) is the precedent that an injected seat must not become a second session authority.

Target repo: sysc-compositor · rung: new-code · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: The isolation rules are security-critical and easy to lose in a wlroots port; virtual-keyboard/virtual-pointer are not per-seat isolation by themselves, so the design must state seat attachment explicitly. No shell-side work to promise.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-int-04)
Audit: pass — compositor-targeted with lock_or_compositor owner-decision; cgo per the compositor charter noted; stays a design commitment until an injection consumer is approved (one-repo rule honoured); no estimates. | Seat isolation unowned; consumer-dependent as declared (REC-int-01/REC-int-06). sysc-lock precedent cited correctly.
notes: Transferred 2026-10-15 to https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-compositor/issues/2. Design: docs/plans/2026-10-15-tier3-session-domain-design.md (D2). Commit 746afa6's TestSeatTable proves three distinct wl_seat objects, independent capabilities, and isolation when clearing the other seats. It does not test virtual-device attachment: attach_to_named_seat, forced_to_seat0, and unsupported remain untested. M0 still has one production seat, so the gh#263 seat table has not landed and the P3.1 probe-removal condition remains future. Pointer routing remains compositor code; virtual-device creation also needs protocol XML not shipped by wlroots. Build this only after an owner-approved consumer.

title: Pleamar-inspired capabilities beyond Niri parity
description: Owner direction 2026-10-19: sysc-compositor should retain Niri's product, IPC, and config shape while supporting selected capabilities demonstrated by Pleamar and pleamar-wm, implemented with Go+cgo. title: [pleamar] Browser remote session as a session/compositor decision (owner decision)
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-integ-ses-04).

Recommendation: Conditional on the owner wanting browser remote access: the compliant vehicle is the session/compositor, not the shell — input injection and capture are session-level security decisions, and sysc has only local capture paths today. sysc-compositor already plans the capture side (screencopy plus ext-image-copy-capture, design:298-299; Mutter ScreenCast/PipeWire at M12, design:327, :335) and the injection globals (virtual-keyboard/virtual-pointer, design:307); a remote feature would add a session-side transport (loopback page, TLS delegated to an external front as pleamar does) with input routed as virtual input or uinput devices on the user seat, an auth model with a second factor, and a desk indicator only if the compositor publishes presence facts. If declined, record the parity exclusion.

Approach: sysc-compositor: fold a session-side remote plan into the design/milestones on top of what is already planned — capture via zwlr_screencopy/ext-image-copy-capture (design:298-299) and Mutter ScreenCast/PipeWire (design:327, :335, M12), injection via the virtual-keyboard/virtual-pointer globals attached to a chosen seat (design:307) or uinput devices on the user seat (pleamar-wm/src/remote.rs:2019-2035 is the model), a loopback page with password plus single-use code and hashed sessions (pleamar-wm/src/remote.rs:29-37, :136-206, :247-250), and a desk indicator fed by compositor-published facts (pleamar-wm session.plm:8363-8399 is the shape). sysc-lock's real-UID and peer verification (sysc-lock README:105-108) is the family precedent for the privileged surface; the shell keeps its local capture paths (screenshot capability, screen-recorder plugin) and gains nothing until facts exist.

Target repo: sysc-compositor · rung: new-code · scope: L · impact: M.
Prerequisites: REC-int-04.
Risk: Security-sensitive: capture plus remote input need the owner's security model before any code, and the compositor's exact-sized SHM-pool rule for screencopy consumers must be honored (design:298). Streaming and codec choices stay session-side; do not pull a web stack into sysc-shell.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-int-06)
Audit: pass — compositor-targeted with owner-decision; capture and injection stay out of the shell (AGENTS.md:9); cgo per charter noted; no shell work promised; no estimates. | Remote unowned; the compositor design owns only the capture/injection plumbing it would build on. Distinct from REC-usurf-03 (shell-side chooser).

Needs the owner's security model before any code; it has the M12 capture work (screencopy, ext-image-copy-capture, PipeWire-ScreenCast-shaped) to attach to once that exists. Nothing in sysc-shell gains from it -- the shell keeps its local capture paths unchanged. Not closing.

title: [pleamar] Component-facing file-watch service (files.watch) on the existing jailed file browser and plugin wire
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-integ-svc-04).

Recommendation: Give components and plugins a way to react to a file changing on disk instead of polling in their own code: add a files.watch host call to the plugin wire and a host-side watcher registry, reusing the jailed path resolution the file browser already enforces (sysc-shell/internal/files/contain.go:20-77) and the existing files capability gate (hostcall.go:229-233). sysc-85 (launcher fsnotify rescan) and sysc-754 (plugin-directory hot reload) are adjacent consumers of the same mechanism, not this service's scope — this is the generic component-facing half neither owns, and the per-plugin KV store already covers the persistence half (state.go:22,53).

Approach: sysc-shell: extend the plugin wire with CallFilesWatch beside CallFilesBrowse (sysc-shell/plugin/v1/message.go:279; hostcall.go:229-233 gate) plus a host-push message, following the SettingsChanged precedent (plugin/v1/message.go:246-253); a watcher registry in internal/files or internal/services watches with inotify through the already-pinned golang.org/x/sys v0.47.0 (go.mod:11; same mechanism as brightness.go:788) and falls back to a 250 ms os.Stat mtime poll exactly as pleamar's files.rs:133-151 does, coalescing per path and bounding watch counts per component. The component's own namespace (StateRoot, state.go:53) is the natural root; watches are torn down with the component.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: stdlib · scope: M · impact: L.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: Watch storms: coalesce and debounce per path, cap watches per component, and never follow a symlink out of the jail (ContainEntry semantics, contain.go:15-35). Delivery must not block the owner goroutine; if a component is torn down with watches open, the registry must close them without leaking inotify descriptors.

Audit: pass — stdlib rung matches the poll-floor plus inotify approach; x/sys pin is existing (go.mod:11); watch roots stay jail-checked (contain.go verified); no new dependency; no estimates. | sysc-85 and sysc-754 are declared adjacent consumers, not owners of a component-facing service. O5 boundary: one shared debounced inotify helper with REC-core-02.

title: [pleamar] describe: an askable element tree over the existing IPC socket
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-dx-plug-01).

Recommendation: sysc is developed by coding agents yet ships no agent-facing product API; the read half is one verb. Add `describe` to internal/ipc returning the named contents of every open surface - per node: name, role, kind, text or value (redacted where masked), selected/disabled state, owning surface and output. It reads only the retained trees the shell already builds and validates (ui.Node Name/Role/Action; plugin views are validated to carry an accessible identity), so there is no new UI primitive, no dispatch and no coordinate guessing. This is what lets an agent drive sysc without screenshots, and it is the prerequisite for act-by-name, wait/watch and the per-node automation opt-out.

Approach: internal/ipc/server.go: add a Describe hook to Handlers (:58) and a namespaced `describe` method beside `status` (:266), reusing the one-line request/reply and Call (:423) that sysc-1411 plans to keep while versioning the envelope. Shell side: a new internal/shell/describe.go walking the open panel trees (Registry.panelHosts, registry.go:157), the bars (Registry.bars, registry.go:57), the OSD (osd.go, osdview.go) and plugin views published into the host records (pluginhost.go:863), in the existing traversal order ui.Focusables (internal/ui/focus.go:4); every focusable already carries Name, Role and Action (internal/ui/tree.go:450, :465-472) with StateDisabled (:504), and plugin nodes must carry name and role (plugin/v1/node.go:334-338, :564) after Convert copies the wire tree (internal/plugin/view.go:25). Values come from ui.Node.Text plus the selection/state bits; masked inputs (plugin/v1/node.go:351-354) answer as hidden. Snapshot under the registry lock and marshal off the Wayland owner, the way Status does (registry.go:1116). No dependency, no new primitive. Consumers: agent tooling, test harnesses, user scripts.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: H.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: describe is a disclosure surface: anything reachable in a tree becomes machine-readable, so masked inputs and lock or session surfaces must be denied by construction, not by omission. Walking every host must not touch Wayland-owned state from the IPC goroutine or it becomes a frame-time hazard. There is one listener today (server.go:110) and the counter-greps warn against growing a second control surface: extend the existing protocol, do not add a socket.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-dplug-01)
Audit: pass — read-only walk over trees the shell already builds, consumers named (agent tooling, tests, scripts); no new socket (one listener kept); lock/session surfaces excluded by construction; no dependency; no estimates. | sysc-1411 (partial) is envelope/versioning only; the askable tree is unowned (sysc-752/759 adjacent). O1 canonical for node-level describe; REC-dtool-02 is revised to compose with it.

title: [pleamar] act-by-name: press, type and submit through the shell's own node path, with refusals
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-dx-plug-02).

Recommendation: Add `act` beside `describe`: a named target plus an event (press, type, submit, focus) resolved to a node in the described tree and dispatched through the path a pointer or key press takes, so focus movement, springs, plugin input events and the shell's own handlers behave exactly as for a hand. Refuse with a reason instead of a silent no-op: disabled node, unknown name, target not offered to automation. sysc already addresses input by node inside the plugin boundary (plugin/v1/message.go:209-217) and already has one dispatch per surface; only the external by-name channel is missing, and together with describe it forms the agent-facing product API the project lacks today.

Approach: internal/ipc/server.go: an Act hook beside Describe (REC-dplug-01). Shell side: resolve the name within the surface that owns it, move focus with the existing helper (PanelHost.setFocus, panelhost.go:4301) and call the same activation path a click uses - PanelHost.activate (panelhost.go:3389), which already refuses StateDisabled nodes (:3391) and fans out to the per-surface handlers (handlePluginManager :3456, handlePalettes :3459, the walls and plugin-action cases at :3403-3418). ui.Hit (internal/ui/layout.go:795) stays the pointer path, not the act path. Plugin nodes: reuse r.handlePluginBar (pluginhost.go:1663) and r.deliverPluginText (:1689) so the plugin receives its normal node-addressed input.event with revision (plugin/v1/message.go:212-216); submit commits the host-owned text buffer the way the submit key does. One-shot request/reply over the existing protocol; errors are replies, not dropped lines.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: H.
Prerequisites: REC-dplug-01.
Risk: An act channel carries the authority of a person's hand: it must honour the same modal shield, the same confirmations for destructive controls (session, power, delete) and the same disabled states, or it becomes a way around dialogs; pleamar's `covered by` refusal has no sysc equivalent yet. Name resolution needs a stable key - ui.Node.Action is already documented as unique within its owning surface (internal/ui/tree.go:486-494), which suggests keying on Action plus Name/Role, with ambiguity answered as an error rather than a first match.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-dplug-02)
Audit: pass — reuses the shell's own activation path (panelhost.go:3389/4301 verified) and plugin input delivery; refusals instead of silent no-ops; needs-design flagged; no dependency; no estimates. | Act-by-name unowned; sysc-752 (CLI-to-plugin route) adjacent, sysc-759 adds unrelated bar IPC. O1 canonical for act; the focus verb belongs to REC-dtool-02.

title: [pleamar] Approval-gated desktop assistant: owner decision first; the Luau/Node worker blocks a straight port
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-dx-plug-11).

Recommendation: Do not implement yet - put the decision to the owner. marea's gate (the model PROPOSES; the shell decides the final step and says what happened; final actions become an approval card) is architecture worth copying, but the worker is a Node/Pi SDK process and the gate logic is Luau (marea chat.luau, agent/worker.mjs). The constraint sheet forbids Lua/Luau in sysc and the shell cannot host that worker, so the blocking constraint is the worker/runtime, not the approval UX. This rec owns the owner decision, the proposal protocol and the blocked-worker question; the approval card's UX belongs to REC-uint-02 (GAP-uiux-int-10) and seat presence stays REC-uint-07's. The owner decision is: (a) does sysc want an on-desktop assistant at all, and if yes (b) may the model worker be a third-party supervised plugin process, with the shell providing only the proposal protocol? Until that is answered there is nothing to build; a no closes the gap as parity-excluded.

Approach: Nothing exists to reuse for a runtime (no assistant, model or prompt path in the tree; the only `assistant` hit is an icon comment at internal/render/iconfont.go:115). If the owner says yes, the shell-side gate is Go and reuses existing mechanisms: a proposal message pair shaped like HostCall/HostReply (plugin/v1/message.go:284-302) rather than a new socket; an approval handoff to REC-uint-02's card (its nearest gated-action precedent is the polkit prompt, internal/shell/polkit.go; polkitHost.activateActionLocked :596), with this rec providing only the proposal/decision payload; and the worker, if allowed, as a supervised plugin process (internal/plugin/supervisor.go:160) so its confinement questions land in REC-dplug-09, whose boundary work would be a prerequisite for anything with side effects. Credentials and the model runtime are the owner's call; no UI primitive is added for a component that does not exist.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: new-code · scope: L · impact: H.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: Owner-decision gated on the worker question; until it is answered any shell-side build is a surface with no gate behind it. Even if approved, an assistant that executes needs REC-dplug-09's boundary and an explicit list of `final` actions, or the shell ships an agent with more authority than the plugin model allows. Subsystem bar: sysc has rejected features for lacking a subsystem (earcons), so an assistant needs a stated owner, credentials story and stop semantics before code.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-dplug-03)
Audit: revise — no code proposed; the non-Go worker question is escalated as an owner decision (Go-only blocks a first-party Luau/Node gate); rung new-code justified as nothing exists to reuse; no estimates. | O7: name REC-uint-02 as the approval card's owner (drop the second card spec); keep the owner decision, the proposal protocol and the blocked-worker question here. Presence UX stays REC-uint-07's.
notes: STAYS IN sysc-shell (not transferred). Design: docs/plans/2026-10-15-tier3-agent-experience-design.md D1-D2. Deliverable is an owner decision, not code: A no assistant; A2 expose Tier 1 to an external harness (cheap only after Tier 1 ships incl. the sysc-1411 contract gate; produces no proposals, so it does NOT unblock sysc-1188 - corrected 2026-10-15 by the ownership audit); B third-party supervised worker (needs sysc-1223 containment, an explicit final-actions list and a proven denial of the niri and shell IPC sockets to the worker); C first-party Go runtime in the shell (not recommended); D worker inside the shell (excluded by AGENTS.md:6). Owner leans B (2026-10-15). Not closing.

title: [pleamar] wait/watch: conditions on the live shell over the sysc-741 subscription envelope
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-dx-plug-03).

Recommendation: Take sysc-1411's planned named subscriptions and split event stream as the transport and add the missing condition layer: `wait EXPR [TIMEOUT]` answers as soon as a condition over the described names holds, or reports it late at the deadline, and `watch [SECONDS]` streams the things that happen. This is the difference between an agent that polls screenshots and one that is woken. The vocabulary stays deliberately tiny (surface open, node present, value equals, node enabled) and is validated against names that exist, so it cannot creep into a query language.

Approach: internal/ipc/server.go: a Wait/Attach handler pair (Handlers, :58) speaking the shape sysc-1411 defines for named subscriptions rather than a second push path - today there is one listener (:110) and strictly one reply per request (Call :423). Evaluator: a new small internal/shell file holding parsed conditions and checking them against the same snapshot describe serves (the describe walk of REC-dplug-01 plus registry.Status, registry.go:1116) driven by the registry's existing invalidation signal (registry.Invalidations, wired at cmd/sysc-shell/main.go:424) rather than a poll loop; the parser refuses unknown names and suggests the closest. Timeouts with a capped maximum answer as a late result, never a hung request; watch emits lines and ends at its window. Tests: table tests for the parser plus one end-to-end check using the reference helper plugin (internal/plugin/helper.go) to change a value under a live wait.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: S · impact: M.
Prerequisites: sysc-1411, REC-dplug-01.
Risk: Transport ownership is the whole risk: inventing a private push mechanism would duplicate sysc-1411 and grow the second control surface the counter-greps warn against, so wait/watch must be a client of that envelope. An open-ended predicate over plugin values needs agreement on which node values are public (REC-dplug-05) or watch becomes an exfiltration channel; timeouts must be capped so a client cannot pin shell resources.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-dplug-04)
Audit: pass — condition layer only, transport stays sysc-1411; deliberately tiny vocabulary with anti-creep validation; no dependency; no estimates. | sysc-1411 (partial) owns subscriptions/split-stream; the condition-expression and wait-semantics layer is unowned, as declared.

title: [pleamar] Declared per-node automation visibility (`agent: yes|no|hidden`) with hidden values
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-dx-plug-04).

Recommendation: Give every node an explicit automation visibility: an optional property on the plugin wire and on the shell's own ui.Node, with hidden nodes omitted from describe entirely, masked and person-only values reported as hidden, and act refusing a no node with a human-readable reason that names the party. It is the policy half of the describe/act pair and should ship with it, not after: without it every node a surface adds is silently exposed to whatever drives the shell.

Approach: internal/ui/tree.go: add the property beside the accessible identity (Name/Role, :465-472), zero value meaning the design's default. plugin/v1/node.go: an optional field on the wire Node with validation in Validate (:432) and a protocol minor bump (Version/HostHello, message.go:50-56, :100-109). Note the decoder is strict (framing.go:203 DisallowUnknownFields), so the addition is negotiated, not a spare key: the host advertises supported versions in the handshake and a plugin library that sees an older host omits the field. internal/plugin/view.go Convert (:25) copies it into the shell-owned tree like every other wire field; describe (REC-dplug-01) filters hidden nodes and redacts masked ones (Masked, plugin/v1/node.go:351-354); act (REC-dplug-02) refuses using the refusal shape of the host-call gate (hostcall.go:161-162). First-party surfaces mark lock and polkit trees as never described by construction; recommended defaults: first-party yes, plugin nodes no until the manifest declares otherwise.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: REC-dplug-01, REC-dplug-02.
Risk: The default is a real design decision: a permissive default reproduces pleamar's choice but exposes every new node until someone marks it; a strict default makes plugin nodes opt in and can make describe look empty at first. A wire field is a protocol change, so old hosts reject it unless the handshake negotiation ships with it. Masked inputs must be redacted regardless of the flag, and the design must say what happens for values that are not user data (metrics, weather rendering).

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-dplug-05)
Audit: pass — gates an existing tree walk rather than adding a primitive; the wire field rides the version handshake (strict decoder noted); prerequisites describe/act; no dependency; no estimates. | No automation-visibility concept in tree, bd or register; downstream of REC-dplug-01/02 as declared. Wire addition rides the strict-decode handshake, correctly.
