title: [pleamar] Version-matched agent skill and in-binary docs: `sysc-shell skill install`, `sysc-shell docs TOPIC`
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-dx-plug-05).

Recommendation: Ship the shell's own guidance with the shell: a skill bundle embedded in the binary (go:embed) that `sysc-shell skill install` writes into the skill folders Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode read, plus `sysc-shell docs TOPIC` printing the same version's reference, and one installer line that calls it. The refresh rule is pleamar's: mark what we wrote, rewrite only when the embedded version differs, never touch a skill we did not write. This is the second half of the agent-facing story - sysc is built by coding agents, so an agent arriving on a sysc machine should find version-matched instructions for the shell and for authoring plugins - and it folds GAP-dx-dist-04 (installer/refresh) here.

Approach: New in-repo package internal/skill (place, install, refresh) over go:embed, which the tree already uses (emoji.tsv, theme templates, the i18n catalog, fonts): no dependency. Content under a committed skill/ directory (SKILL.md for shell usage, one for plugin authoring from plugin/v1, manifest.json and the store) plus the existing product docs (README.md, docs/development.md, docs/ecosystem.md). CLI: extend the subcommand switch that today handles only `ipc` (cmd/sysc-shell/main.go:446) with `skill` and `docs`; both are client-side and need no running shell. Installer: the sysc installer repo calls `sysc-shell skill install` after install - the cross-repo half of GAP-dx-dist-04, one line, no new component. Sequencing: v1 documents config and plugin authoring plus the verbs that exist; the agent-driving sections are added when REC-dplug-01/02 ship, and the version mark keeps the text honest.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: stdlib · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: It writes into other tools' directories: copy-only-if-ours plus a version/fingerprint comparison is what keeps it safe, and missing directories must be tolerated. Text that documents verbs the running binary lacks is worse than no skill, so the bundle is version-marked with the binary and the draft covers only shipped surface; plugin-authoring text must track plugin/v1 changes or it becomes wrong advice.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-dplug-06)
Audit: pass — stdlib substrate (go:embed) in one repository with two named consumers (agents, installer); no new component or repo; no dependency; no estimates. | No skill bundle or embedded-docs path anywhere; adjacent docs work only (sysc-498 plugin-pattern doc, sysc-849 plugin READMEs, sysc-1356 onboarding wizard) - none covers it. O9 boundary with REC-dtool-04/06.

title: [pleamar] Consent keyed to the plugin's content digest, not only to the catalog release
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-dx-plug-08).

Recommendation: Record a digest of the installed plugin with its consent and require it to match: change the entry point, the manifest or the declared asks and the previous approval no longer holds, so the plugin starts with no capabilities and the manager re-asks, saying what changed. Today the pinned identity is the catalog release (version plus linux-arch asset SHA-256, re-checked when the operation runs) and hand-placed plugins have no consent step at all, so a same-asks rebuild installs silently. pleamar's rule - approval is keyed to the plugin's own bytes and its asks - is the model.

Approach: internal/plugin/store: the installed Record already carries source, version, sha256, capabilities and requires (store/installed.go:23-37) - add a content digest computed over the installed directory (manifest.json plus the resolved entry point and declared assets, excluding the plugin's own state root) using crypto/sha256 from the stdlib, the primitive the catalog path already uses (store.go:334-341). Enforcement: the set-wise consent comparison (store.go:306, checkConsent :346) extends to the digest, and the host-call gate stays the runtime enforcer (hostcall.go:62); a mismatch grants no capabilities until re-approval. Discovery: user-root plugins (discovery.go:47-54) get the same record and digest on first enable, which also gives them the consent step they currently lack. UI: the manager's NeedsConsent (pluginstore_model.go:313-317) and ConsentLines (:339-347) gain the digest and a changed-since-approval reason, reusing the existing card. No new dependency.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: Digest scope is the design: manifest-only misses a replaced binary, hashing everything including state breaks plugins that write their own files, and re-asking on cosmetic changes trains click-through - so the digest covers code and asks only, and the design must fix which files count. Hand-placed plugins gaining a consent step is a behaviour change and needs a migration message, not a silent disable.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-dplug-07)
Audit: pass — rung existing (installed Record and catalog sha256 path verified); stdlib crypto only; shares one consent-schema change with REC-dplug-08; no dependency; no estimates. | sysc-1421 plus the 2026-09-24 sources design own the consent card pinned to release identity/capabilities; the content-digest key and the hand-placed-plugin consent case are unowned.

title: [pleamar] Capability granularity: read vs write, named scopes, and refusals that say what to declare
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-dx-plug-07).

Recommendation: Make the capability classes match the decision a user actually makes: split read from write where one class covers both (state.get/state.list vs state.set; wallpaper snapshot vs mask-set; screenshot capture vs reading the save directory), add a named scope where a class ranges over many things (which root for files), and turn refusals into instructions - the runtime reply names the call, the missing grant and the manifest line to add, and the consent card uses the same words. Copy the principle `listening is not commanding`, not the plumbing: host calls are already gated per call kind, so this is a table plus scope plumbing, not a new subsystem.

Approach: internal/plugin/manifest.go: the capability constants (:64-98) and capabilities() validation (:487-505) learn the narrower names and optional scopes; internal/plugin/hostcall.go: the Dispatcher keeps one permit check per call kind but consults the narrower grant (state today shares one gate for get/set/list :160-163; wallpaper shares CapWallpaper for snapshot and mask-set :190-193; screenshot shares CapScreenshot for start and directory :224-228; files :229-232), and the flat refusals (:161-162, :180, :185, :192, :197, :216, :221, :226, :231) become one helper producing `call X needs capability Y; declare it in manifest.json as ...`. Store side: the consent record (store/installed.go:23-37) and card (pluginstore_model.go:330-350) list the same terms with aliases so existing consent keeps its meaning. Files browse keeps its host-owned root scope (v1.FilesBrowseParams) as the model for named scopes. Required commands stay a PATH hint (MissingCommands, manifest.go:234-236) and both the consent lines and the refusal text must say exec permissions are not gated - that half is REC-dplug-09.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: Consent migration before code: a grant named `state` consented yesterday must map exactly onto the new names without widening or silently revoking, or the change breaks installed plugins. More names mean more click-through, so split only where the user's decision changes. The refusal must not imply enforcement the shell does not have - a plugin can still exec its own children. Shares the consent-record schema change with REC-dplug-07.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-dplug-08)
Audit: pass — table plus scope plumbing over the existing per-call gate (shared gates at hostcall.go:160-232 verified); no new subsystem; consent migration flagged; no dependency; no estimates. | Capabilities remain coarse call-kind gates (state/wallpaper/screenshot/files share one gate each); no read/write splits, named scopes or actionable refusals planned. sysc-745 is a notify capability string, unrelated.

title: [pleamar] Plugin containment: staged rlimit + landlock/systemd boundary behind the supervisor, design first
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-dx-plug-06).

Recommendation: Replace the disclaimer with a staged boundary around plugin processes: apply child resource limits at exec (address space, CPU time, file size, descriptors), add filesystem confinement through landlock via the already-pinned golang.org/x/sys/unix (or a systemd user scope with hardening for the cgroup half), and make network restriction its own explicit decision. Design first with owner sign-off, because the mechanism changes the plugin trust contract the package documents (manifest.go:5-8) and the consent text the user reads; an unconfined fallback must be visible, never silent.

Approach: internal/plugin/supervisor.go starts the child directly as the shell user with a scrubbed environment (exec.CommandContext :160, pluginEnvironment :166); rlimits go in through SysProcAttr on that command (stdlib syscall), a landlock ruleset before exec through x/sys/unix (already in go.mod at v0.47.0 - no new dependency, no CGO), and optionally a cgroup through `systemd-run --user` (native Linux service rung) for sessions that have a user manager. Denials surface like today's failed-view path (pluginhost.go:506) rather than a mysterious exit. The mechanism commit changes the trust statement (manifest.go:5-8) and the store's consent lines (pluginstore_model.go:339-347) with it, and tests use the existing helper plugin (internal/plugin/helper.go) to prove a denied read or write. Independent of sysc-754's directory watch.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: dependency · scope: L · impact: M.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: The boundary must cover what plugins legitimately need (the compositor socket, their own state root, declared commands) or every plugin breaks; landlock needs kernel/API probing with a reported fallback and a systemd scope assumes a user manager, so neither can be mandatory. A half-configured sandbox gives false confidence, which is worse than the current honest disclaimer, so the mechanism and the documentation land in one change with owner sign-off; network confinement deserves a separate decision because it changes the plugin contract more than filesystem confinement.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-dplug-09)
Audit: pass — dependency rung pinned (golang.org/x/sys v0.47.0, already in go.mod:11); owner sign-off required and stated in notes; landlock/rlimits are not CGO; no estimates. | No confinement work anywhere: manifest states the trust model outright; sysc-1424 (rate limits) is adjacent only. Landlock/rlimit absent from bd and register.

title: [pleamar] `sysc-shell config check`: validate a config file offline and exit
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-dx-tool-01).

Recommendation: Add a `config check [path]` subcommand beside `ipc` in cmd/sysc-shell/main.go that reads a candidate config.json through the same loader the running shell uses, prints `path: ok` with the resolved facts or the field-path errors, and exits 0/1. It never opens Wayland, Niri or the socket, so a hand-edited or candidate config can be tested before it is deployed and scripts/agents can gate configs without taking the session down - the mechanism pleamar's `--check` provides. Scope the first cut to config.json only; sysc-740 (one schema driving validation and the settings pane) is adjacent, so if it lands first the check must call the same schema-driven validator rather than become a second, weaker parser.

Approach: cmd/sysc-shell/main.go: add the subcommand branch in main() (:445-452) next to `ipc` and a runConfigCheck that calls config.Load (internal/config/load.go:302) / config.Parse (:318, strict DisallowUnknownFields at :321) on the argument or config.DefaultPath() (load.go:291-298); print the error as returned (field paths come from pathErr, internal/config/config.go:800) and mirror the startup semantics where a missing file means defaults and an invalid one is non-zero (main.go:83-87). Rung existing: the loader, resolver and error formatting all ship; only the CLI entry point is new. No new dependencies.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: S · impact: M.
Prerequisites: none.
Risk: sysc-740 may move the validator's home; staying on one code path is what keeps the check honest. Output becomes a script contract - keep it stable or add an explicit --json mode.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-dtool-01)
Audit: pass — rung existing (config.Load/Parse/pathErr verified); offline CLI only, never opens Wayland/Niri/socket; owner scope question recorded; no dependency; no estimates. | No offline validation path or issue; sysc-740 is one-schema validation/settings, not a CLI check. Scope question (config.json only) correctly left to the owner.
notes: Batch 2 (dtool-01) implemented on branch feat/tier4-config-check from origin/main d513c401, 5 commits, 3 files under cmd/sysc-shell only. RED-then-GREEN per task. Local review: ownership stays in cmd/sysc-shell (internal/config untouched, it owns parsing); the trust boundary is the path argument - directory, -prefixed token, second argument and an incomplete grammar all refuse with exit 2 and no source text echoed; no goroutine, context or file handle beyond config.Load; no Wayland proxy or redraw path; no new settings key, IPC method, status field or flags. Focused test TestRunConfigCheckReportsLoaderErrorsVerbatim plus TestRunConfigCheckOutputIsByteStable pin the exit split and the verbatim loader text. No architecture-review trigger. Live niri 26.04 (8ed0da4): config check on the real config prints the resolved path and exits 0; an invalid copy exits 1 with stderr exactly 'config: terminal-opacity: 10 is outside 50..100' and empty stdout; two paths and a bare 'config' exit 2 with the usage line; unset NIRI_SOCKET and WAYLAND_DISPLAY still exit 0; niri msg -j layers and sysc-shell ipc status are byte-identical before and after. Deviation from the plan, found by the live matrix: the planned dispatch passed os.Args[2:], so 'config check PATH' treated 'check' as the path and 'config' alone silently checked the default path; the grammar now lives in runConfigCheck so the verb is exactly 'config check [path]' and an incomplete invocation refuses instead of falling through to a compositor run. Two fixtures were corrected against the real loader: two non-empty JSON values report the decoder's unknown-field error (the 'more than one JSON value' text needs a second value that decodes clean), and an empty file reports 'config: EOF'. Exit 2 for read failures is decided by errors.As on the loader's wrapped *fs.PathError rather than by the plan's 'config: read ' prefix. Added a refusal for an unresolvable default path instead of printing ': ok'. Issue stays open: nothing here is deployed and README discovery of the verb is recorded as discovered work.

title: [pleamar] Installer Update path on the existing stop-swap-stamp pipeline, with a printed version delta
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-dx-dist-01).

Recommendation: Implement the Update entry the owner-approved suite-installer design already carries (design :114, :172) rather than a self-updating binary: when a stamp exists, `sysc update` re-fetches the current release installer (the one-liner path, design :176-183), verifies SHA256, then runs the existing install pipeline - stop the units it wrote, download-all-then-swap with .bak, rewrite the stamp, restart previously running units on failure - and prints a per-component version delta between the old stamp and the new pin so the user sees what changed. Use sysc-744's report-only check (its issue) as the 'newer release?' step; keep the update a command the user runs, not a self-replacement path (the deploy guard's no-self-install stance stands). Release and tag publication stays owner-gated (sysc-1158), and non-Arch systems keep the named refusal.

Approach: Installer repo: cmd/sysc/main.go gains the verb in usage/dispatch (:52-54, :696); internal/install/install.go reuses stop-before-swap (:373-377), restart-on-failure (:354-366) and stamp persist (:390); internal/fetch/fetch.go keeps the .bak swap (:168-191); internal/stamp/stamp.go reads Release/Components (:46-53) for the delta; the embedded pin (internal/pin/pin.go:137-143) means the update must fetch the newer installer binary, not re-install its own pin. Design rows live in the worktree-only copy (sysc-worktree/docs/plans/2026-10-05-sysc-suite-installer-design.md). Rung existing: the whole install pipeline ships; the verb and the delta print are new.

Target repo: sysc · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: sysc-744, sysc-1158 (releases owner-gated).
Risk: With no published release the path has nothing to fetch, and a kept older installer silently re-installs its embedded pin - the fetch-the-newer-installer step must be explicit. Do not let the delta print imply a changelog the repo cannot produce.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-ddist-01)
Audit: pass — installer repo rec; rung existing (install.go stop-before-swap, fetch .bak swap, stamp Read, embedded pin verified at /home/nomadx/sysc); releases owner-gated (sysc-1158) and no self-replace; no estimates. | The owner-approved installer design carries the Update row (:114,:172) but no bd issue exists in this snapshot (installer-repo bd is out of scope of 04-*), so the implementation is unowned - keep. Prereqs sysc-744/sysc-1158 resolve.

title: [pleamar] IPC element verbs: describe/get/act/focus beside the imperative set (streaming stays sysc-741)
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-dx-tool-06).

Recommendation: Extend the shell's IPC dispatch with the element-facing surface facts the pleamar `--say` channel has and sysc lacks - an expanded get/status over what the shell is showing (outputs, bars, panels, focused item) plus the focus verb - keeping state queries namespaced apart from imperative UI verbs as sysc-1411's acceptance requires. The node-level describe/act semantics (element tree, name-to-node resolution, refusals) are canonical in REC-dplug-01/02: compose onto them rather than defining a second pair, and share one verb namespace and version with sysc-1411. The wait/watch streaming half is explicitly sysc-1411's (capability advertisement, named subscriptions, split event stream): do not grow a second subscription mechanism here. The one-shot CLI stays valid for the new verbs, so scripts, tests and a future agent front-end can ask the running shell instead of guessing.

Approach: internal/ipc/server.go: add dispatch cases beside the existing set (:266-430) wired through ipc.Handlers (:180-205); the get/status expansion reuses and extends the Registry.Status payload shape (internal/shell/registry.go:1116-1149) with per-panel/element facts, and focus routes through the same registry handlers panel.toggle/osd.step already use (server.go:277-317); describe/act are thin aliases onto REC-dplug-01/02's node-level layer, with no second resolution or refusal logic and one namespace and version shared with sysc-1411. cmd/sysc-shell/main.go runIPC (:464-489) stays one-shot. Rung existing: dispatch, handlers, registry state and the CLI all ship; the new verbs are additive. No new dependencies.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: existing · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: sysc-1411 (streaming half only).
Risk: A describe schema frozen too early can constrain sysc-1411's naming - keep payloads additive and version them with sysc-1411's API integer. Avoid duplicating wait/watch outside the subscription work.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-dtool-02)
Audit: revise — additive IPC verbs over the existing dispatch and registry state (server.go, registry.go:1116 verified); streaming explicitly left to sysc-1411; no dependency; no estimates. Outside the seven checks: its describe/act verbs duplicate REC-dplug-01/02 (different gap facets) - merge at ledger time. | O1: do not define a second describe/act - compose onto REC-dplug-01/02 (node-level canonical) and keep the surface-level state expansion, get/status and focus verb here, in one verb namespace versioned with sysc-1411.

title: [pleamar] flake.nix + home-manager module for sysc-shell, following the sysc-greet precedent
description:
From the pleamar gap analysis (gaps: GAP-dx-dist-03).

Recommendation: Ship declarative packaging in the sysc-shell repo: a flake exposing packages.default (buildGoModule of cmd/sysc-shell and the weather plugin), an overlay, and a home-manager module with programs.sysc-shell.{enable,package,autostart} that installs the package and wires autostart as a systemd user service into graphical-session.target - the shape pleamar's nix/home-manager.nix provides. flake.lock pins NixOS/nixpkgs by revision and that revision is the recorded pin; no floating input. sysc-greet/flake.nix is the in-family precedent (packages.default :20, nixosModules.default :142) for structure only. Start with the shell and its plugin artefact; companion daemons get their own flakes if they ever have a second consumer. Owner-gated: the reconciliation records no issue and no decision, so this proceeds only on an owner go-ahead; packaging is build-time only and leaves the Go-only runtime constraint untouched. Until releases are tagged (owner-gated, sysc-1158) the derivation can carry a commit/rev version.

Approach: New flake.nix + flake.lock at the sysc-shell root, derivation modelled on sysc-greet/flake.nix:20-45 (buildGoModule, subPackages, ldflags version injection); module under nix/ following pleamar/nix/home-manager.nix:34-45 but emitting systemd.user.services for graphical-session.target, whose manual equivalent is installing packaging/systemd/sysc-shell.service by hand (sysc-shell/README.md:94-104). The guided installer and AUR routes stay the primary paths (sysc-shell/README.md:62-84). Rung new-code: no Nix exists in the suite (sysc-greet is a different product); the module reuses sysc-greet's structure and pleamar's module shape.

Target repo: sysc-shell · rung: new-code · scope: M · impact: M.
Prerequisites: owner go-ahead (reconciliation: no issue).
Risk: nixpkgs upstream could not be checked offline and no sysc derivation is claimed to exist; do not let an unpinned nixpkgs input become the default. Keep daemon packaging out until a second consumer exists.

Ledger entry: docs/plans/2026-10-14-pleamar-improvement-ledger.md (REC-ddist-02)
Audit: pass — new-code justified (no Nix anywhere in the suite); nixpkgs pin recorded via flake.lock and the rec is owner-gated; packaging is build-time only so Go-only is untouched; companion daemons deferred until a second consumer; no estimates. | No Nix/flake/home-manager work in any repo or the register (0 hits); sysc-greet is precedent for structure only, owner-gated as declared.
notes: Batch 4 (ddist-02) implemented on branch feat/tier4-nix-packaging, stacked on feat/tier4-version-visibility because the stamping check needs the internal/buildinfo that batch owns; the diff against its parent touches only flake.nix, flake.lock, nix/ and README.md, and the Go tree is byte-identical to the branch that passed the full gate (git diff --stat -- '*.go' is empty). Four commits: the pinned flake, the two package outputs, the home-manager module with its harness, the README row. Local review: the Nix files own the Nix surface, packaging/systemd/sysc-shell.service still owns the unit, internal/buildinfo still owns the stamp text, and no Go file learns about Nix. The module's inputs are booleans, one package, and a list of directories whose manifest.json is read at eval time, so a malformed manifest fails before anything starts. No goroutine, no runtime state; removing the module is the user's home-manager switch. Focused checks: the module harness (nix/tests/module.nix) asserts disabled writes no unit, the enabled unit starts a store path and keeps graphical-session.target, Restart, KillMode and the stop timeout, autostart=false omits Install, and a plugin is linked under its manifest id. Every finding was applied: the module passed a stub-lib evaluation that caught lib.mkMerge being given an attrset where it takes a list, and a package default written as 'pkgs.sysc-shell or throw' that would have fired during option merging; package now has no default and the flake's homeModules supplies it with lib.mkDefault, so a user pointing at their own build wins. Other deviations from the plan: the plugin is not also built inside the shell package (two derivations would compile the same source twice for nothing), the module lives in nix/module.nix because a derivation file cannot also be a module, and only homeModules is exported because the module writes home-manager options and a nixosModules entry would promise a configuration that cannot evaluate. Verified here: every .nix file parses, flake.nix imports to {description, inputs, outputs} with one input, the overlay exposes exactly the two names and delegates to the right file with the right arguments, enable=false writes no unit, autostart toggles Install, the unit source is the committed service file and the substitution is %h/.local/bin/sysc-shell to a store path, and a plugin links under its own manifest id. NOT verified, because this machine's Nix store daemon is down and the user is not a trusted user, so no fetch or build can run: nix flake check, nix build of either output, the vendorHash, and the harness under a real nixpkgs. flake.lock carries the nixpkgs revision and hash sysc-greet already pins, copied from that lock file rather than invented, and vendorHash is lib.fakeHash with the refresh command in a comment; nix build will print the real hash on the first run. Follow-up recorded as discovered work. Issue stays open: nothing is built, merged or deployed.

notes: Batch 3 (dtool-04) implemented on branch feat/tier4-docs-drift-gate from origin/main d513c401, 12 commits: one refactor plus three exports in internal/ipc, the new command tools/docscheck, and the new workflow .github/workflows/docs-examples.yml. .github/workflows/ci.yml is byte-identical. No goroutine, no context, no network, no Wayland, no compositor contact - it reads files and prints text. Scope added is one refactor and three exports, one command, one workflow. Focused tests: TestJSONExamplesAreChecked, TestIPCExamplesAreChecked, TestDefaultInputListAndExitCodes, TestRunExitCodes, TestRunPrintsSummaryAndFindingPrefix, TestRunListsSkippedBlocksWhenAsked, each with fixtures proving the checks do not fire where they must not (untagged fence, unknown KDL escape, unrelated shell commands). title: Virtual input devices: in-process wlr_keyboard_init/wlr_pointer_init need no XML; protocol XML only for an external injector client
description: Corrected 2026-10-15 (audit docs/plans/2026-10-15-tier3-ownership-audit-report.md T3-1). wlroots 0.20 has no wlr_keyboard_create/wlr_pointer_create, but wlr/interfaces/wlr_keyboard.h:20 wlr_keyboard_init and wlr/interfaces/wlr_pointer.h:18 wlr_pointer_init are public (WLR_USE_UNSTABLE), so sysc-compositor can create agent-seat devices in process and feed them from its control socket (session design D3.4) with no Wayland protocol. The server-side managers (wlr_virtual_keyboard_manager_v1_create / wlr_virtual_pointer_manager_v1_create) include no generated protocol header either. wlr_virtual_keyboard_v1 carries the client-requested seat and wlr_virtual_pointer_v1_new_pointer_event a suggested_seat; wlroots attaches nothing, the compositor's handler chooses the seat. Remaining decision, only if an EXTERNAL Wayland client is to inject (a test injector or third-party tool): vendor virtual-keyboard-unstable-v1.xml / wlr-virtual-pointer-unstable-v1.xml from wlroots/wlr-protocols (they are not in wayland-protocols 1.49) and generate client bindings. Not a blocker for the control-socket design. Does not approve implementation.

title: Glass lens: recover a live ground under a translucent material panel (premise corrected: an opaque panel hides the background from recapture)
description: The live lens is implemented end to end and inert: PanelHost.lensOursFrame is nil, so the ladder resolves to the static rung and no recapture is asked for. Without that buffer a recapture contains the panel's own silhouette, and painting it back is a hall of mirrors. Remaining work: retain the panel's last painted pixels for the capture region (the Render callback already receives them), map surface-local pixels into the captured region's coordinates (the inverse of the blit's offset and scale), set lensOursFrame, and qualify the result live. The unmix maths (render.Unmix) and its tests already ship. Found while implementing the glass material tranche (sysc-1197).
notes: Fallback, corrected 2026-10-15 (supersedes the 'Tier 3 path (sysc-1212)' wording in the comments below): if the lens fails, it stays at the static rung. sysc-1212 is WM-as-scene and recorded as excluded; glass D13 is the GPU/EGL gate (sysc-202). No issue owns compositor-side glass or capture exclusion, and it would never help Niri. Before choosing a material alpha, find out what the probed strip (x548-566, y400-900 physical) actually paints: the opacity-60 and opacity-92 captures are byte-identical there, so 0.945 is not known to be the body alpha. When quoting the bench, say quantisation, stable frame to frame: repeat captures are byte-identical, the blurred strip has 4-6 values per channel, so the recovered ground steps by about 1/k (around 18 levels at 0.945); the 0.6/0.8/0.9 projections are that model, not measurements.

title: Shell binds the last-advertised wl_seat; with a compositor agent seat it can bind the agent's seat or lose its own
description: Found in the Tier 3 ownership audit 2026-10-15. internal/platform/wayland/registry.go:113 addGlobal stores every non-output global in r.singletons[iface], so a second wl_seat overwrites the first; client.go:423-434 binds that single entry at startup. removeGlobal (registry.go:119-) drops the singleton when the stored global is removed. Today Niri advertises one seat, so this is latent. Once sysc-compositor advertises an agent seat (sysc-1208, owner said yes to D8.2/D8.4), a shell started while the agent seat exists can bind the agent seat instead of the user seat, and removing the agent seat can be seen as losing wl_seat. Fix at the narrowest layer: keep every wl_seat global, read wl_seat.name (v2+), bind the user seat (seat0, or the first advertised if no name matches) and ignore others. The structural guarantee that agent-seat input never reaches shell surfaces (so an agent cannot press the shell's own Allow/Stop) depends on this. The session design's D6 'the shell does nothing' needs this exception. Gated on sysc-1208; do not build before that commission.

title: Assistant worker boundary: deny the B worker AF_UNIX sockets, the runtime dir, compositor/shell env and /dev/uinput
description: Owner chose option B for sysc-1217 (2026-10-15). Under sysc-1223's current boundary (milestone/tier2-plugin-trust), a confined plugin gets read-write on $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (internal/plugin/boundary.go:89) and NIRI_SOCKET in its environment (supervisor.go:538), and Landlock's filesystem rights are not known to mediate connect() to an existing pathname socket. An assistant worker could therefore drive Niri or the shell's Tier 1 socket directly and bypass the approval gate. The plugin protocol is stdio (supervisor.go:168-172), so a stricter worker profile is feasible: no AF_UNIX socket creation (seccomp or a systemd scope RestrictAddressFamilies), no runtime-dir grant, no WAYLAND_DISPLAY/NIRI_SOCKET/shell IPC env, no /dev/uinput, network egress kept for the model API. First failing test: a confined worker that tries to reach $NIRI_SOCKET and the shell IPC socket must fail; also verify the Landlock connect() behaviour on the running kernel rather than assuming it. Design: docs/plans/2026-10-15-tier3-agent-experience-design.md D1.11. Prerequisite for any sysc-1217 implementation; not an implementation commission.

title: sysc-compositor: prune destroyed listeners from Compositor.listeners

Remove an entry when it is destroyed (or keep per-object listeners in their own owner maps only). Before M1's long-lived sessions. Found reviewing PR #5.

title: internal/wallpaper TestThumbStopsOnCancel is load-sensitive: the 2s cancel deadline can be missed mid-item under the serial race sweep

title: Startup ignores saved idle-lock choice when sysc-walls is enabled
description: On the affected laptop, sysc-shell has idle.lock=1h30m while sysc-walls daemon.conf has timeout=5m and its per-user unit is enabled and active; its journal records idle callbacks. The running daemon has the user's UID. A separate system unit exists but is inactive, and its log says no display server was detected. pacman reports no sysc-walls package installed. Registry arms shell lock from saved config but does not reconcile the Walls user unit at startup. Settings apply disables Walls when the choice changes, so service state can drift after an install or out-of-band enable and its own timer can fire first.
acceptance_criteria: After the Walls user unit state is known at startup, a persisted positive Idle.Lock with a configured locker disables and stops that unit before its independent timer can fire. Preserve daemon.conf timeout; leave Walls unchanged when Lock is unset; expose disable failures through existing Walls action status.

Same class as sysc-1249. Fix: the test helper should detach the relay (setMedia(nil) or a fake media) before seeding mediaState, or setMedia should not start a relay for the unavailable service.

description: PR #279 (milestone/tier2-sound) CI run 38749233911 failed only on tests/integration TestPluginWeatherGateNetworkAndViews: plugin_weather_gate_test.go:79 unchanged weather redrew: snapshots 11 -> 13. The sound branch does not touch the weather plugin, its host or the integration harness; not reproduced locally in 15 -race runs on main c65c528b. The assertion counts snapshots across a window, so two extra redraws under CI load (a resize, a theme or reveal tick) fail it. Fix: count snapshots caused by weather updates, not all snapshots in the window.

title: Integrate sysc-compositor into the sysc suite once it is a usable session (shell, greet, launch, lock, walls, installer)
description:
Very future; owner flag 2026-10-16. Do not start until sysc-compositor is a real session: M9 (sysc-1274: --session, graphical-session.target, complete niri CLI, live-reload) at minimum, and plan against the parity reached by then (M15 sysc-1280 for zero unimplemented actions). Milestones already prove pieces: M2 (sysc-greet works), M3 (sysc-shell draws bars). This item is the product-level integration across repos, designed first:
- sysc-shell: running on sysc-compositor as well as Niri (compositor detection, the niri-ipc wire both serve), the control-socket facts for presence (sysc-1193), the first-advertised seat rule (sysc-1254, done), capability differences surfaced honestly.
- sysc-greet and greetd: session entries for sysc-compositor beside niri; greeter running on it (M2 proves the mechanics).
- sysc-launch: L0/S0 (sysc-1264/1265) make sysc-compositor the preferred compositor on PATH.
- sysc-lock, gSlapper/sysc-walls, sysc-notify and plugins: anything that assumes Niri-only protocols or the niri socket path.
- sysc installer and packaging: installing the compositor, session files, systemd user units, scripts/deploy and the deploy guard, docs site.
- Migration and rollback: choosing sysc-compositor or Niri per session, keeping Niri working, an owner-approved switch of the default.
Deliverable when it starts: a cross-repo integration design with an owner decision on the default, then per-repo plans.

title: Reconcile sysc-walls when enabled during an active shell session
description: With Idle.Lock configured and a locker present, sysc-shell reconciles the sysc-walls user unit only once after it first observes a valid loaded state. If the unit is disabled at that point, a later out-of-band enable/start while sysc-shell remains running is not reconciled, so sysc-walls' independent timeout can fire before the configured lock delay. This was observed during laptop validation after enabling the user unit while sysc-shell was already running. Separate from sysc-1259, which covers startup reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: When Idle.Lock is positive and a locker is configured, a sysc-walls user unit that becomes enabled or running after the initial reconciliation is disabled/stopped before its independent timer can fire. Preserve daemon.conf timeout. Surface failures through existing Walls action status and avoid repeated disable commands once the unit is stopped/disabled.

title: TestLauncherListFillsThePanel flakes under the full internal/shell race run ('list {X:13 Y:109 W:534 H:556}, want height 554 ending at 663')
description: Seen once 2026-10-16 in the serial full-package race sweep of milestone/tier1-config-quality after merging origin/main 86f9683a. Passes alone (3/3 under -race) and in the next full internal/shell race run. Two logical pixels of list height: likely order-dependent shared text measurement or font state from an earlier test.
notes: Root cause: launcher results can arrive before the first surface Configure. The early rebuild sizes the viewport with the 16px fallback because h.text is nil; Configure later uses real font metrics without rebuilding. The fix loads the renderer before the initial launcher tree. Added TestLauncherListFitsWhenResultsArriveBeforeConfigure; it failed before the fix and passes after. Targeted race checks passed 10 repetitions. Per owner direction, PR CI is the full internal/shell race gate; defer another local full-package race run.

title: Turning off the terminal background is not persisted: a restart replays the effect
description: Owner report 2026-10-16: the terminal (sysc-terminal) background was turned off, but came back during testing. Observed on archThink: after a service restart (scripts/deploy at 06:40:10), the owner turned it off again in Terminal Art; the panel showed 'Showing a wallpaper' and awww-daemon held Background, yet ~/.local/state/sysc-shell/wallpaper/assignments.json, written at 06:40:55, still read kind effect, effect ak-47, desired_playback playing. Startup reconcile replays that assignment on the next restart, which is how deploys and restarts bring the effect back. Expected: switching the effect off records the shown wallpaper (or an off state) as the assignment. Workaround applied on the bench for the Tier 1 live gates: the assignment was rewritten to kind image, the shown preview image, static (backup assignments.json.bak-tier1-terminal-off-20261016T064220Z). Relevant code: internal/wallpaper/assign.go, engine.go (active assignment, desired playback), terminal.go.

title: Plugin path.open host call (Tier 2 P3): open a file in the user's app from a confined plugin
description: Design: docs/plans/2026-10-16-plugin-open-path-design.md. A program a confined plugin starts inherits its Landlock domain, so kdeconnect and screenshot (which run xdg-open) cannot be confined until the shell opens paths for them. Needs a plan after milestone/tier2-plugin-trust merges and Tier 1 takes minor 19.

title: Settings shows stale values after an external config edit
description: C live gate 2026-10-16 (laptop, build 7e9a7a3f): with Settings > Bar open, external saves moved bar.edge top->right->bottom; the bar moved, but the Edge dropdown still read 'Top' 2.5 s later (grim c6-right/c6-bottom). The reload path replaces the open Settings host's draft and setting registry (internal/shell/registry.go:2140-2144), but nothing shown there rebuilds the panel tree. RecordConfigReload rebuilds it only on an error change (configerror.go:44). Acceptance: after a valid external save, an open Settings page shows the new values without reopening; a table/unit test drives an external reload with Settings open and asserts the rendered control value. Verify the root cause before fixing.

title: Settings flattens the located config diagnostic onto one line
description: C live gate 2026-10-16: the Settings error banner renders the multi-line located diagnostic ('path:line:col: invalid JSON', excerpt line, caret line) as one line, e.g. 'config.json:1:23: invalid JSON   1 | {"***": ...   |   ^', so the caret no longer points at the column (grim c3/c11). The status IPC carries the newlines correctly. Acceptance: Settings renders the excerpt and caret on their own monospace lines, or shows only the first line with the location. Relates to sysc-1171 (positional diagnostics).

title: Left-click bar metrics opens sysmon; unclip bar metric icons
description: CPU and memory bar widgets must left-click to toggle the system-monitor panel (Noctalia sysmon Left = panel-toggle control-center system). Metric glyphs in sysc-icons.ttf are scaled to a 1200-unit box with a 900-unit advance, so they clip horizontally and look stretched on the bar. Rebuild the face so a 24px SVG stays square at body size (~Noctalia baseGlyphSize 16 vs fontSizeBody 14).

title: Glass V3: toast material and a user-facing lens refresh-rate setting (designs)
description: Owner decision 2026-10-16: design both. Toast material costs one readback per toast (glass design D7 fidelity note); refresh-rate setting follows the cadence measurement (D5 note). Smoke at the floor is sysc-1246.

title: Retheme crossfades open panels when only motion settings change
description: B live gate 2026-10-16 (laptop): with the clock panel open, a config reload that changed only accessibility.reduced-motion produced a 20-frame/~316 ms full-buffer panel burst (base 90cd0e5b on reduced-on, a87382ac on reduced-off). PanelHost.retheme (internal/shell/panelhost.go:4672) restarts the animTheme crossfade whenever Theme differs, and Theme includes Motion, so it blends between identical palettes. It is invisible: no settled transition replays, because animator.Configure re-springs only unfinished values. But it paints about 20 frames for nothing. Acceptance: a reload that leaves the palette unchanged reconfigures the animator without starting a crossfade; a unit test asserts no animTheme target after a motion-only retheme. Not a B regression; base does the same.

title: Integration gates cite WAYLAND_DEBUG, which sysc-wayland ignores
description: tests/integration/README.md ('Repaint ceiling and regional damage', cases 4-6) says to run the shell under WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 and read wl_surface.damage_buffer lines. sysc-wayland is a pure-Go client with no wire tracing (no WAYLAND_DEBUG anywhere in sysc-wayland v0.3.2), so the log is empty. The 2026-10-16 Tier 1 gates used a scratch proxy instead: docs/plans/2026-10-16-tier1-live-gate-tools/wlspy.go (it forwards fds, follows delete_id, and logs per-commit damage with layer namespace and buffer size). Decide: fix the README to name a working method, keep the proxy as a test tool in-tree, or add a debug env to platform/wayland. Each needs owner approval.

title: Attribute tranche D's ~25 MiB higher RSS before merge
description: Laptop measurements 2026-10-16 (t1measure, same bench): D 95a94c87 RSS is idle 101 MiB, weather open 112, clock open 110. Baseline origin/main 90cd0e5b: 73 / 84 / 84 MiB; B and C builds 74-75 MiB idle. D's retained complete-frame caches are the likely source (bar 1920x55, toast host 505x1080, panels up to 575x700 at scale 1.25, plus a per-output OSD cache) but are not proven. Design D7 bounds memory, so take a heap profile (SIGUSR2 writes .heap) on the D build with the bar idle and with a panel open, compare it with baseline, and record whether the increase matches the design's bound. Run before the D merge review.

title: Config reload (SIGHUP) does not start or stop plugins added to or removed from plugins.enabled
description: Found in the Tier 2 plugin-trust live gate (2026-10-16). Adding two IDs to plugins.enabled in config.json and sending SIGHUP to the main process left them unstarted; a service restart started them. pluginHost.syncEnabled runs only at startup (pluginhost.go) and from the Settings toggle (popout_plugins.go syncEnabledLocked); the reload path (wayland reloadConfig -> registry persist) never calls it. Same on origin/main ad56fbcd. Expected: a reload reconciles the running set with plugins.enabled, as the Settings toggle does.

title: sysc-compositor: user-seat keyboards need one group with an xkb keymap; drop the Escape quit
description: From sysc-compositor docs/plans/2026-10-16-input-pattern-comparison-report.md K1-K3. wlroots gives backend keyboards no keymap (wayland backend closes the host keymap fd, backend/wayland/seat.c:21), and internal/wlr/input.go handleNewInput sets none, so user-seat clients get untranslatable keycodes. handleKeyboardKey/Modifiers drop every keyboard except the last attached (input.go:267/280); on a VT the real keyboard can be the ignored one. Escape terminates the compositor (input.go:271), which would end a greetd session. Fix: one wlr_keyboard_group for the user seat (Mango main.c:869, input/keyboard.c:143) with a keymap from default rules / XKB_DEFAULT_* and repeat info 25/600 (niri defaults); injected seat keeps its own keyboard (D2.4.1); remove the Escape quit (M2 Quit IPC replaces it). Gates M2: sysc-greet needs a typed password. Nested test: a client on the user seat receives a keymap and keys from two attached keyboards.

title: sysc-compositor: pointer focus correctness (implicit grab, default cursor, root-surface lookup, unmap)
description: From sysc-compositor docs/plans/2026-10-16-input-pattern-comparison-report.md P1-P4 and M4. (1) Keep pointer focus on the pressed surface while a button is held (Mango input/pointer.c:1295 CurPressed); input.go:301 re-targets on every motion. (2) Set the default xcursor over empty space (Mango pointer.c:1389); input.go:315 keeps the client image. (3) Resolve a hit surface to its view via wlr_surface_get_root_surface and popup parents (Mango manage/client.c:70); input.go:411 misses subsurfaces and popups. (4) Clear keyboard/pointer focus and any grab on unmap, not only destroy (input.go:583). (5) Clear pointer focus when a compositor grab starts (niri Focus::Clear). Gates M4. Nested tests for each.

title: sysc-compositor: parent xdg popups under their window and unconstrain them
description: From sysc-compositor docs/plans/2026-10-16-input-pattern-comparison-report.md X1. internal/wlr/xdg.go:37 creates every xdg surface, popups included, under the scene root, so menus draw at the layout origin and can leave the output. Mango creates the popup tree under its parent's tree on the popup's initial commit (manage/layer.c:448) and calls wlr_xdg_popup_unconstrain_from_box against the output's usable area (:418). Same parenting for layer-shell popups once layer-shell lands. Gates M1 (xdg-shell exit gate). Nested test: a popup's scene position follows its parent and stays inside the output.

title: Shell -race CI hangs 10m in TestSettingsAfterIdleApply: idle settings fixture never drains invalidations
description: PR #285 CI run 38894875392 timed out after 10m in TestSettingsAfterIdleApply/enabled_unit_overlay_and_apply. Stack: applyIdleSetting's worker holds Registry.mu and blocks in publishSurface on a full r.invalidations (cap 8); bluetooth and control publishers block on the same channel; the test waits for r.mu forever. newOpenIdleSettings (idle_settings_test.go) builds on newPanelRegistry and never calls keepInvalidationsDrained (panelhost_test.go), whose comment names this exact stall. Pre-existing on main; test-only fix: drain in the fixture.
notes: PR CI is the merge gate for go test -race -count=1 ./...; local repo-wide race verification is deferred because the workstation safety hook blocks it. Follow-up: rerun the full local race suite when the guard permits and record that result separately from CI.

title: sysc-compositor: send frame done to clients after each scene commit
description: The output frame handler (internal/wlr/output.go sysc_repaint_scene_output) commits the scene but never calls wlr_scene_output_send_frame_done, so wl_surface.frame callbacks are never answered. Clients that pace on frame callbacks (kitty) stop repainting after their first frames: in the sysc-1296 live check kitty got 9 done events in a minute while the host frame loop ran 3750 times, and typed text and selections never appeared. tinywl calls it right after wlr_scene_output_commit. Needs a nested test that counts a frame-paced client's done events (weston-simple-shm), and a laptop grim shot of kitty showing typed text.

title: Commit the uncommitted policy_test.go on milestone/stable-bar
description: internal/platform/wayland/policy_test.go is modified and unbacked by any commit in that worktree.

title: Restore recorder dest path when adopting an owned process
description: Adopt matches exe+args and signals the owned PID, but recover does not restore the original -o path, so stop after adoption verifies an empty dest and can mark Failed.

title: DMS shell vs sysc-shell gap analysis
description: Completed the approved DMS shell vs sysc-shell audit plan. Pin current DMS and sysc origin/main sources; compare first-party shell behavior on Niri; produce and register evidence-backed report and deduplicated defect/SHOULD-have ledger. Reconcile against sysc-677 and existing parity issues; do not implement findings.

title: Screen-reader export for accessible shell surfaces
description: sysc UI nodes carry accessible names and roles, but the shell does not publish a screen-reader tree. The accepted roadmap defers AT-SPI until adoption is decided; DMS QML controls declare Accessible.name and Accessible.role. Decide whether sysc adopts screen-reader support, then specify the AT-SPI bridge and Orca acceptance before implementation.

title: Switch audio output ports and card profiles
description: The sysc audio panel selects sink and source devices and controls volume, but exposes no PipeWire port or card-profile state. DMS v1.6.3 provides headphone, speaker and HDMI port selection with profile switching. Add output port and profile selection with unavailable-device handling and preserve the selected sink state.

title: Add automatic wallpaper cycling
description: sysc-shell assigns static and video wallpapers per output but has no cycling schedule. DMS v1.6.3 supports interval and time-based automatic cycling. Add an opt-in cycle policy that works with the existing wallpaper library and per-output assignments; define suspend, battery and failure behavior in design.

title: Add timed Caffeine presets
description: The current Caffeine control holds an indefinite process-wide idle inhibit until the user turns it off. DMS master adds timed presets, remaining-time display and expiration; this is newer than v1.6.3. Add bounded duration choices and expiry while keeping the indefinite option. sysc-716 covers external inhibitor reporting and is separate.

title: Add an enlarged clipboard image preview
description: sysc clipboard rows show bounded thumbnails up to 48 logical pixels and do not provide a full-size preview. DMS master adds a separate image preview surface; this is newer than v1.6.3. Allow the user to inspect an image entry before pasting, with payload and decode bounds retained.

title: Add a screen color picker
description: DMS v1.6.3 includes a first-party screen color picker that captures a chosen pixel and copies its hex value. sysc-shell has Niri screen/window/region screenshot capture and editable palette hex values but no screen-pixel sampling UI. Add an opt-in Niri-compatible picker that reports and copies the selected color, with clear fallback when screen capture is unavailable.

title: Show active microphone, camera, and screen-share use
description: DMS exposes a first-party privacy indicator for active microphone, camera, and screen-share use. sysc-shell has no corresponding state or indicator; sysc-1413 separately owns Niri cast-state decoding. Define reliable PipeWire and Niri signals and confidence/fallback behavior before adding a bar or Control Centre indicator; do not copy DMS's name-based screencast heuristic as authoritative.

title: Plugin protocol 1.17: stepped sliders and compact bar images
description: ThinkPad controls require host-rendered fan and keyboard sliders plus the official wordmark inside a bar button.
design: Add a stepped slider node with finite min/max/step/value validation and committed numeric EventChange input; route pointer and keyboard commits through the existing plugin event path. Allow only compact (up to 128x32) images in bar views. Keep sliders restricted to panel/floating views and bump plugin protocol minor to 17.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol, conversion and shell input tests pass; vet passes; CI full test suite passes; the ThinkPad plugin can draw its wordmark in the bar and control sliders.

title: sysc-launch: tag a release containing L0 (owner asks first)
description: Cross-repo gate for S0 (sysc-1265). L0 (sysc-launch PR #10, 7d73e95) is merged but untagged; latest tag v0.2.1. Tags happen only when the owner asks. Once tagged, sysc-1265 bumps sysc-shell's module.

title: Owner decision: confirm or veto design section 14 amendment (vendored protocol XML, generated headers)
description: sysc-compositor design section 14 was amended 2026-10-16 (M1): protocol XML vendored unchanged from the wlroots tag in protocols/, headers generated by go generate ./internal/wlr into a gitignored directory, never committed. Every later wlr-protocols global (screencopy, gamma, data-control, foreign-toplevel) uses this path. Open to the owner's veto; close when they confirm.

title: sysc-compositor: end a nested session when its last output closes
description: Niri's winit backend quits when its window closes. A nested sysc-compositor stops only on SIGINT/SIGTERM or the Quit action (the Escape quit was removed in sysc-1295). Closing the host window should end the session. Nested only; DRM sessions end through Quit or the session manager.

title: sysc-compositor: keep the libseat session and switch VTs on Ctrl+Alt+F1-F12
description: Prerequisite for M2's greetd VT gate. wlr_backend_autocreate(c.loop, nil) (internal/wlr/compositor.go:179) creates the libseat session for DRM but never returns it, so the compositor cannot call wlr_session_change_vt. Keep the session; switch VTs on the XF86Switch_VT_* keysyms regardless of binds {} (the greeter config has none, and a VT switch is the way out of a broken greeter; match Niri 26.04's handling in src/input/); destroy the session after the backend on exit. Nested tests cannot reach the DRM path; the VT gate is its first run.

title: Join manually entered or hidden Wi-Fi networks from the shell
description: Add manual SSID and credential entry for hidden or unlisted open and WPA-Personal networks through a supported NetworkManager or iwd backend. Keep credentials out of logs. WPA-Enterprise (802.1X/EAP) uses a separate identity and authentication flow tracked in sysc-1318; this feature can reuse the SSID entry path.
acceptance_criteria: Enter a hidden or unlisted SSID; choose open or supported WPA-Personal security and enter its passphrase; connect through a supported backend and show an actionable result; never log credentials.
notes: Local service/panel implementation and full Go suite pass after the profile-reuse fix; go vet, formatting, dependency-diff, and service race checks also pass. Safe live qualification is delayed pending isolated lab profiles or a runner. The previous full internal/shell race attempt ended after 150s with a stack dump; sysc-1298 and sysc-1285 track the known shell race issues.

title: Show and control first-party VPN connections in the Network panel
description: sysc-shell has no first-party VPN state or controls in its Network panel. Start with installed NetworkManager VPN profiles. Plugin-provided VPN behavior remains outside this feature.
acceptance_criteria: The panel reports VPN state and can connect or disconnect a supported installed profile. It reports backend and connection errors without requiring provider-specific command configuration.
notes: Local service/panel implementation and full Go suite pass after the profile-reuse fix; go vet, formatting, dependency-diff, and service race checks also pass. Safe live qualification is delayed pending isolated lab profiles or a runner. The previous full internal/shell race attempt ended after 150s with a stack dump; sysc-1298 and sysc-1285 track the known shell race issues.

title: Manage app favourites, visibility, and defaults in Settings
description: Settings has no first-party application library preferences. Add shell-owned favourites and hidden-app choices, plus supported default application choices, without editing system desktop files or becoming a general application manager.
acceptance_criteria: Users can mark installed applications as favourite or hidden and choose supported defaults. Launcher visibility and ranking and shell launch actions follow saved choices.
notes:
2026-10-18 review checkpoint: implementation is in /home/nomadx/sysc-shell/.worktrees/caelestia-tranche-7-app-preferences, based on origin/main b28948f. Review fixed cross-list favourite/hidden conflicts and retries a Settings refresh when the old launcher service is retired; focused tests, full go test ./..., and go vet ./... pass with GOWORK pointing at the merged sysc-launch refresh worktree. GOWORK=off compilation still fails because the current module pin lacks required APIs. No PR was open at this checkpoint; keep this issue gated by sysc-1347 until a tagged compatible release is pinned. Live Niri qualification remains outstanding.

2026-10-18 handover execution: rebased onto origin/main d6f937d043b20f4592032b534598022512c35a37 and committed as c2afa24e5f1ccc5163a551b03c8b4d6e63038ed1. Pushed feat/caelestia-tranche-7-app-preferences and opened PR #332: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-shell/pull/332. Full suite passed with GOWORK=/tmp/sysc1315.work go test -p 2 -count=1 ./...; vet passed with GOMAXPROCS=4 GOWORK=/tmp/sysc1315.work go vet -p 2 ./...; race checks passed for internal/shell, internal/config, internal/settings, and internal/i18n. Normal GOWORK=off build remains blocked by the pinned sysc-launch APIs; v0.3.0 lacks RefreshApplications. Live Niri qualification remains outstanding. Keep sysc-1346 open.

PR #332 CI recheck: docs-examples passed; the test job failed at go vet because the pinned sysc-launch lacks ServiceConfig.TerminalDesktopID, Service.RefreshApplications(), and Entry.TerminalApp. This matches the known sysc-1347 release blocker.

PR #332 is ready for code review. The merge gate remains sysc-1347 plus normal GOWORK=off Go checks, locale checks, and live Niri qualification.

2026-10-19: PR #332 merged as 08b3f695 after CI passed. Laptop Niri check confirmed hidden btop stays out of the launcher; Htop and Btop launch successfully.

title: Toggle a window between floating and tiled placement from the shell
description: The running-apps/window action menu has no per-window floating toggle. Add the shell affordance and coordinate it with sysc-compositor M6, which supplies floating-window behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A focused window can be toggled between floating and tiled from the shell when the compositor supports the action. The shell reports resulting state, preserves focus, and hides or disables the control when unavailable.
notes: 2026-10-18: Shell implementation is in feat/caelestia-tranche-8-compositor-20261018 based on the latest origin/main. Focused menu and race checks pass. Laptop Niri live gate: window 277 changed tiled to floating; the open menu updated to Move to tiling. Escape returned focus to window 277. Reopening and toggling back returned it to tiled, and Escape restored focus to the same ID. The installed binary hash was unchanged; the original service and Niri config were restored. Keep open until integrated; sysc-compositor M6 is a related compatibility gate, not a blocker.

title: Select a keyboard layout from the shell
description: The shell observes keyboard-layout changes and shows an OSD but cannot select a layout. Add a picker that lists layouts reported by the compositor and requests a selection. sysc-823 covers key mapping and editing inside text fields; this issue covers changing the active compositor layout.
acceptance_criteria: The shell lists layouts reported by the compositor and requests the selected layout. It reports success in the OSD only after compositor confirmation and explains unavailable state.
notes: 2026-10-18: Shell implementation is in feat/caelestia-tranche-8-compositor-20261018 based on the latest origin/main. Focused picker and race checks pass. Laptop Niri reports only English (US), so the opt-in keyboard-layout item remained hidden and live selection could not be exercised. No keyboard config was changed. Keep open until integrated and live selection acceptance is available; sysc-823 and M9 are related work, not blockers.

title: GAP-01: Add WPA-Enterprise authentication
description: Add a supported WPA-Enterprise (802.1X) credential flow through NetworkManager. Collect identity and credentials for a supported EAP method, report failures, and never log secrets. Related: GitHub #289 covers manual SSID entry; #291 covers VPN profiles.
acceptance_criteria: The user can select 802.1X where supported, enter required identity and credentials, connect, and see actionable authentication or backend errors. Diagnostics never include credentials.

title: GAP-01: Add cellular connection controls
description: Add first-party mobile-broadband controls to the Network panel through supported NetworkManager and ModemManager services.
acceptance_criteria: Show modem and connection state when supported; connect or disconnect a saved mobile-broadband profile; explain unavailable backends, hardware, or operations; preserve Wi-Fi and Ethernet behavior.

title: Implement M6D Weather reference plugin
description: Execute the committed M6D plan after M6C.
acceptance_criteria: Weather bar, tooltip, settings, forecast, and offline stale/error integration gates pass.

title: GAP-02: Route individual audio streams to an output
description: Add a destination selector to each application stream in the Audio panel using the existing PipeWire and WirePlumber control path.
acceptance_criteria: Route only the selected stream to an available output; leave the default output and unrelated streams unchanged; reflect refreshed stream state and handle a destination that disappears.

title: GAP-18: Allow remapping in-shell navigation actions
description: Add a bounded configurable key-action set for shell panel navigation while keeping Niri responsible for global shortcuts.
acceptance_criteria: Keep current behavior by default; allow remapping navigation, activate, cancel, and tab actions; reject invalid or conflicting mappings clearly; provide a reset path; do not change Niri global shortcut handling.

title: GAP-21: Let users show passive tray items
description: Add a setting that lets users choose whether passive tray items appear.
acceptance_criteria: Users can show or hide passive items; the default remains hidden; existing pinned and hidden ordering is preserved; the setting persists across restarts.

title: GAP-22: Support multiple bars on one output
description: Design and implement multiple independently configured bars on one output, with stable identities and defined Niri exclusive-zone behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Define stable bar identities, independent placement, output-change and reload behavior, and each bar's contribution to Niri exclusive zones before implementation.

title: Add fixed config-defined command actions to the launcher
description: Add a fixed list of user-defined argv actions as searchable launcher results. sysc-1405 covers dynamic command providers that return launcher rows from command output. This feature covers static config entries and reuses the existing launcher execution path, which starts argv directly without a shell.
acceptance_criteria: Show configured argv actions in launcher results; start actions without a shell; require explicit opt-in for actions marked dangerous; report launch failures.

title: Add opt-in readable GTK palette templates
description: Restore GTK 3/4 color integration as separate opt-in templates. Generate contrast-safe GTK semantic and legacy foreground/background colors from the active sysc-shell palette, apply through marker-managed blocks in the user gtk.css files, preserve unrelated user CSS, and remove only sysc-shell blocks when toggled off. Do not change gtk-theme-name, icon, font, or cursor settings.

title: [onboarding] Let users choose startup plugins during first-start setup
description: Add a dedicated graphical onboarding section with checkboxes for installed bar plugins. Checking enables the plugin and adds its bar entry to the onboarding draft; Save/Finish persists enabled IDs and bar placements. Plugin installation stays in Settings.

title: Launcher usage boost has no frequency signal past its caps
description:
Measured with a crafted history through the real ranker:

  boost= 25  used 200x today
  boost= 25  used  10x 5 days ago
  boost= 25  used 200x 5 days ago
  boost=  1  used 200x 11 days ago
  boost=  1  used 200x 40 days ago
  boost=  1  used   1x 11 days ago
  boost=  1  used   1x 40 days ago

Two flattenings. historyAmountCap=10 saturates the open count, then usageBoostCap=25 clamps the product, so anything opened a handful of times recently is indistinguishable. Then base = 10 - ageDays goes non-positive at 10 days and max(base*amount,1) collapses everything older to exactly 1: a daily driver used 200 times ranks level with something opened once last month, and the tie falls back to alphabetical.

The mechanism itself works -- 9 entries carry a boost on the desktop today and they do sort above the alphabetical run. This is the shape of the curve, not the wiring. Changing it is a behaviour change in sysc-launch, shared with its own consumers, so it needs agreement before shipping.

title: Prevent stale reload commits from dropping newer Settings edits
description: Review follow-up for merged PR #329. An external config candidate can be read before a delayed Settings write, then commit after that write has recorded its own config snapshot in settingsWriteReloads. The unmatched candidate clears that snapshot list. The queued reload of the writer's snapshot is then treated as a genuine external reload and can cancel a newer debounced Settings edit before it applies. Preserve or correlate outstanding writer snapshots across stale external commits, and add a deterministic ordering regression proving a newer edit survives this interleaving.

title: sysc-terminal raster.FindFont has no distro-neutral font fallback
description: internal/raster/font.go:30 FindFont probes only Arch/Nix layout paths: /usr/share/fonts/TTF/JetBrainsMonoNerdFont-Regular.ttf, /usr/share/fonts/TTF/JetBrainsMono-Regular.ttf, /usr/share/fonts/noto/NotoSansMono-Regular.ttf. On Debian/Ubuntu nothing matches, so renderer.New without an explicit Font fails with 'raster: no supported font found'. sysc-shell CI hits this on three lockscreen preview tests and only passes because the workflow apt-installs fonts-noto-core and symlinks truetype/noto/NotoSansMono-Regular.ttf into the probed path. title: Card fill is indistinguishable from the panel it sits on
description:

Two stories in the parity docs: the live DMS grim used widgetBackgroundColor "sch" (Material surface-container-high), but design D3 mapped the mid token SurfaceContainer. Raising Capsule globally would also change the bar. A panel-only step (map cards to surface-container-high, keep bar on SurfaceContainer) needs a second fill token; the matugen template currently emits only surface_container. Owner taste on which surface, not a missing paint path.

title: Launcher usage boost has no frequency signal past its caps
description:
Measured with a crafted history through the real ranker:

  boost= 25  used 200x today
  boost= 25  used  10x 5 days ago
  boost= 25  used 200x 5 days ago
  boost=  1  used 200x 11 days ago
  boost=  1  used 200x 40 days ago
  boost=  1  used   1x 11 days ago
  boost=  1  used   1x 40 days ago

Two flattenings. historyAmountCap=10 saturates the open count, then usageBoostCap=25 clamps the product, so anything opened a handful of times recently is indistinguishable. Then base = 10 - ageDays goes non-positive at 10 days and max(base*amount,1) collapses everything older to exactly 1: a daily driver used 200 times ranks level with something opened once last month, and the tie falls back to alphabetical.

The mechanism itself works -- 9 entries carry a boost on the desktop today and they do sort above the alphabetical run. This is the shape of the curve, not the wiring. Changing it is a behaviour change in sysc-launch, shared with its own consumers, so it needs agreement before shipping.

title: setSessionProfile runs a command under Registry.mu
description:
internal/shell/popout_session.go:243 calls r.runArgv(powerProfileSetArgv(name)) straight from an action handler, which holds Registry.mu. That is command I/O under the lock, which the project constraint forbids: no command or filesystem work may run while Registry.mu or the Wayland owner is blocked.

The same file already has the correct shape two functions up: scheduleLoadProfiles copies the exec hooks, runs off the owner without the lock, re-takes it, checks the panel host is still current, then applies. The set path should schedule the same way.

Found while designing the control centre (sysc-158). The control centre routes every command through its own scheduleControl seam rather than copying this, so it is not blocked on the fix.

title: Host silently rejects malformed plugin views (wrong root kind, node-budget overflow) with no signal

title: Bar renders corrupt output on the laptop; cause not established
description:
2026-09-01. The bar paints scattered coloured blocks instead of content, or is absent and the window behind shows through. Process alive, single instance, log completely silent.

Not reproduced in tests. The same commit and the same font rendered correctly earlier in the same session, so the variable is not obviously the code.

Ruled out by reverting one at a time, none of which restored it: icon advance width 1260 back to 900, usWinAscent 1100 back to 900, and the entire internal/render/icons directory back to the prior commit. Also checked: only one sysc-shell process, no competing shell running.

Untested hypothesis: session state after roughly a dozen kill and restart cycles, which is the territory of sysc-51. A Niri session restart would rule that in or out and was not tried. The pre-session binary is kept at ~/.local/bin/sysc-shell.pre-fix.

Establish the cause before trusting any further live capture from that machine, since a bad session invalidates visual judgement of every other issue.

title: Plugin panels: report the granted size in view.open and find the laptop width clamp
description:
On the laptop (eDP-1, 1536x864 logical, scale 1.25) the calendar panel (manifest 1040x760) is drawn about 810x758: width clamped, height intact. Placement.FittedSize would allow ~1500 wide, so something else clamps width. Separately, pluginHost.openPanel (internal/shell/pluginhost.go ~806-834) fills view.open Width/Height from the manifest (spec.Width/Height), so a plugin is told 1040x760 while its tree is laid out in the smaller surface: plugins cannot lay out for the box they actually get, and layout the plugin linted at the declared size can be refused (calendar's status-banner Refresh button fails lint at 810x758).

Wanted: (1) root-cause the width clamp; (2) view.open (and a resize path when the surface changes) carries the fitted/granted size; (3) test that a panel declared wider than its placement is told the smaller size.

Consumer: sysc-plugins calendar (currently designed for a fixed 800x720 as a workaround, see sysc-plugins docs/plans/2026-09-25-world-clock-handover.md and the calendar polish commit). Evidence: laptop screenshots 2026-09-26, panel borders at x=905..1918 physical.

title: Keep DND OSD state ordered across rapid toggles
description: Each DND relay change launches an independent goroutine to publish an OSD. Rapid toggles can acquire Registry.mu out of order and leave the visible OSD describing an earlier state. Serialize these publications or re-read current DND state when applying them; cover out-of-order delivery.

title: Version the shell IPC: capabilities, subscriptions, split event stream
description:
DMS's socket contract pairs an explicit integer API version with capability advertisement, per-service named subscriptions that snapshot before deltas, refcounted lazy managers, and a second connection so a flooded subscription never delays a command. sysc's internal/ipc should adopt the same shape as it grows verbs, keeping imperative UI verbs namespaced apart from state queries. Acceptance: a slow event consumer cannot head-of-line-block a panel toggle.

Evidence: reviews/references/DankMaterialShell/core/internal/server/subscription.go:5-34; reviews/references/DankMaterialShell/core/internal/server/server.go:412-496; reviews/references/DankMaterialShell/core/internal/qsipc/client.go:24-40

title: Icon resolver drops 37% of application icons: no SVG support
description:
internal/icons is raster-only by design (package doc: 'Milestone 5 is raster-only. No SVG rasterizer is pinned'). Measured against the desktop's real 199 launcher entries through the resolver the launcher actually uses:

  74 of 199 (37%) fail to resolve and fall back to the letter capsule
  66 of those 74 have an SVG on disk that would have resolved
   6 have nothing on disk
   2 name an absolute path that no longer exists

Every entry names an icon; none of this is missing Icon= keys. Misses include org.gnome.Boxes, org.gnome.Cheese, com.github.rafostar.Clapper, ca.desrt.dconf-editor -- all present as scalable/apps/*.svg.

Found while auditing the launcher's letter-capsule fallback, but the resolver is shared with notifications and the tray, so this is not launcher chrome. Fixing it means pinning an SVG rasterizer, which is a new dependency and needs agreement.

title: Running-apps and tray icons lose resolution at bar size
description: Live: compact bar icons look soft. attachRunningIconsLocked requests Square(name, size) at 18 if bar.scale120() is 0 and never re-requests after configure. decodeRaster uses ApproxBiLinear; paintImage is nearest-neighbour and upscales if the raster is smaller than the box. Shared one Image for all bars. Do not start a second icon worker; reuse trayIcons. Request at Physical size after configure.
acceptance_criteria: Icons requested at Physical(runningAppIconSize) once scale is known; a configure that changes scale re-requests. Raster edge matches the paint box so paintImage does not upscale. Tray path already uses trayIconPixelSize — keep that, do not regress it.

title: Panel backdrop blur: screencopy binding and blur kernel
description:
Executes docs/plans/2026-09-11-panel-backdrop-blur.md Tasks 1-10 on feature/panel-backdrop-blur, rebased onto main at 79e9899 (which brought the control-centre work in). Eleven commits.

Measured 2026-09-12/13 (go1.27.0, Ryzen 7 5700X, powersave): blur kernel 4.94 ms median against a predicted 4.60, linear at 4.6-5.1 ms/MPix over six panel sizes; screencopy readback 5.67 ms median against D16.1's 15 ms stop threshold; ~11 ms per open, inside one 60 Hz frame.

Design corrections found live, each by measurement rather than reading: this Niri offers xrgb8888 only for a region capture, so the captured alpha byte must be filled; a screencopy target's wl_shm pool must hold exactly one buffer, which newGeneration cannot do (hence newCaptureBuffer); the backdrop must go through the rounded mask or panel corners fill in; the shell, not the wayland package, assembles a panel's Style, so the image returns via a new HostCallbacks.Backdrop; and the panel-opacity bound had to move in three places or the lower floor stayed unreachable from config.

capture_output_region is OUTPUT-RELATIVE, not global: probed directly because this output sits at logical 2560,0. A global-space region is refused with nil, an output-relative one returns real content. D3 assumed this and never verified it.

Post-rebase defect found and fixed (876ca72): main's AttachedPanelStyle resolves an attached panel's root at the BAR's opacity, which is opaque, so an attached panel painted straight over its own backdrop. Caught by measuring a live capture: the Audio panel body was a single flat colour, pixel-identical to the bar fill. rootStyle now keeps the panel's own alpha whenever a backdrop is present, with a regression test.

Verified live on two machines: archPC 3440x1440 scale 1.0 and archThink 1920x1080 scale 1.25 (the first fractional-scale exercise of this path). Blur visible on both; ships off by default.

Depends on (1):
  → sysc-202: Milestone 8: rendering qualification [P2]

Coverage gate added 2026-09-13 (9537440): blur is enforced for panels that do not exist yet, not merely true for today's. internal/shell/blurcoverage_test.go walks the whole PanelID enum (failing if it grows past the known end) and scans package sources so every wayland.AuxSpec either sets BlurRegion or carries a blur-exempt comment with its reason. Seven surfaces carry reasons; three of them - the running-apps menu, the tray menu and the tray drawer - record an open scope question for the owner rather than a settled no, because design D13 names neither.

title: Noctalia v4 parity: re-base the ladders, radius axis, Display role, contrast floor
description:
Executes docs/plans/2026-09-11-noctalia-parity.md on feature/noctalia-parity, branched from main at 493ac6b. Thirteen tasks executing three designs: the parity ladders, token conformance as Task 1, component parity as Tasks 5A/5B.
