The token-conformance design measured 105 literal geometry sites in internal/shell on 2026-09-11 against main at d84c9da, and its own Not Verified section flagged that the figure might not be stable. Re-measured 2026-09-13 against main at 493ac6b using the design's own D2 rule (thirteen geometry fields, comments stripped, zero exempt, tests and theme.go skipped): 169 sites, not 105.

By field now: Gap 78 (was 58), Height 36 (was 17), Padding 29 (was 38), Width 17 (was 13), IconSize 5, Stroke 1, MaxWidth 1, ItemHeight 1, ImageSize 1.

The growth is concentrated in one file the design never examined: controlcenter_pages.go carries 62 sites on its own, more than half the original total. The design's worst-file list was popout_audio 24, popout_settings 13, popout_process 11, popout_plugins 8, popout_launcher 7, notifycard 7.

The unmerged feature/network-panel branch adds 18 more (popout_network.go 0 to 17, wifiwidget.go 0 to 1), so the gate reaches about 187 once that slice lands. Tasks 2 to 9 are therefore sized against a number roughly 60 percent too small, and the plan's 105 framing needs correcting as the work proceeds.

Anchors verified against current main: surfacerole_test.go:212, shell/theme.go:199 and theme_test.go:252,255 are exact; render/style.go:145,192 is stale (Shapes is at 111, textRoleCount at 196) and palettes.go:236 is stale (the outline derivation is at 303).

Relates to-110 (in_progress since 2026-09-02, untouched since): Task 7 lowers the nested-surface floor to 1.30:1, but that issue's own text says the open question is owner taste over which surface the cards map to, not a missing paint path. Re-inherits the live gate from the closed sysc-142, whose Task 13 never ran.
notes: PARITY TASKS 10 AND 11 STEP 2 LANDED 2026-09-15 on feature/parity-task10-11 (pushed to origin, awaiting merge to main). Task 10 (4b09377): the three surface conformance tests now cover all twelve PanelIDs instead of PanelMonitor/PanelSession. Five panels legitimately build no cards and record as skipped; the old t.Fatalf turned a widened loop red for them. Card titles read headings inside cards and accept RoleHeadline beside RoleTitle, because a panel that wraps its header in a card (audioHeaderCard) puts its own title there one rung above a card title. Task 11 Step 2 (9936d1e): input radius plumbed end to end - wireTheme field, load bounds row, sparse-write deviation row, settings entry with its read and write cases, plus round-trip, bounds and rejection coverage. Before this a document naming input-radius did not merely go unread, it failed to parse under DisallowUnknownFields. Step 1 stays superseded by the density migration; the release note is filed separately. Step 3 (live gate) is the only remaining item. Widening also found two card-padding deviations, filed as sysc-278 and sysc-279, and a one-pixel control-centre overflow fixed in 4ab5042.

title: sysc-wayland: v0.3.2-rc.1 is tagged on unmerged feat/sessionlock, blocking a final v0.3.2 tag
description:
v0.3.2-rc.1 (2da65cb) sits on feat/sessionlock, which has no PR and was never merged, so it is not on main. Its three commits vendor ext-session-lock-v1, generate the sessionlock bindings, and register sessionlock in release qualification. main meanwhile took 27 commits including three audited client fixes.

The trap: tagging main now would have to be v0.3.3, which numerically outranks the rc while lacking the sessionlock binding, so a consumer resolving by semver silently loses that feature.

The binding is not abandoned. docs/plans/2026-10-04-sysc-lock-parity-audit.md audits exactly that binding at 2da65cb and anticipates a final v0.3.2; bd sysc-974 is live against it. So the fix is to merge feat/sessionlock to main first and then tag v0.3.2, giving one linear history. Until then the pin bump has to use a pseudo-version.

Owner decision on 2026-10-05 was to leave sessionlock alone and tag nothing, so the pin bump landed as a commit pin instead.

title: Keep concurrently enabled plugins during startup sync
description: Concurrent plugin sync can stop a plugin enabled by a newer config if an older sync finishes afterward. Reproduce by pausing plugin A after runtime startup, enabling plugin B in a second sync, then resuming A; the stale first pass drops B. Re-read the committed enabled set when reconciling removals and cover the overlap with a focused regression test.

title: Drain in-flight plugin startups during host shutdown
description: If the shell shuts down while pluginHost.ensure is in its launch handshake, Close can cancel the shared host context before the runtime is inserted and stopped cleanly. Wait for queued reconciliations and active starts to finish before canceling the host context; a regression test must verify HostShutdown reaches a plugin whose startup is delayed.

title: sysc-compositor: FocusWindow leaves mapped offscreen windows unfocused
description: M4 follow-up found during PR #17 review. Reproduction in a nested compositor: map two weston-terminal windows, move the target center outside the output, then call FocusWindow(target.id). It returns true but keyboardFocusedView() is not the target. Root cause: focusView passes outputNameAt(viewCenter) to setActiveOutputName; an offscreen center resolves to empty and preserves the prior active output. updateKeyboardFocus then rejects the window because outputNameAt(center) differs from that active output. Meanwhile the M4 Niri snapshot assigns offscreen windows to the focused output. A temporary named nested regression test reproduced this on 2026-10-20 and was removed from the merged worktree.
acceptance_criteria: Add a permanent focused regression for an offscreen-center mapped target. Make FocusWindow and the Niri snapshot use consistent output fallback semantics, preserve layer keyboard priority and ordinary on-output focus, then verify with named internal/wlr and internal/server checks.

title: Live Niri gate: verify recorder exits on shell SIGTERM
description: Verify PR #352 on live Niri: start a recording, send SIGTERM to the mapped sysc-shell, and confirm sysc-plugin-screen-recorder and its gpu-screen-recorder child both exit without manual cleanup. Record process IDs and journal output. Use scripts/deploy from a clean worktree if deployment is needed.
acceptance_criteria: After shell SIGTERM, the plugin and gpu-screen-recorder exit within the configured shutdown budget; no recorder process remains orphaned.

title: sysc-lock: reduce residual frozen backdrop redraw CPU

title: DND notifications replay after the centre closes
description:
Reproduced on the desktop on 2026-10-20 with sysc-shell ca2e724, sysc-notify v0.1.1, and sysc-tray v0.1.2.

Steps: Open the notification centre, turn on DND, and send a notification. The centre records it and shows no toast. Turn DND off while the centre stays open, then close the centre. The same notification appears as a toast on both outputs.

Expected: keep notifications received during DND in the centre without replaying them after DND clears.

Likely source: internal/shell/toasthost.go, toastHost.recompute. It hides active records while DND or the centre is open, then displays them when both close.

Evidence: /tmp/sysc-m5-dnd-center-record-crop.png, /tmp/sysc-m5-dnd-off-dp1.png, /tmp/sysc-m5-dnd-off-dp3.png.

title: sysc-terminal: CPU blur kernel costs ~12 ms/frame at 3440x1440 and forces the 8.3 FPS blur cadence
description: GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-terminal/issues/30 (tracked there; evidence and numbers live in the issue). Audited origin/main f3557d0. internal/raster/blur.go:79-83 runs 3 rounds of H+V sliding box blur (6 passes) on the quarter-size image regardless of radius; boxBlur (:97-123) does per-pixel LittleEndian []byte access with edge clamps in the inner loop and a column-strided vertical pass. Recorded blur-64 vs blur-0 delta ~12-13 ms/frame at 3440x1440 (artwork-motion qualification :86-93); isolated benchmark 21.9 ms/op with 0 allocs, 77% in the box passes, radius-independent. The <25% one-core budget is why surface.go:116-121 clamps blur ticks to 120 ms, so loops run 2.4x slower with blur on. Fix: fewer passes, 8x downsample at radius>=32, tightened loops; then revisit the 120 ms blur cadence. Effect timing (sysc-1012) is out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: SYSC_BLUR_BUDGET=64 TestWallpaperFrameBudget delta <= 6 ms mean at 3440x1440/491x90 on archPC; blur_test passes plus new benchmark; no visible regression at radius 16/64; if met, raise blur tick to the fastest rate under 25% CPU on desktop and laptop and update README.

title: sysc-lock: GPU effect path blocks on glFinish + synchronous full-frame glReadPixels + CPU flip/swizzle every frame
description: GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-lock/issues/63 (tracked there; evidence lives in the issue). Audited origin/master 863f92e. internal/lockd/effect_gpu.go Draw calls glFinish (:439) before glReadPixels (:455), which already syncs; readback is synchronous into Go memory and flipRGBAToBGRA (:488-499) makes two whole-frame CPU passes (row flip plus R/B swap). The padded-stride fallback swizzles byte by byte (:464-480). This all runs under glMu on a LockOSThread worker. Baseline from sysc-1038: fire/GPU 18.64% of one core at 20 FPS, 1080p, Intel UHD 620 GBM (passes the <=25% gate); the readback share is not measured yet. Fix order: drop the redundant glFinish; flip and swizzle in the shader (or GL_BGRA_EXT); double-buffered PBO + fence; dmabuf export only with a separate design.
acceptance_criteria: Profile the readback/swizzle share before changing anything; effect_gpu_test orientation/colour/odd-height/stride tests pass; live gate (sysc-1038 method) mean CPU below 18.64%, RSS <=128 MiB; any PBO path falls back to sync when unsupported.

title: sysc-wayland: ReadMsg allocates a 1 KiB oob buffer per recvmsg (6 allocs / 3.5 KB garbage per pointer report, ~0.8 GC/s at 1 kHz)
description: GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-wayland/issues/36 (tracked there; evidence and numbers live in the issue). Audited origin/main c328f3e (v0.3.2). client/event.go:119 allocates make([]byte, oobSpace) (1040 B) on every recvmsg, and :60 makes an 8-byte header, with 2 recvmsg per bodied event. Socketpair benchmark of motion+frame: 2.0-2.3 us, 3488 B, 6 allocs/op; 60 s @1 kHz = 210 MB garbage, 49 GC. A prototype with a Context-owned hdr+oob gets 16 B, 1 alloc/op, 0 GC.

title: sysc-notify: history commit re-reads, re-hashes and PNG-decodes every retained image sidecar on each mutation
description: Filed as https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-notify/issues/61 (perf medium, audited at da7068b). Store.commit (internal/history/store.go:444) calls writeImage for every retained image, and for an existing sidecar writeImage runs loadImage (image.go:115-125), which does ReadFile + sha256 + png.Decode only to compare bytes already in memory. AddPrepared also deep-copies all image bytes (store.go:300) and trimToBudget re-hashes every image (store.go:326). Measured with a full 100-entry image history: ~20 ms CPU, 17 MiB allocated, 104 openat / 196 read / 5 fsync per closed notification, against 0.26 ms / 0.1 MiB without images. Fix plan, benchmarks and acceptance thresholds are in the GH issue.

title: sysc-metrics: ProcessSampler allocates a 64 KiB scanner buffer per process per sample (47.5 MB, ~14 GCs, ~41 ms CPU per sample)
description: GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-metrics/issues/52 (perf high, tracked there; evidence and numbers live in the issue). Audited origin/main d1c8769. process_linux.go:85 parseProcessStatus does scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 64*1024), ...) once per process per sample, with strings.Fields on every status line. On archPC (640 procs) a sample costs 47.5 MB / 82.6k allocs / ~14.5 GC cycles / ~41 ms CPU / ~19k syscalls. The same 64 KiB buffer appears at 10 more sites (CPUSampler 1.22 MB/sample, NetworkSampler 933 KB/sample). A Buffer(nil, max) prototype gives 7.8 MB per process sample.

title: sysc-metrics: GPUSampler fork/execs nvidia-smi on every sample (~24.5 ms CPU per sample)
description: GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-metrics/issues/53 (perf medium, tracked there; evidence and numbers live in the issue). Audited origin/main d1c8769. gpu_linux.go:130-137 calls runNvidiaSMI (:375-382), a fresh exec, on every readGPUs. On archPC (RTX 4060, persistence mode on) that is ~24.5 ms CPU and ~26-28 ms wall per sample, against ~2.5 ms/sample for a long-lived nvidia-smi -lms child. The 400 ms timeout and dGPU wakeups stay accepted design.

title: sysc-metrics: pci.ids (1.67 MB) re-read and split on every sample per GPU (4.08 MB, 894 allocs, ~1.2 ms)
description: GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-metrics/issues/54 (perf medium, tracked there; evidence and numbers live in the issue). Audited origin/main d1c8769. gpu_linux.go:90 calls lookupPCIName per card per sample, and that (:235-269) runs os.ReadFile on the whole pci.ids plus strings.Split into 43k lines. On archPC this is 4.08 MB / 894 allocs / ~1.2 ms per GPU per sample (~1.5 GC cycles), 97% of GPU sampler bytes. A memoised prototype gives ~70 KB/sample.

title: sysc-plugins: mini-docker runs docker ps -a every 5 s with no panel open (~57 ms CPU per poll incl dockerd, ~1.2% of a core)
description: GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-plugins/issues/204 (perf medium, tracked there; evidence and numbers live in the issue). Audited origin/main ec01075. cmd/sysc-plugin-mini-docker/main.go:158-185 refreshes containers every interval (default 5 s, main.go:60) regardless of open views. docker.go:127 spawns docker ps -a each time. With no panel open, only the bar icon (availability) and the tooltip running count are shown. Live on archPC: 0.27 s client plus 0.50 s dockerd CPU per minute (~1.3% of a core, 720 spawns per hour). Fix: a docker events stream, a 60 s safety poll when no panel is open, and the configured interval only while the panel is open.

title: sysc-plugins: protonvpn polls protonvpn status (~1.3 s CPU per call) every 5 s while connected, ~26% of a core
description: GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-plugins/issues/203 (perf medium, tracked there; evidence and numbers live in the issue). Audited origin/main ec01075. cmd/sysc-plugin-protonvpn/main.go:429-443 keeps the status interval at refresh_seconds (default 5) whenever proton0 is present; #159 only floored the disconnected case to 30 s. A counting test over 3600 ticks gives 720 status spawns per hour while connected. Each protonvpn status costs ~1.30 s CPU on archPC, so ~936 s per hour (~26% of a core). The /sys traffic read (1 s) and nmcli link probe (2 s) already detect disconnects. Fix: 60 s connected floor plus an immediate poll on the proton0-gone edge.

title: sysc-shell: plugin view Preparer ticks at 30 Hz forever, about 160 idle wakeups/s
description:
GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-shell/issues/372
The Preparer's free-running 30 Hz ticker (internal/plugin/prepare.go:167-179) broadcasts to its workers even with no pending jobs or plugins, raising idle wakeups from ~5/s to ~163/s.

title: gSlapper wildcard coalescing when every output shares one video
description: v1 fans out one process per connector and never uses gSlapper '*'. Coalesce identical All-outputs video into one wildcard process only after a measurement on two outputs.

title: sysc-shell: StrokeRounded blends every pixel of the stroked rectangle (~20% of panel frames)
description:
GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-shell/issues/373
StrokeRounded (internal/render/canvas.go:489-491) runs blendMask over the full ring mask although under 1.5% of pixels are covered; a pixel-identical banded blend makes Settings and control-centre frames ~17-25% faster at 2x.

title: sysc-shell: plugin Preparer 30 Hz ticker wakes two workers forever when idle (~157 wakeups/s, ~2.4 ms CPU/s)
description: GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-shell/issues/374 (perf medium, tracked there; evidence and numbers live in the issue). Audited origin/main 5323fc7 (re-checked 012e431). internal/plugin/prepare.go:101/167-179 starts an unconditional time.NewTicker(publishInterval=1/30 s) that Broadcasts to both workers (pluginhost.go:151 NewPreparer(2)) for the whole session; idle Preparer measured at 1,619 vs 45 voluntary ctx switches and 24.7 ms vs 0.34 ms CPU per 10 s. Fix: arm a one-shot timer only while a rate-gated view waits.

title: sysc-shell: pluginHost.inputs logs every plugin input event forever (218 B/event retained, 20.8 MiB per 100k events)
description: GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-shell/issues/375 (perf medium, tracked there; evidence and numbers live in the issue). Audited origin/main 5323fc7 (re-checked 012e431). internal/shell/pluginhost.go:104 inputs []v1.InputEvent is appended at 9 sites (pluginhost.go:206/539/1009/1545/1660/1698/1989, pluginsurface.go:245) and never truncated; its only reader lastInputs() (:1717) is test-only. Measured 100,000 delivered submits -> len 100,000, +20.8 MiB heap after GC. Fix: test-only recorder behind an option.

title: sysc-shell: icon Resolver rescans the theme tree on every lookup (~1,400 stats, 3-5 ms on archPC) and never caches misses
description: GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-shell/issues/376 (perf medium, tracked there; evidence and numbers live in the issue). Audited origin/main 5323fc7 (re-checked 012e431). internal/icons/theme.go:140-291 re-reads index.theme and walks every size/category dir with per-extension stats on each Resolve (archPC: ~1,395 stats/166 getdents/123 opens, 2.96-3.33 ms per resolve; 350 desktop icon names, 89 misses, 4.81 ms/name; box bench 2.0 ms, 823 KB, 10.1k allocs/op). worker.go:153-164 stores no negative result, so launcher/tray/notification rebuilds re-walk every missing icon. Fix: per-theme index with mtime invalidation plus a TTL miss cache.

title: sysc-shell: tray stale-item retry deadlocks on Registry.mu (ApplyTray -> reprojectTray)
description:
GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-shell/issues/368
ApplyTray holds Registry.mu; the ErrorStaleItem retry path calls reprojectTray, which locks Registry.mu again, freezing the shell. Verified at tip 5323fc7c: the issue's test fails with 'did not return' / 'could not acquire r.mu'. sysc-tray v0.1.2 does emit ErrorStaleItem.
notes: Working in worktree /home/nomadx/sysc-shell/.worktrees/fix-sysc-1484-tray-stale-reply on branch fix/sysc-1484-tray-stale-reply. Repro confirmed failing on origin/main 012e4319; Option A fix (tracker decides, never acts) drafted.

title: sysc-greet: greetd conversation handles only one auth_message; info/fingerprint/OTP stacks can never log in
description: authenticate() in cmd/sysc-greet/main.go answers the first greetd auth_message with the password regardless of auth_message_type and rejects any further auth_message as 'expected success or error', so PAM stacks with an info/error notice or a second prompt (pam_fprintd, pam_u2f, TOTP, expired password) fail even with the correct password. Verified against real greetd 0.10.3 on the box with a pam_echo+pam_exec stack at master 6e39e38; no tests cover the greetd conversation. Fails closed (no bypass). GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-greet/issues/111

title: sysc: Niri binds spawn bare sysc-shell, which a stock Arch session PATH cannot find in ~/.local/bin
description: The installer puts sysc-shell in ~/.local/bin (internal/install/install.go:127) but writes Mod+Space/Mod+Comma binds in sysc.kdl as spawn "sysc-shell" (internal/niri/niri.go:27-28). Niri resolves spawn through its own PATH, which on stock Arch (greetd source_profile with /etc/profile, default skel, niri-session import-environment) omits ~/.local/bin, so both keybinds silently fail while the units still start through their absolute ExecStart. Fix: spawn "~/.local/bin/sysc-shell" (niri expands a leading ~) or an absolute path from BinDir. GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc/issues/68

title: sysc-shell: unleased media bus pump stalls; godbus parks one goroutine per session-bus signal
description: With no media lease, sessionBus.emit (internal/services/media_bus.go:135) blocks once 32 MPRIS events fill changes; the pump stops reading and godbus v5.2.2 spawns a blocked goroutine per matching session-bus signal (all PropertiesChanged/NameOwnerChanged). Probe at 012e4319: +6,137 goroutines after 6,000 signals, drained on re-Acquire. Fix: non-blocking emit with overflow flag and re-enumerate. GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-shell/issues/377

title: sysc-shell: forced plugin stop kills only the plugin PID; spawned helpers orphaned
description: plugin.Supervisor (internal/plugin/supervisor.go:164) starts plugins in the shell/niri process group with default CommandContext cancel; grace expiry (:439), handshake reap (:211) and ctx cancel kill only the main PID, so descendants are reparented and keep running after disable/restart/shell exit. Probe at 012e4319: child alive, ppid=subreaper. Generalises sysc-1362 (PR #352 only widened grace). Fix: Setpgid + group SIGTERM/SIGKILL on forced paths only. GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-shell/issues/378

title: sysc-shell: media art negative cache never expires; transient failure blanks cover for the session
description: mediaArtWorker.failed (internal/shell/mediaart.go:38) records every failed art key incl. 5xx and watchdog timeouts (:174, :189) and is never deleted; Request (:114) then skips the key forever, contrary to the :101 comment. Probe at 012e4319: 503-then-200 URL never refetched (hits=1); 2,000 distinct 404s -> 2,001 entries. Fix: time-stamped entries with retry window and a size cap. GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-shell/issues/379

title: sysc-shell: notification image-data replaced by desktop-entry icon after first frame

title: sysc-shell: plugin settings mask only _api_key suffix; steamgriddb_key shown in plain text
description: popout_plugins.go:345 suffix-only masking, no secret flag in manifest schema; games steamgriddb_key unmasked. GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-shell/issues/381

title: sysc-walls: findDisplayBinary misses ~/.local/bin (sysc install layout)
description: Daemon/client lookup only PATH,/usr/bin,/usr/local/bin,./; sysc installs to ~/.local/bin and unit sets no PATH -> no screensaver. GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-walls/issues/70

title: sysc-shell: plugin death undetected while a spawned child holds its stdout; stays Running as zombie, never restarted, Disable stalls 4 s
description: The plugin supervisor learns that a plugin process has died only from EOF on its stdout pipe (internal/plugin/supervisor.go:375-397). Nothing waits on the process during the session. If a plugin spawns a child that inherits stdout (any script entry point running 'cmd &'), the pipe stays open after the plugin exits. The runtime then stays StateRunning with a zombie PID, never enters the restart budget (runtime.go:406-412, 455-501), and Disable/Retry blocks for the full 4 s WaitDelay grace (supervisor.go:178, 429-442). Verified at 012e4319 (v0.2.0-229-g012e4319) with a probe: state=running starts=1 with the PID in Z state 3 s after exit, and disable took 4.003 s. The control run without a child ends failed starts=3. Fix: a waitid(WNOWAIT) exit watcher closes stdout, supervise treats that as end of session, and shutdown skips the grace when the process is already gone. Killing the leftover descendants is #378. GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-shell/issues/382

title: internal/shell tests can hang forever: publishSurface blocks when the cap-8 invalidations buffer fills
description:
CI run 39481720142 (PR #383, head 9f8e9055) failed with 'panic: test timed out after 10m0s' for package internal/shell. The goroutine dump shows (*Registry).publishSurface (internal/shell/panelhost.go:5089) blocked in its select for 7m50s, reached from PrepareConfigWithGeneration's Commit closure (internal/shell/registry.go:2371) by TestEdgeReloadRetainsOpenPanels (internal/shell/panelhost_test.go:1725). No tray frame is involved: the hang is in the config-reload publish path that PR #383 does not touch.

Mechanism: Registry.invalidations is make(chan wayland.Invalidation, 8) (internal/shell/registry.go:500). publish (internal/shell/registry.go:1731) and publishSurface (internal/shell/panelhost.go:5089) block when the buffer is full; only r.closed unblocks them. In production the Wayland owner bridge drains the channel continuously; internal/shell tests have no owner, so nothing drains it.

Measured on origin/main 012e4319: TestEdgeReloadRetainsOpenPanels publishes 7 invalidations (6 x publishSurface + 1 x publish[7]), leaving exactly one slot of headroom. One extra bar republish and the next send blocks that test forever. The fixture helper keepInvalidationsDrained (internal/shell/panelhost_test.go:2215) exists for this; the edge-reload fixtures do not use it.

Fix: drain the channel in the affected fixtures (keepInvalidationsDrained), or make the publish path non-blocking under runningAsTest() so a full buffer drops instead of hanging the suite. Acceptance: the internal/shell package cannot block on a full invalidations buffer, and repeated CI runs of the edge-reload tests are stable.

title: Registry.Close() writes r.plugins without Registry.mu while viewLocked() reads it under the lock (data race)
description:
Confirmed by the race detector in a local 'go test -race -count=1 ./internal/shell/' run on branch fix/sysc-1484-tray-deadlock-20261021 (log: /tmp/opencode/sysc1484-test.log). The race report: Read at 0x00c0aeddfbd8 by goroutine 133165 in (*Registry).viewLocked() (internal/shell/registry.go:2963, 'view.Plugins = r.plugins.frames(connector)'), reached through settingsBarImage -> paintSettingsBar -> settingsPictureCards -> settingsCardsFor -> settingsBarPage -> settingsTree -> panelTree -> rebuildPanel -> scheduleControlResult.func1 (internal/shell/popout_audio.go:685); Previous write at the same address by goroutine 2834 in (*Registry).Close() (internal/shell/registry.go:2563, 'r.plugins = nil').

Close() nils r.plugins outside Registry.mu while a panel render reads it under Registry.mu. Once the detector fires, every test running at that moment fails, which is how a single race turned into 25 failing internal/shell tests locally. Fix: take r.mu for the teardown write (or move the plugin teardown into the locked section and keep the pointer stable until the renderers are quiesced). Acceptance: 'go test -race -count=1 ./internal/shell/' is clean, and Close() cannot write r.plugins concurrently with a render.

title: internal/ipc race-detects under a full-parallel repo test run
description: At 0eb39ae8, 'go test -race -count=1 ./...' at default package parallelism failed internal/ipc with 13 'race detected during execution' failures (TestServerRoundTrip, TestListenReplacesAStaleSocket, TestPanel*Dispatches, ...). The same package passes in isolation (3.9 s) and the full run passes with -p 2. internal/ipc does not import internal/icons, so this is not a regression from sysc-1483. Likely a test goroutine shared across subtests or socket timing; find with 'go test -race -count=1 ./...' at default -p and read the race report.

title: internal/lock: TestBusUnavailableBacksOff fails intermittently under a loaded -race run
description:
Found while running go test -race ./... on 2026-10-21. TestBusUnavailableBacksOff (internal/lock/backoff_test.go:261) failed once in a full-suite run and once in 5 isolated runs, then passed 12 consecutive runs (6 isolated + 6 whole-package). The package is untouched by the change under test, so this is a pre-existing flake.

Mechanism (from the test source): swapSeams replaces the bus factory, which always fails, and the backoff timer factory, which records each wait into a cap-8 channel and returns time.After(0). The reconnect loop therefore dials as fast as the scheduler allows while the test reads a strict 8-step duration sequence. The timer factory parks the loop on a nil channel once the buffer is full, so any extra or reordered wait fails the comparison.

Not yet characterised: the failing assertion text was not captured before the run ended. Next step is to capture the failure output by running the package under load, then decide between widening the waits channel, asserting on a prefix, or synchronising the park with the reader.
acceptance_criteria: The test is stable across 20 consecutive -race runs of the package under load, and its expectation still proves the backoff sequence.

title: Network service, panel and wifi widget
description: Replace the control centre Network disabled destination with a native Niri-first Wi-Fi and wired status/control page. Requires a separately approved NetworkManager ownership and secret-agent design; do not shell out from UI handlers.
notes:
LANDED ON MAIN 2026-09-14 at merge commit 2576e14.

Closed against the code stop condition, not the live one. Every automated gate passed before merging: the merge was conflict-free against main, the merged tree passed internal/shell, theme, config, settings, services, ui and render, the merged binary built, and it was deployed to the live Niri laptop where it started clean, logged zero errors over ten minutes, and painted the bar with the Wi-Fi glyph rendering. The five P1 defects are closed: sysc-257, sysc-258, sysc-263, sysc-264 and sysc-266, the last of those being the laptop gate itself.

The live credential gate (plan Task 12) was deliberately deferred by owner decision rather than run, because it needs a real secured network and the radio. It is filed as sysc-268 (P1) with its prerequisites and acceptance criteria, so it is tracked rather than lost. This issue is closed so sysc-155 stops being dependency-blocked; the concurrent Bluetooth session was stalled waiting for the network implementation to exist on main.

Two known gaps stay open and do not depend on this issue: sysc-254 (no forget affordance, deliberately not invented in this slice) and sysc-267 (slow shutdown, visible in the restart logs as the gSlapper helper reaching its kill timeout). The header Down/Up dash decision is recorded on sysc-268.

title: Color emoji paints as notdef boxes
description: Toast (and any other text) shows tofu for emoji. This machine's only covering face is Noto Color Emoji (CBDT bitmaps from noto-fonts-emoji). FontMap.outlineFaceForRune rejects non-outline GlyphData and falls back to the primary face, which draws .notdef. TextRenderer only rasterises vector outlines into an alpha mask that paint.go later tints, so a color PNG/COLR blit does not fit that path. Observed live: 👋 U+1F44B and 🗞 U+1F5DE in notification bodies. Design deferred color emoji past M2. Fix is a color glyph blit beside Mask.Alpha, not a family tweak.

title: Chrome catalogue live Niri gate: pointer-driven checks
description:
Live gate for sysc-141, run 2026-09-03 on baremetal Niri (DP-1 3440x1440 + DP-3 2560x1440, both scale 1.0).

RAN AND PASSED: panel.toggle/open/close over IPC; niri msg -j layers shows sysc-shell-panel and sysc-shell-shield mapping on open with Exclusive keyboard interactivity and unmapping cleanly on close with no leftover surface; selected profile segment moves across performance/balanced/power-saver with no label clipping and swaps its profile icon for the check; destructive Reboot and Power off render as error-toned outlines; Lock correctly absent because config.Session.Locker is empty; resting, selected and keyboard-focus states captured by grim.

FOUND AND FIXED during the gate (commit 48c5d02): KindSegmented had no paint case, so opening the power panel killed the shell with 'unsupported kind 17'; and measureSegmented summed segment widths while layoutSegmented allocates them equally, under-measuring the row.

NOT RUN, needs a pointer or keyboard at the machine: right-click battery with left-click inert; hover and pressed state capture; Escape and outside-click closing; Super+X keybind (IPC equivalent was exercised instead). The shell IPC exposes only status, panel.toggle/open/close and osd.step, so it cannot synthesise pointer or key events.

NOT APPLICABLE on this hardware: battery card (desktop, no battery). Two-output case IS now runnable and the bar mapped on both outputs.

STILL OPEN from the plan: theme apply (valid light/dark, invalid, reduced motion) crossfade/retention/snap was not exercised live.

title: sysc-76 and sysc-125 are the same issue with one content hash
description:
Both records carry title "M6A Tasks 6-9 remain: attach plugin views to shell owners", the same description, the same created_at (2026-09-02 04:18) and the same content_hash 76f700ed. sysc-76 is in_progress with no dependencies; sysc-125 is closed and holds the depends-on edge to sysc-65. They are one issue that a past collision remap duplicated.

Consequence: any rebuild of beads.db from .beads/issues.jsonl silently drops one of them. 'bd import' reports "1 skipped" and the next 'bd sync --flush-only' writes a JSONL with 151 records instead of 152, so a commit made from a freshly built database commits the loss. This is how it surfaced: a worktree whose beads.db had to be recreated could not commit without dropping an issue.

Fix is to decide which record survives and delete or re-describe the other so the hashes differ. Whoever decides also settles whether M6A tasks 6-9 are done, since the two disagree on status.

D4's chrome calls for a folder strip (selector, not tiles). The M7 panel navigates
within the first library root only, so with the default two roots
(~/Pictures/Wallpapers and ~/Videos/Wallpapers) the video root is unreachable
from the picker.

Found by the 2026-09-04 live gate: the video had to be applied through the
engine directly. Recorded in tests/integration/README.md under Not covered here.

Fix: add the folder/root strip from D4 above the grid, listing each configured
root plus the current directory's children.

Shipped panel has the grid but not D4/D6/D7 controls: no title/close, no output
select, no All/Images/Videos filter, no Up, no folder strip, no Pause/Resume or

Also: gslapper maps a Background surface and reports playing while a competing

title: Brightness control reports unavailable on hardware with a backlight
description: sysc-shell ipc osd.step {"kind":"brightness","action":"up"} returns "brightness unavailable" on archThink, which has /sys/class/backlight with a live value (24242). Audio on the same machine works after the wpctl suffix fix. Found while retiring the DMS keybinds: the brightness keys are the one pair with no working sysc-shell equivalent, so they were left pointing at dms. Start at services.Brightness.Available and how the device path is resolved.

title: Named colour-scheme palettes as a theme source
description: Named palettes cover the ten DMS built-ins and ten Noctalia built-ins. Noctalia values are canonical for overlapping palettes, and existing palette IDs/config shape remain stable. Eldritch uses upstream Cthulhu in dark mode and Dusk in light mode; upstream Abyss is available as eldritch-abyss. RAMA uses sysc-greet source colors in both modes because it has no light variant. DMS Monochrome is included. Void uses sysc-greet dark pure-black colors in both modes. Community downloading remains in sysc-712.
design: Palettes resolve to theme.Tokens and reuse the existing contrast validation. Noctalia caches downloaded palettes under ~/.local/state; a first cut can compile them in, since the fallback tables already establish that shape.
acceptance_criteria: The palette selector includes every DMS and Noctalia built-in plus eldritch-abyss, rama and void. Existing IDs/config remain valid. Every palette resolves complete and contrast-valid tokens in dark/light and normal/high-contrast modes through the current resolver. RAMA, Void and Eldritch Abyss use their source colors in both modes. Wallpaper, hex, and stock sources remain unchanged. Tests assert catalog coverage, representative source anchors, completeness and contrast.

title: External application theming, opt-in, with DMS parity
description:
sysc-shell writes no application theme files at all today. DankMaterialShell did, which is the parity gap: it wrote kitty, GTK, Qt and browser CSS from its palette.

Build that export, but opt-in per target rather than on by default. Nothing outside the shell should be rewritten because a wallpaper changed, unless the user asked for that target specifically. This came out of a real incident: DMS flipped isLightMode on a schedule and silently rewrote kitty to a light palette, and the cause took a long time to find precisely because the writes were invisible and unattributed.

Targets to cover for parity: kitty, GTK 3/4, Qt5ct/Qt6ct, terminal window borders, and browser CSS.
design: sysc-shell already writes ~/.cache/sysc-shell/colors.json, which is the same shape Noctalia uses as its export seam (~/.config/noctalia/colors.json plus user templates). Prefer templates over hardcoded per-app writers so a user can add a target without a code change. Each target needs an explicit enable, a recorded output path, and a way to see what was written.
acceptance_criteria: No file outside sysc-shell's own directories is written unless that target is explicitly enabled; enabling a target writes it and records where; disabling stops future writes and leaves the last output in place.
notes:
Correction after reading the tree: external application theming already EXISTS as internal/theming, and is already opt-in per target. It ships 16 templates (kitty, gtk3, gtk4, qt, alacritty, foot, ghostty, wezterm, niri, starship, btop, cava, emacs, helix, kcolorscheme, scroll) and settings exposes a theme.templates.<name> switch for each. An earlier note here said no export existed; that was wrong.

What was actually missing is now fixed under sysc-176 task 12: the template context exported 11 of the 49 roles from a hand-written list, so a template naming a secondary, an error container or any fixed accent silently rendered nothing, and Mode was pinned to dark. The context is built from the palette's own role table now, with mode and source metadata.

Remaining scope for this issue is therefore narrower than filed: audit the shipped templates against the full role set now that they can reach it, and compare the target list against what DankMaterialShell wrote (it also produced firefox and zen browser CSS, which have no template here).

title: Tranche 4A implementation: panel foundation
description: 14 tasks in docs/plans/2026-08-30-panel-foundation.md. Blocked by the two review blockers, and by M2 corrections and tranche 3A per its own prerequisites.

title: Launcher browse list was capped at 50 entries
description:
The empty-query browse list arrived capped, so it stopped in the E's. sysc-launch's rank applies resultLimit=50 to every query; with an empty query every entry scores 0, the sort collapses to alphabetical, and the first 50 survive. Measured on the desktop: index 49 was 'Eye of GNOME', and 'Faugus' at index 50 was the first entry silently dropped. 199 visible entries were showing as 50.

Fixed in sysc-shell by injecting launcher.ServiceConfig.Rank (internal/shell/launcher_rank.go): the search cap is kept, the browse list is left whole. The ranker is a copy of the library's, pinned against the original by TestLauncherRankMatchesLibraryForSearches so search order cannot drift.

title: Held keys do not repeat: no client-side repeat timer
description:
wl_keyboard.repeat_info names a rate and delay once, and the compositor then sends exactly one key event per physical press; synthesising the rest is the client's job. niri never sends KeyboardKeyStateRepeated, and there was no repeat_info handler and no timer, so a held Down moved one row and a held Backspace deleted one character in every panel.

UPDATE 2026-09-06: implemented and landed in f755eea. The owner goroutine's poll deadline carries the repeat timer; repeatTimeout returns -1 when idle, fireRepeat delivers at most one synthetic press per pass, modifiers are exempt by evdev code, and repeat stops on release, on leave, and on capability loss. Unit tests in internal/platform/wayland/keyrepeat_test.go pass. Niri config confirms repeat-delay 600 / repeat-rate 25 so the path will engage.

STILL OPEN because it has not been confirmed with a real held keypress. wtype cannot be used to drive the panel: attaching a virtual keyboard drops the exclusive grab and dismisses it. Needs a human to hold Down in the launcher.

title: Launcher usage boost has no frequency signal past its caps
description:
Measured with a crafted history through the real ranker:

  boost= 25  used 200x today
  boost= 25  used  10x 5 days ago
  boost= 25  used 200x 5 days ago
  boost=  1  used 200x 11 days ago
  boost=  1  used 200x 40 days ago
  boost=  1  used   1x 11 days ago
  boost=  1  used   1x 40 days ago

Two flattenings. historyAmountCap=10 saturates the open count, then usageBoostCap=25 clamps the product, so anything opened a handful of times recently is indistinguishable. Then base = 10 - ageDays goes non-positive at 10 days and max(base*amount,1) collapses everything older to exactly 1: a daily driver used 200 times ranks level with something opened once last month, and the tie falls back to alphabetical.

The mechanism itself works -- 9 entries carry a boost on the desktop today and they do sort above the alphabetical run. This is the shape of the curve, not the wiring. Changing it is a behaviour change in sysc-launch, shared with its own consumers, so it needs agreement before shipping.

title: Panel corners composite as black: opaque region ignores the radius
description:
Every panel in the shell claimed its whole rectangle was opaque, including the rounded corners.

internal/platform/wayland/aux.go applyAuxRegions passed a hardcoded radius of 0 to applyOpaqueRegion. With radius 0, opaqueRects returns the full body rect, so the compositor was told it could skip blending the corners. The painter meanwhile does clear(c.Pix) and fills a *rounded* body, so those corner pixels are genuinely transparent -- composited unblended they come out pure black behind the border.

Measured on the desktop at the launcher panel's top-left corner arc:
  before: 32 of 78 pixels pure #000000
  after :  0 of 78, every corner pixel identical to the desktop behind it

The bar was never affected: applyHostRegions already passes policy.Radius. Theme.Radius's own doc comment says it 'rounds the body's corners and shapes the opaque region' -- the aux path just never received it.

Fixed by adding HostCallbacks.Radius, set from h.theme.Radius in panelSpec, and using it in both applyAuxRegions branches. Surfaces that do not set OpaqueBackground get no opaque region at all and were never affected. Regression test: TestPanelSurfaceCarriesItsCornerRadius.

title: Startup errors are swallowed: deferred registry.Close deadlocks
description:
Any error returned by run() presents as a silent hang with no message, because the deferred registry.Close() at cmd/sysc-shell/main.go:77 blocks forever on r.mu.Lock() at internal/shell/registry.go:725. A goroutine dump taken during the hang shows goroutine 1 parked in Close via deferreturn and no other goroutine holding the mutex, so the lock was leaked on a path that returned while holding it.

Found while diagnosing the wallpaper-widget nil deref (sysc-169). That panic surfaced as 'wayland: second roundtrip: dispatch: panic handling opcode=2 senderID=4: nil pointer dereference' -- but the message never reached the journal, and the shell just sat in futex_do_wait with no Wayland connection, no IPC listener and no bar. It was only recoverable by temporarily converting run() to a named return and logging before Close.

Fixing sysc-169 removed today's trigger; this hides the next one.

Repro: make run() return any error after the registry is constructed, then start the shell. Observe a hang instead of the error.

title: Launcher rows render at half height for some entries
description:
Reported 2026-09-06. In the launcher result list most rows draw at the full 60px slot, but some entries draw at roughly half that. Confirmed by eye on pwvucontrol, sonusmix, rofi, and rofi theme selector; there are likely more.

The list is a KindVirtualList with a fixed ItemHeight of launcherSlotHeight, so every slot is the same size by construction. That means the row content, not the slot, is short: launcherRow builds a capsule per result and something about these particular entries is producing a shorter subtree.

title: Launcher search field: glyph, border, tokens, and text baseline
description:
Design audit raised 2026-09-06, against the Noctalia launcher as reference.

Four defects in one control, all in paintTextField:

1. Typed text sits against the top edge of the well instead of on its midline. paintText draws from the top of the box it is given; invisible while a field was only as tall as its text, obvious now the field is a 56px pill.
2. The magnifier was built from a filled square with a smaller square punched out in the well colour, plus a staircase of 3x3 blocks for the handle. It cannot antialias, and the punch-out assumes a flat well behind it. It also sat 13px from the left edge, inside the curve of the stadium cap, so it read as crowding the corner.
3. The border did not render crisply. It was drawn as a fill of the border colour with a smaller fill laid on top, so the border was the arithmetic difference of two silhouettes quantised to whole pixels, which thins and breaks up around the corners. The same construction was used for the panel's own rim.
4. The field stroked Rim, which is the floating panel's edge token. The field and the panel it sits on drew the same colour, so neither read as deliberate. A field is a control and should carry Outline.

WORK IN PROGRESS on feature/launcher-ui-parity: added RingMask and SearchGlyphMask as antialiased cached masks, routed strokeRoundedRect and the panel rim through the ring, moved the field to Outline, gave the focused field the existing 2px accent focus ring, and added centreLine. Four render tests still need updating to the new geometry.

title: Launcher panel: shadow instead of a drawn rim
description:
Raised 2026-09-06. The launcher currently separates itself from the wallpaper with a 1px rim. The reference (Noctalia) draws no outline at all and relies on a soft shadow.

This is not a paint-only change. panelhost sets style.Body to the full logical surface, so the painted body fills the layer surface edge to edge and a shadow has nowhere to go: it would be clipped at the surface boundary.

Doing it properly means giving the panel surface a transparent margin and insetting the body by the shadow spread, which touches panel sizing, the body rect, the input region, and the opaque region (which must cover only the body, or the compositor will composite the margin as opaque and reintroduce the black corners fixed in sysc-183).

The renderer already has what it needs: Canvas.DrawShadow, ShadowTexture, and theme Elevation/Shadow tokens, currently used only by menus.

Estimate is small but cross-cutting, and it affects every panel, so it wants its own slice rather than being folded into the search field work.

title: Wallpaper picker: let the engine strip choose an engine, not just report one
description:
Raised by the owner 2026-09-06 on the reworked picker: 'there is no default selected.. also clicking on one of the engines does not highlight the button, there is also no hover over effect like with the other buttons'.

The default half is fixed (2885264): Capabilities.EngineFor is now the single statement of which engine an apply uses, the store records it per output in Runtime.Engine, and an output nothing has painted yet reports the engine that would take it, so a pill is always marked.

The clicking half is not, and cannot be without new plumbing. There is no engine override anywhere: gslapperEngine.Apply picks gSlapper whenever caps.GSlapper is set and the static fallback otherwise, and Service.set is fixed at construction, so nothing can express 'use swaybg on DP-1'. Making the pills clickable today would be a control that highlights and changes nothing.

Work, if taken:
- wallpaper.Settings gains an engine preference, honoured by Apply, with the hard constraint that a video can only be gSlapper and a pill for an engine that cannot serve the current assignment must be disabled rather than silently ignored.
- The service needs a way to take new Settings after construction (a Command op), since it currently only ever reads the ones it was built with.
- config.Wallpaper gains the field, with load validation, the write diff, and defaults, so the choice survives a restart like every other picker choice.
- Only then do the pills get Action and Focusable, at which point they pick up hover and press from interaction.apply for free.

Until then the strip is deliberately a readout: Role status, no Action, no Focusable.
acceptance_criteria: An engine chosen in the picker paints the next apply on that output, survives a restart, and a pill that cannot serve the current assignment is visibly disabled rather than inert.

CPU/power case, evidence found 2026-09-13 while scoping the idle run (the run itself is deferred):

archPC's journal records one sysc-shell run consuming 10h 11min 23s of CPU over 23h 2min 8s wall clock, logged at 2026-09-13T14:21:18, so covering roughly 2026-09-12 15:18 to 2026-09-13 14:21. That is about 44 percent of one core sustained for a day. Other long runs on the same era of binary sat far lower: 45min 24s over 22h 38min (3.3 percent) and 44min 26s over 1d 2h 49min (2.8 percent), and 1h 56min over 22h 40min (8.6 percent). The spread matters more than any single figure: something makes this shell burn a core intermittently, and that is exactly the failing case this epic names.

Not yet attributable to a commit. The binary deployed on archPC at the time was a foreign build (mod 77a66f10ce75+dirty, zero screencopy symbols), not the blur or smoothness work.

The idle observation still has to be run. archPC currently has no graphical session at all (greeter only, sysc-shell.service inactive, no niri socket), and the laptop is not reachable from archPC over ssh (publickey denied), so neither machine could host it at the time of writing. Design corrections found live: this Niri offers xrgb8888 only for a region capture, so the captured alpha byte must be filled; a screencopy target's pool must hold exactly one buffer, which newGeneration cannot do; the backdrop must be clipped to the rounded mask or panel corners fill in; and the shell, not the wayland package, assembles the Style for panels, so the image returns through a new HostCallbacks.Backdrop. title: Panel backdrop blur: screencopy binding and blur kernel
description:
Executes docs/plans/2026-09-11-panel-backdrop-blur.md Tasks 1-10 on feature/panel-backdrop-blur, rebased onto main at 79e9899 (which brought the control-centre work in). Eleven commits.

Measured 2026-09-12/13 (go1.27.0, Ryzen 7 5700X, powersave): blur kernel 4.94 ms median against a predicted 4.60, linear at 4.6-5.1 ms/MPix over six panel sizes; screencopy readback 5.67 ms median against D16.1's 15 ms stop threshold; ~11 ms per open, inside one 60 Hz frame.

Design corrections found live, each by measurement rather than reading: this Niri offers xrgb8888 only for a region capture, so the captured alpha byte must be filled; a screencopy target's wl_shm pool must hold exactly one buffer, which newGeneration cannot do (hence newCaptureBuffer); the backdrop must go through the rounded mask or panel corners fill in; the shell, not the wayland package, assembles a panel's Style, so the image returns via a new HostCallbacks.Backdrop; and the panel-opacity bound had to move in three places or the lower floor stayed unreachable from config.

capture_output_region is OUTPUT-RELATIVE, not global: probed directly because this output sits at logical 2560,0. A global-space region is refused with nil, an output-relative one returns real content. D3 assumed this and never verified it.

Post-rebase defect found and fixed (876ca72): main's AttachedPanelStyle resolves an attached panel's root at the BAR's opacity, which is opaque, so an attached panel painted straight over its own backdrop. Caught by measuring a live capture: the Audio panel body was a single flat colour, pixel-identical to the bar fill. rootStyle now keeps the panel's own alpha whenever a backdrop is present, with a regression test.

Verified live on two machines: archPC 3440x1440 scale 1.0 and archThink 1920x1080 scale 1.25 (the first fractional-scale exercise of this path). Blur visible on both; ships off by default.

Six tasks: a pure damage accumulator, per-rectangle damage submission with a full-buffer fallback, a theme-resolved animation frame cap, stopping the wallpaper picker's per-thumbnail tree rebuild, coalescing thumbnail arrivals, and the architecture amendment. Closes the remainder of sysc-202: blur measured the large-blurred-panel case; this covers animation frame time, image-heavy grids and CPU/power.
notes:
Tasks 1-4 complete on feature/rendering-smoothness, branched from main at 127f7aa (post blur merge, so Tasks 2-3 applied without conflict).

71ae0df Task 1: render.DamageSet accumulator, pure, 5 tests.
a0d28c8 Task 2: HostCallbacks.Damaged plus damageRects, clipped to the buffer, full-buffer fallback. Every surface still reports nil, so every surface still damages fully.
98858d8 Task 3: theme.MotionTokens.FrameCap at 33ms, scaled in AtSpeed; animateSurface takes minInterval and always publishes the settling frame. Three callers resolve the cap under their mutex.
6a65808 Task 4: applyWallpaperThumb publishes without rebuilding the panel tree.

Task 5 (coalesce thumbnail arrivals) is BLOCKED as written. Its flush mechanism does not exist: the plan says icons.Worker has a Progress() channel signalling burst completion, but Worker exposes only Lookup, Request, Run and internals, so the final pending publish of a burst could never be flushed and that tile would stay a glyph until an unrelated repaint. The plan also forbids a timer here. Its premise is additionally undercut: publishSurface sends to an 8-deep channel and drops when the owner is behind, and render.Scheduler.Invalidate is a single bool documented as coalescing repeated calls into one redraw, so N arrivals already cost one blit, not N.

Task 6 (retire sysc-202) is BLOCKED: it closes the epic citing every named case measured, but sysc-256's live gates are unrun and the two-output case is unrunnable on either machine.

Two plan defects found and corrected while executing: Task 1's tests were mutually unsatisfiable (a reset DamageSet and a zero-valued one are the same state, yet one assertion demanded Full() and the other not-Full); Task 3 Step 7's git add list omits the three caller files, which would have produced a non-compiling commit.

title: Weather surfaces are unstyled and under-informed: audit and parity pass
description:
Audit 2026-09-15 of every first-party weather presentation against the DMS/Noctalia v4 reference (docs/plans/assets/2026-08-31-bar-visual-parity/refs/noctalia-weather.png).

Presentations today, three sites, all thin:

- Bar widget (widget.go:226, weatherwidget.go): one text run - inline WMO glyph + temperature + optional condition word + stale age. The glyph is text, not an icon node: it inherits text tone and metrics, so sysc-58's advance defect applies to it. The tooltip is the static word "Weather" (textWidget.tooltip is a plain string). No Action is set: clicking does nothing.
- Control centre weather page (controlcenter_pages.go:349 ccWeather): a Today card that presents raw coordinates ("%.2f deg, %.2f deg") as the location plus "Updated 15:04"; below it four 143x132 forecast cards showing day name, glyph and "H / L" only - no condition word, today excluded, count pinned at four.
- No standalone weather panel exists.

Data path (weather/client.go, weather/model.go, internal/services/weather.go): the request carries current=temperature_2m,weather_code and daily=weather_code,max,min,sunrise,sunset for seven days. Open-Meteo also returns, and Decode silently discards, elevation and timezone from the response root; the current block can carry is_day, apparent_temperature, humidity, wind_speed_10m, wind_direction_10m and uv_index; the daily block can carry uv_index_max and precipitation figures. The reference panel shows wind, UV, elevation and a named timezone; none of that is reachable today without extending the wire model.

Vocabulary drift - three copies of the same facts:

- Icon mapping: render/iconfont.go IconRune/IconName (eight WMO glyphs) versus ccWeatherIcon's separate Material ligature set (sunny, partly_cloudy_day, ...) for the same codes.
- Condition words: conditionWords (weatherwidget.go:14), ccWeatherCondition, and the plugin's Condition() are three tables. The plugin's routes through IconName; the shell's two do not agree with each other.
- No night variants: WMO code 0 at night renders a sun; is_day is not fetched.

State handling drift: formatWeather's three-state rule (placeholder / error / stale-with-age) lives in the bar only. ccWeather dashes and "Updated HH:MM" ignore FailedSince, so an aged reading renders identically to a fresh one.

Conformance and collision hazards: ccWeather's geometry (Height 336/480, 132; Width 143; Gap 8/12) sits on the open token-conformance worklist, and the parked feature/noctalia-parity session has controlcenter_pages.go dirty in its worktree. This slice must not re-edit that page's geometry concurrently - sequence the cc page after parity lands or confine this slice to new files.
acceptance_criteria:
- weather.Query/Forecast/Decode extended for current is_day, apparent_temperature, wind speed and direction, humidity, uv_index; daily uv_index_max and precipitation; root elevation, timezone, timezone_abbreviation. Decode stays strict: checked pointer fields, bounded body, table tests for the new fields.
- One icon mapping and one condition-word table shared by the bar, the control-centre page and the tooltip; night variants for clear and partly-cloudy added to the icon subset and selected via is_day.
- The bar weather widget renders a real icon node beside the temperature, opens the weather panel as its Action, and its tooltip carries current facts rather than the literal word "Weather".
- A standalone PanelWeather appended to the PanelID enum after PanelNetwork (the blur coverage walk must see it), composed like the reference: hero card (large glyph, temperature, min/max, condition, configured location name - not coordinates), a details card (feels-like, wind, humidity, UV, sunrise, sunset, elevation, timezone), and the seven-day list with per-day icon, day, range and condition word. Daily only; Hourly is a separate decision with its own wire growth.
- Stale and error states follow formatWeather's three-state rule on every surface; an aged reading looks aged everywhere.
- No new literal geometry: spacing from the margin ladder, control sizes from the density row, shapes from the shape role. The control-centre page's existing literals stay untouched until the parity conversion lands.
- Focused checks per changed unit; gofmt, go vet, and the affected-package gates pass before any commit.

The hourly presentation is intentionally capped at seven rows to match the reference; the panel remains two-column per the recorded amendment; the city-only unresolved fallback retains the configured city label rather than fabricating zero coordinates.

Completed parity slices sysc-287, sysc-288 and sysc-294 are closed.

Proof: GOMAXPROCS=4 go test -p 2 ./weather/ ./internal/services/ ./internal/render/ ./internal/config/ ./internal/theme/ ./internal/shell/ ./internal/plugin/ ./tests/... -count=1; GOMAXPROCS=4 go build -p 2 ./...; GOMAXPROCS=4 go vet -p 2 ./...; gofmt scan; git diff --check; legacy-visual and backdrop scans; night/detail font-ink tests; go.mod/go.sum diff clean.

title: Notification cards pad from a package constant, not the density row
description: notifycard.go:16 defines cardPadding = 12, which matches no ladder rung: the density row's CardPadding is 9 (MarginM) and PanelPadding is 13 (MarginL). Recorded meanwhile in cardPaddingDeviations in surfacerole_test.go; remove the entry when this is fixed.

title: Bar clips overflowing right-side items silently instead of degrading gracefully

Found live on the laptop while verifying the sysc-plugins rebuild (2026-09-16, 1920-wide output).

Reproduce: place enough right-side items to exceed the width (four plugin placements is enough at 1920) and look at the right edge.

Expected: items that do not fit collapse (hide-when-tight behaviour like other shells), move to an overflow slot, or the bar refuses the placement at config load with a diagnostic -- anything but silent clipping. Config load already validates placements; the overflow case needs the same treatment at layout time.
notes: Owned by M9 sub-project C as of 2026-09-17: sysc-322 subsumes this. docs/plans/2026-09-17-bar-geometry-design.md D4 takes overflow because what does not fit is axis-dependent, so it is solved once for all four bar edges rather than fixed horizontally and reopened when the bar turns vertical. D5 is the policy: whole items drop in declaration order from the section's far end behind a visible indicator whose own extent is reserved before selection. Explicitly not refusal at config load, which this issue already rules out because plugin widgets appear and disappear at runtime. Do not fix separately in ui.ArrangeBar; that function is gated on sysc-314.

title: Settings rows overflow the panel's right edge
description:
On a 1536x864 logical output at scale 1.25 the settings pane clips every trailing control at the right edge: the enum pills (wallpaper, catppuccin, dark, standard, mini) are cut mid-word and the appearance.seed field runs past the viewport. Reproduced live on the laptop, twice, with screenshots.

Giving the scroll column an explicit width (panel - 2*PanelPadding - rail - MarginXL), mirroring ccBodyWidth, improved it but did not close it, so a row is still measuring wider than the column. The likely cause is the label column: Entry.Describe renders as a single unwrapped text node, so a long description forces the row wide and pushes the right-pinned control past the edge. Wrapping the caption to the label column's available width is the thing to check first.

Not visible on a 3440x1440 output at scale 1.0, which is why the per-package tests and the first live gate both passed. Found by M9 sub-project A's live check on a second machine.

title: Plugin cards do not use the settings row anatomy
description:
The Plugins section renders the plugin host's own composition: a meta line, an enable switch, a Retry button, then per-setting rows. Since M9 sub-project A the rest of the pane is label over caption with a right-pinned control and a reset that appears only on a changed row, so the section reads as a different product.

Bounding the column stopped the switches stretching the whole surface (done in A), but it did not make the cards read like settings. The work is in internal/shell/popout_plugins.go and pluginSettingRow rather than the settings pane, and it needs a decision about how much of Entry's anatomy a plugin-declared setting can borrow: a plugin manifest declares a label and a type but no description or default, so IsDefault and the caption line have no source unless the manifest grows one.

Flagged by the owner on the laptop during the A live check.

title: M3: render tooltips from the accepted theme and font
description: Tooltip paint hardcodes size, radius, background, foreground, and default font instead of the accepted configuration. The 3D completion handover already records this defect; resolve it through the current theme/font owner without adding a second theme model.

title: Settings font picker is not searchable
description:
D8 of docs/plans/2026-09-15-settings-foundation-design.md ships a searchable picker in the control vocabulary. Sub-project A built the enumerating half only: settingsFontFamilies reads fontscan.SystemFonts, dedupes and sorts, then hands the list to the ordinary Menu. This workstation has 720 families, so the control is a wall rather than a picker.

Approach that fits the existing machinery: Menu gains an optional retained ui.Field rendered as the first child of the open popup and named so PanelHost.editField can route IME to it, the way Search and Password already are. Menu.Next, Menu.Prev and Menu.PickAt then move over the filtered indices while index and cursor stay indices into the full option list, so Select commits the right value and PickAt accounts for the field occupying the first child slot. Opening the menu focuses the field.

Reached by internal/shell/popout_settings.go settingsMenuControl and internal/shell/menu.go.

title: Weather unit and interval are silently dropped when weather is unconfigured
description:
config.Write only emitted a weather block when Weather.Configured was true. The settings entries for weather.unit and weather.interval set neither the value's flag nor Configured, so changing either preference before setting a place was silently lost on save and reload.

Decision: non-default unit and interval preferences persist before a place is set. Preference-only blocks leave Weather.Configured false and do not invent coordinates. Empty weather blocks, incomplete coordinate pairs, weather widgets without a place, and non-empty location labels without a place remain invalid.

Found during M9 sub-project A. internal/config/write.go and the weather entries in internal/settings/registry.go.

title: Font families are shown in their normalized form
description:
The picker lists dejavusans rather than DejaVu Sans. fontscan stores Footprint.Family normalized, and D10 of the settings foundation design allowed presenting normalized names explicitly, calling a display form its own decision. It still looks wrong in the pane.

The decision is what the display form is derived from, because the normalized string is lossy and title-casing it does not recover word boundaries. The honest source is the font file's own name table rather than the footprint. Worth settling alongside the searchable picker, since both change the same control.

title: A described settings row measures itself instead of taking a ladder height
description:
Every other settings row takes Metrics.StandardControl. A row with a description is two stacked lines and a fixed height cropped the caption, so settingsEntryRow sets Height only when Describe is empty. The density ladder therefore governs the text inside a described row but not the row box, which is not what the design says.

Closing it properly means a minimum height rather than a fixed one, and internal/ui carries no MinHeight on Node today. That is a layout-engine addition with reach beyond this pane, so it wants a decision before it is made: either add MinHeight and have every settings row take the ladder as a floor, or amend the design to say that a described row is self-measuring. internal/shell/popout_settings.go settingsEntryRow.

title: Plugin setting rows do not use the settings pane's row anatomy
description:
The Plugins section renders the plugin host's own composition: a meta line, a switch, a Retry button, then per-setting rows. Sub-project A bounded that column so it stopped stretching the surface, but it still does not read like settings next to the label-over-caption rows every other section now uses.

Flagged by the owner during A and deliberately left, because the change is to internal/shell/popout_plugins.go and pluginSettingRow rather than to the settings pane. It carries its own decision: how much of settings.Entry's anatomy a plugin-declared setting can borrow, given a plugin declares a label and a type but no description or group.

title: Home System card: four 40px radial gauges in one row
description:
Owner-approved 2026-09-17. Design package: docs/plans/assets/2026-09-17-metrics-control-centre-radial-design/.

Replace the provisional 22px two-row layout, which overflows the padded System card by 4px at font scale 100, 13px at 125, 29px at 150, and fails to lay out at 200.

Composition: four 40px rings in one row, value centred inside each ring, caption beneath, no card title. Content 57 of the 70px interior.

Approved amendments (design.md D2):
1. Drop the 'System' card title; keep an accessible group name on the card.
2. Visible caption 'Temp'; accessible name 'CPU temperature'.
3. paintRadialGauge derives its centred glyph and value size from the box instead of the literals 11 and 8.

Seams: ccHome, ccResourceGroup, ccGaugeSize, paintRadialGauge, and TestControlCentreHomeSystemGaugesFitInsideCardBounds, whose (len(s)*8, 16) stub cannot see the current overflow.

Acceptance: docs/plans/assets/2026-09-17-metrics-control-centre-radial-design/acceptance-checklist.md

title: ccMonitor omits GPU and CPU temperature
description:
Found while designing the Home System card (2026-09-17). The Control Centre's own monitor section (ccMonitor in controlcenter_pages.go) builds graph cards for CPU, Memory and Network only. Once Home shows four metrics, that section contradicts the page one click away from it.

The standalone System Monitor (monitorTree) does carry GPU via selectGPU, and shows temperature as a second legend chip on the CPU card. So the gap is ccMonitor alone.

Needs a named decision: add GPU and temperature to ccMonitor, or state why the section is deliberately narrower. See design.md D4 in docs/plans/assets/2026-09-17-metrics-control-centre-radial-design/.

title: Radial thermal warning colour is nearly invisible
description:
Found while designing the Home System card (2026-09-17). radialWarningAmber applies theme.EnsureContrast(amber, track, 3), which walks #ffb300 toward black until it clears 3:1 against the track. The painted result is #6c4b00, a dark brown that reads as the arc fading out rather than as a warning on the dark card.

The error role above 85C receives no EnsureContrast treatment and sits at 1.20:1 against the track.

More broadly the arc is distinguished from the track by hue, not luminance: accent against track is 1.44:1.

The approved Home composition puts the number inside the ring, so the reading no longer depends on the arc. This issue is about whether the warning band should be legible as a warning at all. See design.md, Observations.

title: Settings input fields read as a thin bar at mini density
description: Reported by the owner from live use of the settings pane after M9 sub-project B. At mini density Metrics.InputHeight is 24, and a 24-pixel control reads as a thin bar rather than a field. Needs the owner's eye before the density ladder is touched: that metric is shared by every surface, so changing it moves controls everywhere. The control-sizing pass that stopped dropdowns and toggles stretching may have improved the proportion on its own, so re-look at the current build first.

title: Bar lane editor polish: insertion indicator, add-list filtering, group drag
description: The owner's verdict on the M9 sub-project B lane editor after live use: still rough. The tooltip, labelling and grouping-colour pass helped; it is not finished. Three concrete candidates, all on branch milestone/m9-bar-composition: (1) no insertion indicator when a drop would insert rather than join, so only the join target is marked; (2) the add list is 22 unfiltered rows and wants a filter; (3) a group's members cannot be reordered by drag, only by Alt+arrow.

title: M3: prevent a cancelled dwell callback showing a tooltip
description: A time.AfterFunc callback that has begun can outlive timer.Stop in dwell.leave, set shown after leave observed false, and send a show with no later hide. Add a generation/current-timer check under the mutex and a focused race-boundary test.

title: Clock and date pills paint empty for up to a minute after start
description: Observed on the laptop 2026-09-18 while running the sysc-321 live gate. After a systemctl restart the bar's clock and date pills render as empty rounded rects and stay empty until the next minute boundary, then fill in correctly. Reproduced on both the top and the lower edge, so it is not related to the bar anchor, and it reproduces on a binary built from main: pre-existing, not introduced by the bar geometry work. Likely the clock widget takes its first value from a minute-aligned tick rather than painting the current time at start.

title: Intel i915 GPU metrics integration and laptop qualification
description: Complete the M10 metrics, Control Centre, and GPU slice with the published sysc-metrics v0.5.1+ Intel i915 path. The shell metrics service must own one stateful GPUSampler, project the selected GPU consistently to the bar, System Monitor, and Control Centre, and retain exact-PCI GPU history. Record the laptop CAP_PERFMON requirement, the existing radial bar configuration, and the upstream completion evidence.
design: Use sysc-metrics GPUSampler as the only Intel reader. Keep sampler ownership in the shell metrics goroutine, keep GPU identity and history keyed by PCI ID, and leave unavailable usage truthful when PMU permission is absent. Do not add a shell-side perf reader or duplicate GPU sampler.
acceptance_criteria: Merge the feature implementation to main; keep the sysc-metrics v0.5.1+ pin; pass focused tests and the required shell gates; qualify Intel i915 usage on the laptop with the first sample as a baseline and the second sample valid; verify cap_perfmon on the installed binary and one live shell service; verify CPU, memory, temperature, and GPU radial bar entries; record the completion handover and README update.

title: M3: remove or make Metrics.Leased total
description: Metrics.Leased has no callers and dereferences m.leases[sel] without a nil guard, so the natural unleased query panics. Grok already classified it as a cheap deletion; delete it unless a concrete consumer appears.

title: M4 spec review sweep
description: Implementation-vs-spec pass for Milestone 4 (4A+4B) against the panel-foundation and settings-osd-theme-catalog designs/plans, the post-M3 audit, AGENTS.md, and the roadmap exit gate. Main effort of the M4 sweep pair. Live Niri matrices stay owner-deferred. Do not action M3 audit defects (sysc-31..35). Produce docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-m4-spec-review-sweep.md and register it.

title: M4 code quality sweep
description: Code quality pass over landed M4 (panels, controls, settings, OSD, theming). Use engineering judgement: correctness risks, dead paths, races, leaked goroutines, missing tests, API leaks. Not a ponytail-only cut list. Report first; do not apply cuts. Produce docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-m4-code-quality-sweep.md and register it.

title: M4: OSD lease, chrome, and motion vs D5/D7
description: Landed OSD is Overlay / exclusive_zone -1 / no shield / 1.5s timer, but: (1) audio/brightness Changes only fire while leased and OSDStep uses a transient lease, so external wpctl does not show OSD; (2) render is a fill bar, no glyph or label; (3) no fade+slide. Spec: 4B D5/D7 and Task 10. Discovered in sysc-36.

title: M4: template apply writes sandbox paths, not app configs
description: ApplyEnabled writes niri/gtk correctly but every other catalog template to ~/.config/sysc-shell/themes/<name>.conf. No kitty SIGUSR1, apply errors discarded, no single-flight supersede. Spec: 4B D9 and Task 13 HookWrite/HookKitty. Discovered in sysc-36.

title: M2 corrections: global-keyed identity, font map wiring, lossless invalidation
description: Owned by the implementing agent on milestone/stable-bar. Quota-limited; resumes 05:00 2026-08-30. Gates Tranche 3A Task 0. See docs/plans/2026-08-29-stable-multi-output-bar-progress-handover.md (that branch only).

title: M4: settings schema misses live widgets, bar items, virtual list
description: settings.Default() snapshots config.Default() widget entries; live bar config is ignored. Bar item lists are not registry entries. Settings content is KindScroll; KindVirtualList is unused. Spec: 4B D2 table and Task 5 consumer. Discovered in sysc-36.

title: [core] Deadlock risk: sendAux while holding Registry.mu
description:
GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-shell/issues/2

Panel/toast paths call Registry.sendAux while holding Registry.mu. Bounded aux channel + owner needing the same lock = deadlock. OSD already unlocks before sendAux. Audit 2026-09-17.

title: [core] Bar teardownSurface frees SHM before destroying wl_surface
description:
GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-shell/issues/3

teardownSurface munmaps generations before destroying wl_surface — opposite of teardownUnit safe order. Crash risk on bar recreate/disable.

title: [core] publishSurface drops invalidations under load
description:
GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-shell/issues/4

Invalidation delivery under load may drop frames contrary to draw-after-invalidation.

title: [core] Session actions block Wayland owner under Registry.mu
description:
GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-shell/issues/5

runSessionAction/runArgv under Registry.mu stalls Wayland owner for subprocess lifetime.

title: [core] Panel WantIME/IBeamAt race + missing critical concurrency tests
description:
GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-shell/issues/6

WantIME/IBeamAt read focus/hit-test without Registry.mu while rebuilds mutate under lock.

title: [services] External theming templates are stubs that overwrite real app configs
description:
GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-shell/issues/7

Stub templates can overwrite XDG app configs when Appearance toggles enable them.

GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-shell/issues/8

IPC trust model weaker than notify/tray; TempDir fallback insecure.

GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-shell/issues/9

Display pairing prompts never timeout.

description:
GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-shell/issues/10

Video wallpaper still extraction for theme seed/restore not wired.
