description:
GitHub: https://github.com/Nomadcxx/sysc-shell/issues/11

Full os.Environ to plugins; missing schedule/IPC tests.

title: Live panels paint empty chrome; monitor configure crashes the shell
description: Super+P (clock) maps a rounded empty panel: PanelHost.render draws shadow/body/focus ring and never Paint. Super+M (system-monitor) returns ui: child 0: unsupported kind 7 from measureNode (KindTab) during configure; wayland onConfigure fail() tears down the whole owner. columnChildHeight also rejects KindGraph, so tabs-only would still crash on the sparkline.

title: M10 workspaces: shape-only pills with urgency
description: Execute D3 of docs/plans/2026-09-16-bar-weather-launcher-workspaces-design.md. Carry niri is_urgent through the wire and projection, then paint the workspace row as shape-only pills: focused = larger flexible rounded element, occupied = smaller filled shape, urgent = error treatment, empty = present but unfilled. No painted numbers anywhere in the projected tree. Preserve index ordering, focus dominance, the pre-snapshot fallback, and the existing hit/accessibility identity.

title: trayclient dials tray.v1.sock; the service binds presenter.v1.sock
description: internal/trayclient/socket.go hardcodes socketName = "tray.v1.sock". Every revision of sysc-tray in its history, including the pinned v0.1.0-rc.1, binds "presenter.v1.sock" (internal/presenter/server.go:25). The shell therefore dials a path nothing serves, checkSocket fails on Lstat, and no tray icon can ever paint. The package tests build the fake server's path from the same constant (client_test.go:23), so the suite stays green. Found while working docs/plans/2026-09-19-m9-overflow-and-tray-handover.md job one.

title: trayclient retries forever without reporting why it cannot reach the service
description: Client.session drops the dial and handshake errors on the floor (return false) and Run backs off and retries forever, so an unreachable service is indistinguishable from a service with no items: the shell log stays completely silent. This is why sysc-411 survived in the field across two machines and several restarts - the handover records 'the shell logs no tray or presenter lines at all' as a symptom with no cause. Wants a reported first failure and a reported recovery, without a line per retry.

title: Weather effect repaints the whole panel surface each frame
description: An effect loop never settles, so a surface carrying one repaints in full for as long as it is open. Pacing effect-only frames at 66ms took the weather panel from 80% of a core to 63% on the test machine (0% closed), but the residual cost is a full-surface paint of a 575x700 panel where only the effect region changed. A damage-region publish would remove most of it. Measured 2026-09-19 at scale 1.25; bounded benchmark is 10.9ms at the Control Centre size after this tranche.

title: Workspace pills: retarget animation instead of rebuilding the row
description: The commission (docs/plans/2026-09-19-workspace-pill-art-commission.md) defers animation to a follow-up. refreshWorkspacePills currently rebuilds every pill node whenever any pill's state changes. Per the Noctalia diffing model, a state change should retarget the existing width and fill transition channels on the same nodes, keeping identity stable, rather than replacing the row. Identity keys are already stable: each pill carries the compositor workspace id in its action.

title: Workspace pills: cycle workspaces on scroll
description: The commission defers scroll cycling to a follow-up. The pill row now handles a primary click (workspace:<id> -> niri.FocusWorkspace); a wheel over the row should step to the neighbouring workspace. The bar already routes EventPointerAxis through an onAxis seam that resolves the action under the pointer, so the row needs an axis handler beside its action handler, plus a decision on whether the wheel wraps at the ends.

title: Toast host places cards against a guessed 1920x1080 output and kills the shell
description: toastHost.geometryFor stood in 1920x1080 for an unmeasured output and recompute wrote the guess back as real. On a 1.25-scaled 1920x1080 laptop the logical surface is 1536 wide, so a card landed at x=1528 w=380; aux_surface.go:241 rejects an input rect that leaves the surface and sysc-shell exits 1. Any notification pending before the first configure took the bar down. Never seen on a 3440-wide output.

title: Control centre Home split overflows its body by one pixel
description: ccLeftColumnW 356 + MarginL + ccRightColumnW 228 = 597 across a 596px body from ccBodyWidth at the standard 700px panel. A composition sized to fill its container exactly then refuses the child. Found while reviewing feature/parity-task10-11, which carried the fix and a guard test; the branch predates sub-project B's settings rewrite so the fix was ported rather than merged.

title: Input radius is a theme axis but not a configuration key
description: theme.Composition.InputRadius exists and resolveShapes consumes it, but no config key writes it: internal/config has no InputRadius field and the settings catalogue has no appearance entry for it. feature/parity-task10-11 exposed it end to end against the pre-sub-project-B registry, so the entry must be re-expressed as a catalogue Entry rather than merged. Branch kept for reference.

title: Bar body gap is hardcoded to the top edge; a lower-edge bar paints its gap on the far side
description: internal/shell/bar.go bodyLocked insets Y: gap and H: height-gap unconditionally, and BarGap is documented as the outer gap between the screen edge and the painted body. For a top-anchored bar that is correct. For the lower edge, shipped by sysc-321, the gap must sit at the surface's lower edge against the screen; the code instead floats it on the far side and runs the painted body flush to the screen edge. Derived from code during the-322 investigation; not yet observed live. C2 must make the body derivation edge-aware anyway, so this fix belongs in that slice or immediately before it.
notes: Reopened 2026-09-29: was closed by commit 204700e on milestone/m9-c2-vertical-axis, which was archived unmerged (origin/archive/2026-09-28/milestone/m9-c2-vertical-axis). Fix 'derive the bar body from the edge' (04a021b) is NOT on main. Closes with the C2 rebase.

title: Closing the settings panel panics the Wayland client
description: Live: panel.close settings (and Super+Comma dismiss) tears down the aux surface then dispatch panics: invalid server object ID. Clock/session/monitor close do not. Settings is the only panel with a text field (IME) and a KindRow+KindVirtualList tree. wayland teardownUnit destroys shm buffers immediately rather than waiting for wl_buffer.release.

Plan: sysc-plugins docs/plans/2026-09-19-kdeconnect-phone-connect.md. Worktrees: sysc-plugins .worktrees/feat/kdeconnect, sysc-shell .worktrees/feature/kdeconnect-icons.

title: kdeconnect parity: read announcedName/selfId via daemon methods
description: Audit gap 1 (docs/plans/2026-09-19-kdeconnect-parity-audit-report.md). DMS reads announcedName as a DBus method call on org.kde.kdeconnect.daemon; GetAllProps does not carry it (live smoke proved empty). Read both via method calls and surface them (DMS shows them in its status card).

description: Audit gap 3. DMS converts a local path to a file:// URI and calls share.shareUrl; my plugin calls share.shareFile which DMS never uses and kdeconnectd may not export. Match DMS.

description: Audit gap 4. DMS refreshes and re-runs auto-select when the popout opens; my ViewOpen only publishes.

title: kdeconnect parity: per-card pairing actions in the switcher
description: Audit gap 6. DMS DeviceCards carry Accept/Reject rows on isPairRequestedByPeer and a Request Pairing row when reachable+unpaired+not requested, visible on selectable switcher cards too. Mine offers pairing actions only for the selected device.

title: kdeconnect parity: share dialog URI gating and close button
description: Audit gap 7. DMS validates URI-ness with a scheme regex: URI button enabled only for valid URIs, Text button only for non-empty text, plus a close button. Mine: buttons always enabled, submit heuristic diverges.

title: kdeconnect parity: SMS dialog send gating and single-line body

title: kdeconnect parity: refresh interval 0 disables, busy state while refreshing
description: Audit gap 9. DMS stateUpdateInterval allows 0 = disabled and shows a spinner via isRefreshing. Mine clamps to >=5s and never reports busy; the wire has StatusBusy unused.

title: KindCapsule measure and layout
description: Plan task 1. ui.KindCapsule + ToneAccent. See docs/plans/2026-08-31-bar-visual-parity.md.

title: kdeconnect parity: battery/network icon bands and per-state network glyphs

DMS battery icon breakpoints: charging >=90/60/40/<20, level >=95/80/65/50/35/20/10 then alert; network icons per strength bar and type (5g, 4g_mobiledata, 3g_mobiledata, 2g_mobiledata, signal_cellular_nodata). Mine: linear bands and one network glyph. Needs sysc-shell catalogue additions.

title: kdeconnect parity: Valent backend (ca.andyholmes.Valent)
description: Audit gap 13, decision needed. DMS auto-detects two backends via NameOwnerChanged: kdeconnectd and Valent (ObjectManager + org.gtk.Actions API, a different protocol). Mine is kdeconnectd-only (documented non-goal). Full parity needs a second backend behind the existing seams.

title: kdeconnect parity: ongoing media (MPRIS) section decision
description: Audit gap 14, decision needed. DMS renders a full player (play/pause, prev/next, replay10/forward10, seek with position/length, track metadata, player identity, artwork, showOngoingMedia setting) from the host MPRIS bridge with the device mprisremote DBus fallback. Mine defers to the shell first-party media widget. Either build the in-panel section or accept and record the deviation.

description: Audit gap 15. DMS scans the SFTP mount for recent images (find, png/jpg/jpeg/webp), renders a thumbnail grid with open/drag-out/portal share, per-device recent-images path validated against the SFTP mount point, custom device images, device type overrides, maxRecentImages 1-12 and scanSubdirectories settings. Needs sysc-shell wire support first (image node, file picking/drag, per-device map settings).

title: sysc-shell: image node and file capabilities on the plugin wire
description: Prerequisite for kdeconnect parity gap 15: the plugin wire (plugin/v1) has no image kind, no file picking, and no OS drag. Adding them is shell work (wire fields + converter + renderer) and must respect the charter (no general toolkit).

title: kdeconnect parity: charging fill on the bar pill
description: Audit gap 16. DMS enableChargingAnimation paints a level fill in error/warning/success tints while charging. The wire has no animation; a static accent approximation is possible, true parity needs shell animation support.

title: kdeconnect parity: keyboard shortcuts (device cycle, Alt-N, share)
description: Audit gap 17. DMS binds Ctrl+Tab/Ctrl+Shift+Tab device cycling, Alt+1-9 direct select, S to share. Shortcuts are a shell capability, not a plugin wire capability; needs a host mechanism first.

title: kdeconnect parity: i18n for plugin strings
description: Audit gap 18. DMS ships 22 translation files through I18n.trFor. The shell has no plugin translation mechanism. Deferred until one exists.

title: Paint KindCapsule with SurfaceContainer fill
description: Plan task 2. ProofStyle.Capsule + FillRounded. See docs/plans/2026-08-31-bar-visual-parity.md.

title: Plugin incompatibility test is flaky under parallel suite load
description: TestRuntimeMarksAnIncompatiblePluginRatherThanRetrying reported state=failed want=incompatible during a full ./... run with another suite running concurrently, then passed 3/3 in isolation and 4/4 on main. The fake plugin is the race-built test binary and needs about a second to exit against a 1s shutdown grace, so under load the runtime records a failure before it can read the incompatibility. Seen 2026-09-19 while gating sysc-418.

title: Bar sections drop the tail of declaration order, so status widgets go first
description: grantsWithin keeps items i<fits and drops the tail, so declaration order doubles as priority. The default right section sheds Battery, Clipboard and Notifications before Now playing. The reading order you want left-to-right is the opposite of the survival order you want under a squeeze. Prior art (DMS, noctalia) may already have a priority model; not urgent while the project matures. Surfaced by sysc-313's overflow fade, which makes the drop visible.

title: Config writer silently drops fields for item ids it has no branch for
description: encodeItem switched on a hand-kept list of metric ids that had fallen two behind the loader's: gpu and temperature were absent, so every write emitted them as a bare {id} and the next load restored defaults. A live bar configured with four radial gauges came back with two radial and two text widgets. Media and clipboard had no branch either. Fixed by guarding on isMetric, the predicate the loader already used, plus a round-trip fixture per knownItems id so a new id cannot repeat it.

title: Shell motion: raise frame rate and cut per-frame paint cost
description: Measured on the laptop (eDP-1, 60.01Hz, 16.66ms budget): a full bar repaint costs 1.22ms with 1272 allocs, yet theme.BaseMotion.FrameCap=33ms paces every animating surface to ~30fps, exactly every other vblank. blendMask is 56.8% of the frame and reads its mask through image.Alpha.AlphaAt (Point.In + PixOffset per pixel); direct Pix indexing with an opaque fast path measured 5.0x faster and byte-identical. Animation is clocked by a free-running 16ms ticker rather than the frame callback the scheduler already owns, so frame spacing beats against vblank. Text is re-shaped through harfbuzz every repaint. Four parts: blendMask fast path, lower FrameCap, frame-callback-driven publishes, shaped-run cache.

title: Drive animation from the frame callback instead of a ticker
description: animateSurface samples unsettled values on a time.Ticker. The tick now runs at half a 60Hz frame so it cannot beat against the vblank, which removes the visible judder, but the sampling phase is still unrelated to the compositor's cadence: a value is read up to half a frame before it is presented. The architecturally correct form is to resample when wl_callback.done arrives, which the scheduler already receives (internal/render/schedule.go, done handler in internal/platform/wayland/client.go). That needs a seam from the Wayland owner back into the shell asking whether a surface is still unsettled, and that call would run on the owner goroutine and take a surface lock, so it needs care against the blank-shell failure mode. Deferred deliberately: the ticker change delivered most of the benefit at a fraction of the risk.

title: Weather bar element carried a redundant Weather label and only activated on left click

sysc-tray Proxy.Close self-deadlocks on the owner-left path
description: Terminate integration tests (sysc-tray redesign/v0.1, tests/integration/terminate_test.go) hang: when a real item owner process dies, the proxy pump detects owner-left and calls onItem -> dropWorker -> closeWorker -> Proxy.Close on the pump goroutine itself; Close blocks on <-p.looped/<-p.pumped, which only fire when pump returns. Self-deadlock. Existing tests never hit it because Close is only ever called from app.Close on a foreign goroutine. Fix direction: run the worker close off the pump goroutine (or make Close reentrancy-safe). Evidence: goroutine dump from go test ./tests/integration/ -run TestTerminate.

title: Stale gslapper socket files block wallpaper applies forever
description: A shell run killed without cleanup (observed Sep 16 08:42 on the desktop) leaves gslapper-<connector>.sock files in the runtime dir with no listener. Every later start, reconcile's Apply sees socket-exists + no owned process and correctly refuses (D17/D18), but there is no recovery path: launch refuses, stopOwned reports 'still holds', nothing unlinks a socket file that has no owner and no listener. Result: 'DP-x: wallpaper: DP-x socket is not owned by this shell' on every boot, wallpaper never applies, and because commit never happens the theme seed is never set. Fix direction: at Apply/launch, when the socket file exists but has no live peer (socketPeerPID fails or no listener), treat it as garbage and unlink before spawn — the same ownership proof socketFileIfOwned already uses, extended to the dead case.

title: Thumbnailer never publishes final counts when the walk tail has no new previews
description: Observed on the desktop: panel stuck at 'generating previews 228/645' while the walk had actually finished (642 cache hits + 3 webp decode errors; no ffmpeg running; last created attempt was index 227). generate() only calls note() when made=true, and the service publishes snapshots only on thumbProgress — so when every entry after the last creation is a cache hit, done reaches total but no final snapshot is ever published. The panel reads ThumbsDone/ThumbsTotal from the snapshot (service.go:482, popout_wallpaper.go:670) and shows a stale 'generating' state forever. Fix direction: publish once at the end of generate() regardless of made, or have the service publish when Counts() reports done==total after a progress tick.

title: Startup theme generation runs matugen with an empty seed and reports a scary failure every boot
description: Default ThemeGen is {Source: wallpaper, Seed: ""} because the seed is deliberately never persisted (D20: rebuilt from the wallpaper replay). At startup generateTheme therefore runs 'matugen image ""' which exits 1 ('No such file or directory', reproduced on matugen 4.2.0), the panel shows 'theme: matugen: exit status 1', and the compiled fallback paints. On a healthy boot the wallpaper apply then succeeds and notifySeed re-generates, so the error is transient noise — but when applies fail (see the stale-socket issue) it looks like a theme bug. Fix direction: skip the generator for an empty wallpaper seed the way Kind==palette already skips it, and surface 'waiting for first wallpaper' instead of a matugen failure.

title: plugin/v1 JSON encoder has no write mutex; concurrent Snapshot calls crash the plugin
description:
Framing encoder (plugin/v1/framing.go:71-106) has no write serialization. Any plugin whose publish() runs from more than one goroutine (poll tick + action goroutine is the common pattern — mini-docker does exactly this) can issue concurrent Snapshot calls while the main recv loop also writes, producing concurrent map/encoder writes and a crash that kills the pill.

Found during the mini-docker audit (docs/plans/2026-09-22-mini-docker-{backend}-audit.md in sysc-plugins). The plugin currently must self-serialize around the whole client; that is an easy trap every plugin author will hit.
acceptance_criteria: Either the client serializes frame writes internally, or the plugin-v1 docs state the threading contract loudly; a regression test at the library level proves concurrent Snapshot is safe (or documented-unsafe with the contract spelled out).

title: Host silently rejects malformed plugin views (wrong root kind, node-budget overflow) with no signal
description:
When a plugin publishes a view the host cannot render, it is dropped with zero feedback to the plugin or logs: a tooltip published with a row root is silently rejected (host requires column roots for tooltips — mini-docker did exactly this and shipped a dead tooltip), and a tree exceeding the MaxNodes budget (1024) silently stops publishing (mini-docker would go blank past ~170 containers with docker ps -a).

Found during the mini-docker audit (docs/plans/2026-09-22-mini-docker-{ui,ux}-audit.md in sysc-plugins). Both failures are invisible: the plugin author sees a blank panel and cannot tell why.
acceptance_criteria: Rejected publishes produce a diagnosable signal — at minimum a host-side log line naming plugin + view + reason; ideally a plugin-visible error response. Cover both the root-kind rule and the node-budget rule.

title: Document the plugin open-panel pattern (Button ID + CallPanelOpen) in plugin-v1 docs
description:
Panels only open when the plugin itself calls CallPanelOpen in response to a Button activate event with a chosen node ID (established pattern: timer main.go:85, world-clock). Nothing documents this, so a plugin whose bar is a bare text node ships an unopenable panel — mini-docker did exactly this and three independent audits initially attributed the blank panel elsewhere before converging on reachability.

Found during the mini-docker audit (docs/plans/2026-09-22-mini-docker-ui-audit.md in sysc-plugins).
acceptance_criteria: plugin/v1 package docs (or the plugin authoring doc) state: panels open only via the plugin's own CallPanelOpen; show the minimal bar-button pattern; mention the tooltip column-root requirement in the same place.

title: Data race: setAudio/setBrightness vs their OSD relay goroutines
description: go test -race ./internal/shell reports three races per run on main (514ab9e). setAudio writes r.audio at registry.go:102 then starts 'go r.relayAudioOSD()', which reads r.audio at registry.go:271 with no lock held; the next setAudio writes it concurrently. setBrightness/relayBrightnessOSD share the shape. Pass the service to the relay instead of re-reading the field. Pre-existing M4 (sysc-38) defect, not introduced by the sysc-41/42 work. M5 adds notify and tray relays of the same shape, so fix before copying it.

title: Close weather HTTP idle connections

After Registry.Close, runtime stacks show only net/http persistConn readLoop and writeLoop from the weather request. acceptance_criteria: A focused service test proves Weather.Close closes idle HTTP transport connections; TestClosingTheRegistryStopsTheWeatherGoroutine passes repeatedly; scoped internal/services and internal/shell checks pass.

title: Fix gSlapper explicit image scaling modes

acceptance_criteria: The gSlapper static-image path applies explicit fill, stretch, original, and panscan modes; automated regression coverage proves the mode behavior, including default panscan. The fix is merged to origin/master and installed. End-to-end DP-1 foreground/cutout alignment is tracked separately in sysc-505.

title: Calibrate Wallpaper Depth alignment on DP-1
description: Follow-up acceptance for sysc-501 after the gSlapper static-image scaling fix landed in 039ec9c and its default-panscan regression landed in 2ff3ffd. Run the installed fixed build with Wallpaper Depth on DP-1 (3440x1440, scale 1) using the branch-crossing calibration image. Capture native-resolution output in fill, stretch, original, and panscan; verify the wallpaper geometry changes as documented and compare the visible foreground edge with the depth cutout. Restore the original wallpaper assignments and shell config after the run. If a mode fails, record the measured discrepancy and root cause and leave this issue open.
acceptance_criteria: For all four modes, save or reference a native-resolution capture and record the measured cutout-to-foreground edge error in physical pixels; every mode is within 1 physical pixel. Confirm original wallpaper assignments and config are restored. If any mode exceeds the bound, keep this issue open with failure evidence.

title: Design user-managed plugin sources
description: Next post-M6 plugin-system slice identified by the owner: let users add plugin sources in Settings and discover/install compatible sysc-shell plugins. Use Noctalia and DMS as behavior references only; the shell AGENTS rules reject their config, runtime, and QML compatibility. The M6 plugin-host design explicitly deferred a catalog, installer, updater, and removal UI. Design this as a new slice before implementation. Resolve source model and persistence, manifest discovery/validation, version or ref pinning, install/update/remove/rollback lifecycle, interaction with existing local development roots, error reporting, and explicit trust/consent for plugins that run with the shell user’s privileges.
acceptance_criteria: An approved design and implementation plan are committed and registered in docs/plans. They define user-added sources, plugin discovery and lifecycle, trust/consent, failure recovery, and how existing local plugins continue to work; they make no DMS or Noctalia runtime/config compatibility claim.

sysc-wayland v0.2.0: unknown surface enter is fatal
description: REOPENED 2026-09-02: reproduced live on 715cc5f, not stale. 12 settings panel open/close cycles with the pointer over the panel produce 'dispatch: panic handling opcode=1 senderID=21: client: invalid server object ID 0x2b'. Note opcode 1 is wl_pointer.leave, not enter as first recorded. The context recovers the panic into setFatal, so the process survives but the Wayland connection is dead: every surface is torn down and the IPC socket goes with it. The user sees the bar vanish rather than a crash, which is why it reads as resolved. sysc-shell pins sysc-wayland v0.2.0, whose client/context.go RegisterWithID still panics for any id below firstServerID while the generated Pointer and Keyboard dispatch call it for unknown surface ids. Upstream fix plus a new tag and repin still required.

Battery icon font: all seven level glyphs are identical
description:
internal/render/icons/sysc-icons.ttf draws codepoints 0xE008 to 0xE00E (battery levels 0..6) as the same solid silhouette. Rendering the band at 96pt and at the bar's 17px shows no difference between an empty and a full battery.

BatteryIconRune is correct: 73 percent maps to level 5 of 0..6 and iconfont_test asserts every charge lands in the band. The selection works and the asset does not encode what was selected, so a battery widget cannot communicate charge through its icon. Live at 73 percent it reads as a solid block.

Fix belongs in the font asset: seven discharging and seven charging glyphs that actually differ, ideally an outline with a partial fill so the level reads at 17px. Check the critical glyph too. A test that rasterises each level and asserts the glyphs differ would stop this recurring, since the existing test only checks codepoint mapping.

Discovered live 2026-08-31 alongside sysc-43.

title: Group members are not centred inside their capsule
description:
Live 2026-08-31: the grouped cpu and memory values sit off-centre inside the group pill.

Introduced by the group tranche. measureNode for KindRow now reports the tallest child rather than the band it was offered, so text measured at the physical size is not cropped. layoutCapsuleChild then grows the layout box to that height when it exceeds the capsule's inner band. Layout centres children against content.H of the grown box, not against the visible capsule, so members are pushed off centre.

Fix: centre members against the capsule's own inner band while still measuring them at their natural height. Add a test asserting a member's vertical centre matches the capsule's, with a child taller than the offered band.

title: Installed plugins built on an old SDK fail the handshake since host protocol floor 1.3
description: Laptop, main c89c4e8 deployed 2026-09-26: org.sysc.weather, org.sysc.kdeconnect and org.sysc.aiusage log 'read plugin.hello: EOF' at start. Since 5674306 (2026-09-20) the host offers only protocol 1.3-1.8 (internal/plugin/supervisor.go Supported), so a plugin binary built against an SDK whose ceiling is below 1.3 finds no common version and exits before replying. The laptop's previous build (2026-09-21) predated the floor. The desktop's weather plugin fails the same way on old and new builds. Either rebuild and reinstall the plugin binaries, or have the host log the version mismatch instead of EOF.

title: Stock themes are not selectable from settings
description: The design (D8, docs/plans/2026-08-30-settings-osd-theme-catalog-design.md) specifies ten curated seeds named as colour families, and selecting one sets theme source = stock plus that seed. internal/theme/stock.go carries all ten and theme.StockSeed resolves them, but the settings entry appearance.seed is KindString with no Options, so a user has to type the exact name. theme.StockNames has no caller outside tests. Make appearance.seed offer StockNames when appearance.source is stock, which needs an entry whose options depend on another entry's value; the settings registry has no such dependency today.
notes: Verified against A's design 2026-09-17: NOT automatically fixed by it. docs/plans/2026-09-15-settings-foundation-design.md gives each entry typed get/set closures, but says nothing about options that depend on another entry's value, which is precisely what this bug needs. settings.DefaultFor(cfg) already builds entries from a config, so the capability is within reach, but PanelHost.set is constructed once when the panel opens. Under A's live-apply a change to appearance.source would therefore not refresh appearance.seed's options. A needs either a registry rebuild from the draft after each change, or Options as a closure over config. Fold into sysc-330 rather than treating this as separately fixed.

title: Bar renders corrupt output on the laptop; cause not established
description:
2026-09-01. The bar paints scattered coloured blocks instead of content, or is absent and the window behind shows through. Process alive, single instance, log completely silent.

Not reproduced in tests. The same commit and the same font rendered correctly earlier in the same session, so the variable is not obviously the code.

Untested hypothesis: session state after roughly a dozen kill and restart cycles, which is the territory of sysc-51. A Niri session restart would rule that in or out and was not tried. The pre-session binary is kept at ~/.local/bin/sysc-shell.pre-fix.

Establish the cause before trusting any further live capture from that machine, since a bad session invalidates visual judgement of every other issue.
notes: Audit 2026-10-14: the 2026-10-11 performance report confirms mapped bars on DP-1 and DP-3, but records no pixel verification or cause for the original corruption. Keep open pending clean-session pixel verification or an owner decision to retire the report.

sysc-metrics: GPU usage for xe from drm-cycles fdinfo
description: v0.7.0's fdinfo fallback reads drm-engine-<class> ns (i915, amdgpu). xe publishes drm-cycles-<class> and drm-total-cycles-<class>, so xe GPUs (Lunar Lake and later, and i915 parts opted into xe) still report no usage. Busy per class = sum over clients of delta cycles / delta total-cycles, divided by capacity. Needs xe hardware to prove live.

title: sysc-metrics: GPU sample repeats pci.ids lookup and denied PMU opens every second
description: On the UHD 620 laptop one GPUSampler.Sample takes ~34 ms: ~10 ms is ReadGPU's pci.ids name lookup, repeated each sample for a name that never changes, and the rest includes four perf_event_open calls that are denied every sample, plus the 7 ms fdinfo walk. Cache names per PCI ID and stop reopening a PMU counter after EACCES/EPERM (retry rarely). Measure before and after.

title: Narrow the dead-socket probe-then-remove window in wallpaper Apply
description: Review finding: Apply probes deadSocketFile then os.Remove; a foreign process could unlink the dead file and bind a live socket in the window, and the remove would then unlink a live foreign socket. deadSocketFile could return the FileInfo and the unlink could route through removeSocketIfSame (inode compare). Residual race is inherent to probe-then-unlink; defense-in-depth, not a correctness fix.

title: Pin stopOwned's refusal of a live foreign socket with a test
description: Review finding: stopOwned's no-process branch unlinks a provably dead socket but has no test that it still refuses a socket with a live listener; Apply's equivalent guard is tested (TestEngineStillRefusesForeignLiveSocket). Add the stopOwned-side test.

title: Plugin panels: report the granted size in view.open and find the laptop width clamp
description:
On the laptop (eDP-1, 1536x864 logical, scale 1.25) the calendar panel (manifest 1040x760) is drawn about 810x758: width clamped, height intact. Placement.FittedSize would allow ~1500 wide, so something else clamps width. Separately, pluginHost.openPanel (internal/shell/pluginhost.go ~806-834) fills view.open Width/Height from the manifest (spec.Width/Height), so a plugin is told 1040x760 while its tree is laid out in the smaller surface: plugins cannot lay out for the box they actually get, and layout the plugin linted at the declared size can be refused (calendar's status-banner Refresh button fails lint at 810x758).

Wanted: (1) root-cause the width clamp; (2) view.open (and a resize path when the surface changes) carries the fitted/granted size; (3) test that a panel declared wider than its placement is told the smaller size.

Consumer: sysc-plugins calendar (currently designed for a fixed 800x720 as a workaround, see sysc-plugins docs/plans/2026-09-25-world-clock-handover.md and the calendar polish commit). Evidence: laptop screenshots 2026-09-26, panel borders at x=905..1918 physical.

title: Icon advance is narrower than its ink
description: The icon glyphs scale to about 1150 font units of ink while the advance stays at 900, so an icon sits tight against the value beside it with no gap. Widening the advance to 1260 corrupted the whole bar rather than only the spacing, which suggests the mask or blend path does not handle an advance wider than the em, or that the corruption has a different cause entirely. See the corrupt-render issue. Fix the spacing once rendering is trustworthy again.

title: Apply's stale-socket error double-prefixes wallpaper:
description: Review nit from sysc-576: Apply wraps removeSocketIfSame's error with 'wallpaper: clear stale %s socket: %w', but removeSocketIfSame already returns 'wallpaper: socket path %s changed while it was stopped', yielding 'wallpaper: clear stale DP-1 socket: wallpaper: socket path ... changed...'. Cosmetic; the wrap is still needed for raw os.Remove errors. Clean fix is to strip the prefix from removeSocketIfSame's errors and wrap at each call site (Apply, stopOwned no-process, stopOwned owned-process paths), which touches the stopOwned error contract.

title: TestEngineDoesNotRemoveReplacedSocket is inode-reuse flaky on ext4
description: The test removed the socket then wrote a replacement at the same path; on ext4 the replacement reuses the freed inode, os.SameFile is true, stopOwned sends stop, the fake peer removes the file, removeSocketIfSame sees it vanished and returns nil, so Restore reports success and the test fails. Passes on tmpfs where inodes are not reused. Pre-existing on main; exposed by the full-repo -race gate with TMPDIR on ext4.

title: bd export drops issue comments from the tracked JSONL
description: The CLI bd export (cmd/bd/export.go in steveyegge/beads 0.17.7) populates dependencies and labels but never populates issue.Comments, so every CLI export rewrites .beads/issues.jsonl without the comments that the daemon/RPC auto-export path (internal/rpc/server_export_import_auto.go) includes. The AGENTS.md recovery procedure (DELETE FROM export_hashes; bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl) therefore silently drops comments from the tracked file; the DB keeps them (comments table intact). Observed 2026-09-27: 17 comment-bearing lines in HEAD, 0 after recovery, 22 rows still in the comments table. Guard: after any CLI export, grep -c '"comments"' .beads/issues.jsonl and restore from git if it dropped.

title: sysc-plugins CI red: go vet fails on runner (calendar libecal-2.0) + TestPluginCalendarGateAllViews broken by 2f1961f
description:
Two independent pre-existing failures on sysc-plugins main (found while fixing sysc-519; NOT mini-docker).

1) CI's actual first failure is 'go vet ./...' (37-43s then exit 1): plugins/calendar requires cgo libecal-2.0 (EDS), not installed on the GitHub runner: 'Package libecal-2.0 was not found in the pkg-config search path'. This masks every later CI step. Evidence: gh run view 36249418113 --log-failed; recent main runs all fail this way (36249418113, 36247382564, 36233161307, 36161564656, 36158589304). Options: install EDS in CI, build-tag the cgo file, or make vet skip calendar.

2) TestPluginCalendarGateAllViews fails deterministically on a clean tree, with and without -race (~5.6s = 5s waitNode deadline). Root cause: panelTitle() at tests/integration/plugin_calendar_gate_test.go:166-171 returns root.Children[0].Children[1].Text, but the current calendar header row's Children[1] is the cal-shortcuts icon button (no Text); the title text ('September 2026') now lives at root.Children[0].Children[0].Children[1]. Introduced by commit 2f1961f 'fix(calendar): design the panel for the box every screen grants'. Fix: one-line panelTitle path change (or search for the title text node).

Note: plugins/screen-recorder TestRecorderRepeatedToggleDoesNotRestart flaked once in a parallel full-suite run ('mode = recording, want idle', recorder_test.go:77), passed on rerun (7.657s) - timing flake, not investigated.
notes: 2026-09-30: A capped full plugin suite also fails in cmd/sysc-plugin-calendar: TestCalendarProcessOpensPopulatedMonthAndShowsEventDetails reports io: read/write on closed pipe at main_test.go:178. Reproduced alone with go test -count=1 -p 1 ./cmd/sysc-plugin-calendar -run ^TestCalendarProcessOpensPopulatedMonthAndShowsEventDetails$. This test and package are outside the AI Usage change.

title: Session panel clips its content when a battery card shows

Drain repaint requests before the Wayland startup handshake
description: Laptop deployment hung during startup. The captured stack shows the Wayland owner blocked in SetCapabilities -> publishSurface during connect(). The eight-entry invalidation channel was full; wake.bridge only started later in loop(). Notification handling then blocked on the same queue while holding Registry.mu, so IPC also timed out. Start the existing bridge before connect and join it before closing its pipe.
acceptance_criteria: A full repaint queue drains while a test compositor holds the initial handshake open. Connection failure cleans up the bridge. Race checks pass and the laptop renders its bar and answers IPC after deployment.
notes:
Confirmed startup deadlock during laptop deployment of sysc-820 revision e0c6255. Captured stack: Registry.SetCapabilities -> publishSurface blocks during the second Wayland connection roundtrip because the eight-entry invalidation queue is full. Its reader starts only after connect returns. A notification publisher also blocks while holding Registry.mu, causing IPC timeouts. This startup ordering predates sysc-820.

Evidence: /tmp/sysc590-goroutines.txt. Recovered laptop archThink with saved revision 278deeb322c516c9c1e378a8fdee077c6e0aefac through the deployment installer. IPC responded and screenshot /tmp/sysc590-restored.png showed the bar.

Fix: start the existing wake bridge before connect, then cancel and join it before closing the wake pipe. Regression test fills the queue during a held initial handshake, verifies publication continues, and checks Run exits on disconnect.

Verification: on main 8225083, gofmt, GOMAXPROCS=4 go vet -p 2 ./..., and the full internal/platform/wayland race tests pass. Race tests ran serially by package because the machine guard blocks repo-wide race builds after prior hard locks. A package-by-package race run on 08449de passed all but internal/shell (section validation and battery layout expectations) and tests/integration (tray hit targets); those failures reproduce in the affected tests on 8225083 and do not call Wayland Run.

Live laptop proof: deployed commit 38dfae739a8a through scripts/deploy. On archThink, sysc-shell ipc status returned ok=true, Niri listed sysc-shell:bar on eDP-1, and /tmp/sysc668-fixed-bar.png shows the rendered bar.

title: Registry audio/brightness OSD relay races with service swap
description:
go test -race ./internal/shell fails on main at 2c2fb7e (~20 tests in one package; the non-race run is clean).

Root cause: Registry.setAudio writes r.audio then launches 'go r.relayAudioOSD()', and the goroutine reads r.audio with no synchronisation. A second setAudio (service reload, or a test that swaps the service) writes the field while a live relay goroutine reads it. registry.go:102 (write) vs registry.go:271 (read). setBrightness has the same shape.

Found during Milestone 6A Task 0 reconciliation. Pre-existing, not caused by M6. Recorded rather than fixed because Registry is being changed by the in-flight M5 work.

Fix direction: pass the service to relayAudioOSD as an argument, or guard the field under the existing Registry mutex, and give the relay goroutine a per-generation stop signal so an old relay cannot outlive its service.

title: Weather surfaces are unstyled and under-informed: audit and parity pass
description:
Audit 2026-09-15 of every first-party weather presentation against the DMS/Noctalia v4 reference (docs/plans/assets/2026-08-31-bar-visual-parity/refs/noctalia-weather.png).

Presentations today, three sites, all thin:

- Bar widget (widget.go:226, weatherwidget.go): one text run - inline WMO glyph + temperature + optional condition word + stale age. The glyph is text, not an icon node: it inherits text tone and metrics, so sysc-1399's advance defect applies to it. The tooltip is the static word "Weather" (textWidget.tooltip is a plain string). No Action is set: clicking does nothing.
- Control centre weather page (controlcenter_pages.go:349 ccWeather): a Today card that presents raw coordinates ("%.2f deg, %.2f deg") as the location plus "Updated 15:04"; below it four 143x132 forecast cards showing day name, glyph and "H / L" only - no condition word, today excluded, count pinned at four.
- No standalone weather panel exists.

Data path (weather/client.go, weather/model.go, internal/services/weather.go): the request carries current=temperature_2m,weather_code and daily=weather_code,max,min,sunrise,sunset for seven days. Open-Meteo also returns, and Decode silently discards, elevation and timezone from the response root; the current block can carry is_day, apparent_temperature, humidity, wind_speed_10m, wind_direction_10m and uv_index; the daily block can carry uv_index_max and precipitation figures. The reference panel shows wind, UV, elevation and a named timezone; none of that is reachable today without extending the wire model.

Vocabulary drift - three copies of the same facts:

- Icon mapping: render/iconfont.go IconRune/IconName (eight WMO glyphs) versus ccWeatherIcon's separate Material ligature set (sunny, partly_cloudy_day, ...) for the same codes.
- Condition words: conditionWords (weatherwidget.go:14), ccWeatherCondition, and the plugin's Condition() are three tables. The plugin's routes through IconName; the shell's two do not agree with each other.
- No night variants: WMO code 0 at night renders a sun; is_day is not fetched.

State handling drift: formatWeather's three-state rule (placeholder / error / stale-with-age) lives in the bar only. ccWeather dashes and "Updated HH:MM" ignore FailedSince, so an aged reading renders identically to a fresh one.

Conformance and collision hazards: ccWeather's geometry (Height 336/480, 132; Width 143; Gap 8/12) sits on the open token-conformance worklist, and the parked feature/noctalia-parity session has controlcenter_pages.go dirty in its worktree. This slice must not re-edit that page's geometry concurrently - sequence the cc page after parity lands or confine this slice to new files.
acceptance_criteria:
- weather.Query/Forecast/Decode extended for current is_day, apparent_temperature, wind speed and direction, humidity, uv_index; daily uv_index_max and precipitation; root elevation, timezone, timezone_abbreviation. Decode stays strict: checked pointer fields, bounded body, table tests for the new fields.
- One icon mapping and one condition-word table shared by the bar, the control-centre page and the tooltip; night variants for clear and partly-cloudy added to the icon subset and selected via is_day.
- The bar weather widget renders a real icon node beside the temperature, opens the weather panel as its Action, and its tooltip carries current facts rather than the literal word "Weather".
- A standalone PanelWeather appended to the PanelID enum after PanelNetwork (the blur coverage walk must see it), composed like the reference: hero card (large glyph, temperature, min/max, condition, configured location name - not coordinates), a details card (feels-like, wind, humidity, UV, sunrise, sunset, elevation, timezone), and the seven-day list with per-day icon, day, range and condition word. Daily only; Hourly is a separate decision with its own wire growth.
- Stale and error states follow formatWeather's three-state rule on every surface; an aged reading looks aged everywhere.
- No new literal geometry: spacing from the margin ladder, control sizes from the density row, shapes from the shape role. The control-centre page's existing literals stay untouched until the parity conversion lands.
- Focused checks per changed unit; gofmt, go vet, and the affected-package gates pass before any commit.
notes:
Scope note 2026-09-15: the parity slices ran on feature/weather-panel and were audited together. The hourly presentation is intentionally capped at seven rows to match the reference; the panel remains two-column per the recorded amendment; the city-only unresolved fallback retains the configured city label rather than fabricating zero coordinates.

Audit verdict 2026-09-16: merge-ready with named corrections applied. Closed findings: sysc-295 (nullable decode and optional-row padding), sysc-296 (control-centre night/stale/error state), sysc-297 (hourly row cap), sysc-298 (detail order), sysc-299 (unresolved-city label), sysc-300 (date-stable fixtures), sysc-301 (Fahrenheit range units), sysc-302 (in-flight city-change cache race). Completed parity slices sysc-1373, sysc-288 and sysc-294 are closed.

Proof: GOMAXPROCS=4 go test -p 2 ./weather/ ./internal/services/ ./internal/render/ ./internal/config/ ./internal/theme/ ./internal/shell/ ./internal/plugin/ ./tests/... -count=1; GOMAXPROCS=4 go build -p 2 ./...; GOMAXPROCS=4 go vet -p 2 ./...; gofmt scan; git diff --check; legacy-visual and backdrop scans; night/detail font-ink tests; go.mod/go.sum diff clean.

The owner-gated live Niri check remains outstanding; do not deploy or restart the service from this audit.

title: plugin/v1 JSON encoder has no write mutex; concurrent Snapshot calls crash the plugin
description:
Framing encoder (plugin/v1/framing.go:71-106) has no write serialization. Any plugin whose publish() runs from more than one goroutine (poll tick + action goroutine is the common pattern — mini-docker does exactly this) can issue concurrent Snapshot calls while the main recv loop also writes, producing concurrent map/encoder writes and a crash that kills the pill.

Found during the mini-docker audit (docs/plans/2026-09-22-mini-docker-{backend}-audit.md in sysc-plugins). The plugin currently must self-serialize around the whole client; that is an easy trap every plugin author will hit.
acceptance_criteria: Either the client serializes frame writes internally, or the plugin-v1 docs state the threading contract loudly; a regression test at the library level proves concurrent Snapshot is safe (or documented-unsafe with the contract spelled out).

title: Investigate duplicate Wayland object ID failure on laptop
description: During the Appearance laptop check, the installed sysc-shell at base commit cbaf1ef and the scratch build both logged `dispatch: panic handling opcode=0 senderID=19: client: duplicate Wayland object ID 0xff000000` and exited. The installed service restarted automatically. The failure is not explained by the Appearance edits and should be investigated separately at the Wayland event/proxy lifecycle boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Identify the event and object lifecycle that produces the duplicate server ID; add the smallest regression check and verify the fix on the laptop without replacing the installed binary by hand.
notes: Root cause (2026-10-01): sysc-wayland v0.3.0 client.Context.RegisterWithID panics on any entry at a server ID, but DataOffer.Destroy only marks the proxy a zombie and leaves it mapped. The server sends no delete_id for its own objects and reuses the ID after handling the destroy. The shell's selection handler (internal/platform/wayland/selection.go) destroys the previous wl_data_offer on each selection change, so the next data_offer at 0xff000000 (sent on keyboard focus, i.e. a click that focuses a panel) panics and the shell exits. It began with b4d2da0 (2026-09-29), which made the data device actually bind; the desktop runs 8225083 (2026-09-28) and has never crashed this way. Laptop journal: 15 exits since 2026-09-29 10:45. Deterministic repro on the laptop scratch instance: copy, open Settings, close, three times; main crashed in round 3 twice; with the fix it survived 10 rounds. Fix: sysc-wayland add1d2e on branch fix/server-id-reuse (RegisterWithID replaces a zombie at a server ID; live duplicates still panic), with a regression test through the generated wl_data_device dispatch. Remaining: push and tag sysc-wayland v0.3.1, bump the pin in sysc-shell, deploy with scripts/deploy.

title: Screensaver idle vs blank/suspend/lock precedence qualification
description: Qualify sysc-walls against blanking, suspend/resume, and secure lock after sysc-910 and sysc-911. Owner-approved interaction (2026-10-04): sysc-lock must report the ext-session-lock locked handshake before shell changes sysc-walls. After acquisition, snapshot whether the service is active/running, persist the prior state in a mode-0600 session marker under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/sysc-shell/ (directory mode 0700), stop with systemctl --user stop, and stop/reap shell-owned Preview. Never change unit enablement. A refused or failed lock leaves walls runtime state untouched. After authenticated unlock, start only if it was running before lock; clear the marker only after successful restore. Preserve the marker and original state across shell restart/re-acquisition. Walls coordination failures never cancel/delay the secure lock; unknown state is left alone and retryable failure is surfaced after unlock. Suspend/resume keeps the lock and leaves walls stopped until unlock. Automatic idle lock obeys shell idle inhibitors (Caffeine, media exemption, org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver); manual Lock bypasses inhibitors. Explain this in lock/idle UI, keep the walls timer independent, keep Settings/Preview unavailable while locked, and refresh after unlock. Qualify initially active/inactive unit, query/stop/start failure, Preview cleanup, suspend/resume, and shell restart. No walls CGO or third idle notifier.

title: sysc-walls preview lifecycle must stay owned and prefix-matched
description: At sysc-walls revision 2676c546, daemon -test calls Daemon.Shutdown, which invokes StopScreensaver. When the preview process has no tracked display, StopScreensaver sweeps all Kitty windows matching sysc-walls-screensaver. A failed preview can therefore stop a display owned by the normal service. Add a preview lifecycle that serializes startup/stop, skips global orphan sweeps, and stops/reaps only display process groups it started. Test spawn failure, early exit, immediate stop, and shutdown with an unrelated matching instance. Reap exited groups before signaling them. Resolve the companion display from the daemon executable prefix before PATH for preview and idle service, so a different /usr/bin version cannot be selected when the unit runs /usr/local/bin. Required before shell exposes Preview.

title: G1+G10: preview column reflows the list and is empty for most types
description:
Audit finding, code confirmed 2026-10-04.

tree.go:194 decides the pane from content: side := m.PreviewImage != "" || m.PreviewText != "". With no preview the list is a plain child at listW 0; with one it gets listW 488 (800 - 2*12 pad - 8 gap - 280). Selecting a file therefore reflows the list by 288px and deselecting reflows it back. UI/UX Pro content-jumping class, High.

Second half: ops.go:277 PeekPreview returns a zero Preview for directories, and ops.go:283 returns zero for anything outside the text allow-list. A folder selection collapses the pane to nothing, so a single click on a folder both reflows the list and shows no information.

Fix: always paint the 280px column at 800px. Empty copy: Select a file. Directory: first N child names. Other files: icon + size + mtime. No full-file dump.

Test: one named test in internal/files, extend the TestTreePreviewSitsBesideList assertion that the list width does not change with or without a preview.

description:
New finding from the 2026-10-04 audit. Not in the original gap list.

The listing is async off the lock, but the preview is not. files.go:214-220 calls files.PeekPreview synchronously inside filesTree. filesTree is called from panelTree (panelhost.go:3384), which rebuildPanel calls (panelhost.go:3238), which runs inside PanelHost.handle, which takes r.mu.Lock for the whole event (panelhost.go:1916-1919). So one click on a file performs 2x EvalSymlinks via Contain plus os.Stat (ops.go:268-282), and for a text file an os.Open plus a 4KiB read, all while holding the one lock every panel, tray, toast and drawer render needs.

The jail root is the caller absolute path, and the live consumer is Phone Connect over an sshfs mount, so those are network round trips. A single click can stall the whole shell chrome.

Fix: cache the preview in filesSession keyed by path, filled by a goroutine using the same gen guard as startFilesLoadLocked (files.go:173-196), and have filesTree read only the cache. Do not move the read into Convert.

Test: one named test in internal/shell mirroring TestFilesOpenModeLoadsOffLock (files_test.go:442), asserting the click returns before the preview read completes.
